### 5. Execution procedure

The following procedure is operational but remains inside the Phase Execution Playbook domain. It does not define function names, CLI commands, final repository paths, model code, final statistical tests, or thesis figure/table placement. [FRAME: domain non-interference]

| Step | Step objective | Inputs consumed | Action and records/artifacts produced or affected | Validation / checkpoint | Failure or downgrade behavior | Source anchors |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm Phase 0 readiness before touching real public data. | Accepted Phase 0 schemas, config templates, validators, mock records, run/seed/config-hash conventions, manifest conventions, diagnostic-only and negative-result fixtures, Layer 0/Layer 10 placeholders. | Consume Phase 0 foundation without mutation; create Phase 1 execution-start status. | Required Phase 0 foundations are present, versioned, and compatible with Phase 1 source-record production. | If hard foundations are absent, block clean Phase 1 promotion; if mock-only work proceeds, mark it diagnostic-only. | [PRIOR: Phase 0 handoff] [EXEC: Phase 1 previous phase dependency] |
| 2 | Declare the dataset-status registry and inclusion boundary. | Public EEG source list, dataset access notes, dataset-status vocabulary, claim-safety tags. | Classify candidate datasets as included, excluded, optional, stretch, or future; preserve source/version/access/citation/license notes and inclusion/exclusion reasons; prepare `DatasetRecord` lineage. | Every candidate dataset has a documented status and reason; no excluded or failed dataset is hidden. | Missing provenance or ambiguous inclusion blocks confirmatory use for that dataset and may produce `NegativeResultNote` / diagnostic status. | [ARCH: Layer 1 dataset selection] [REG: DatasetRecord] [EVAL: negative-result visibility] |
| 3 | Load public EEG sources reproducibly without silent preprocessing. | Public EEG files/APIs/loaders/documented mirrors, dataset-status registry, source access configuration. | Load raw or semi-raw source references; preserve original IDs, source metadata, and access limitations for `DatasetRecord` and manifest linkage. | Source identity, access/version, and reproducibility notes validate or produce explicit warning status. | Failed load, stale mirror, or undocumented source access excludes or downgrades affected dataset records. | [ARCH: Layer 1 dataset loader] [EXEC: source/provenance gate] |
| 4 | Normalize metadata while preserving original fields. | Loaded source metadata, Phase 0 schemas, metadata normalization configuration. | Normalize dataset/subject/session/run/trial/channel/sampling/event/timing fields; preserve original labels, IDs, missingness, and source-specific fields. | Metadata-completeness, hierarchy, ID uniqueness, and required-field checks pass or produce visible warnings. | Missing required metadata narrows claims, blocks affected comparisons, or downgrades records to diagnostic-only. | [ARCH: Layer 1 metadata normalizer] [EXEC: metadata-completeness gate] |
| 5 | Freeze label mapping and task/exclusion policy. | Original labels/events, label configuration, claim-safety labels, proxy-intent notes. | Produce `LabelMapRecord` with original-to-normalized labels, task family, rest/no-action policy, protocol inclusion/exclusion status, exclusion reason, label-map version, and proxy-intent limitation. | Label-map validation confirms explicit mapping, class-order compatibility, and exclusion accounting. | Ambiguous or unmapped labels block affected tasks unless excluded, versioned for repair, or marked diagnostic-only. | [REG: LabelMapRecord] [EXEC: label-map gate] |
| 6 | Register preprocessing before downstream model use. | Preprocessing configuration, split/legal-fit constraints, metadata/channel information. | Produce `PreprocessingRecord` describing filtering, resampling, channel selection, referencing, epoch/window preparation, normalization, artifact policy, fit scope, preprocessing version, and config hash. | Train-only or permitted fitting scope is documented; config hash and preprocessing version validate. | Test/held-out fit leakage invalidates affected outputs; repairs require new preprocessing version and rerun. | [REG: PreprocessingRecord] [EXEC: preprocessing fit-scope gate] |
| 7 | Generate split and low-calibration protocol records. | Split/protocol configuration, label-budget definitions, seed policy, normalized metadata/labels. | Produce `SplitRecord` entries and split manifests for train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation roles, split level, stratification rule, seed, `label_budget_id`, calibration budget, split version, and leakage-check status. | Split-disjointness, membership completeness, low-calibration budget validity, and seed/config lineage validate. | Split leakage, missing memberships, or budget inconsistency blocks or downgrades downstream comparisons. | [ARCH: split/low-calibration/leakage protocol] [REG: SplitRecord] |
| 8 | Materialize traceable trial/window units. | Normalized metadata, labels, preprocessing record, split record, window configuration. | Produce `WindowRecord` entries with dataset/subject/session/run/trial/window identity, `parent_trial_id`, timing, segment pointer, overlap group, labels, split membership, preprocessing ID, label-budget ID, artifact/channel fields where available, config hash, and schema version. | Window lineage, parent-trial grouping, overlap handling, segment pointer, split membership, and label/preprocessing IDs validate. | Missing parent-trial or overlap lineage blocks fair matched claims; standalone `TrialRecord` remains `requires_confirmation` under `MC-001`. | [REG: WindowRecord / MC-001] [ARCH: trial/window generation] |
| 9 | Produce artifact/channel-quality evidence where source-supported. | Source artifact notes, channel metadata, quality annotations, generated windows. | Produce `ArtifactFlagRecord` for missing/bad channels, suspected artifacts, short trials, missing labels, sampling-rate mismatches, overlap risk, severity, action, source, and notes where available. | Artifact-flag schema and linkage validate; missing coverage is measured and surfaced. | Absence of artifact flags becomes a limitation/warning, not proof of clean data; quality claims become diagnostic-only where flags are required. | [REG: ArtifactFlagRecord] [EXEC: artifact/channel flag gate] |
| 10 | Run validation, leakage, reproducibility, matched-key, and field-visibility audits. | All Phase 1 records/configs, Phase 0 validators, readiness/check templates. | Produce `ValidationReport` and supporting leakage, metadata-completeness, exclusion, low-calibration, reproducibility, decision-time/evaluation-only separation, and matched-key status reports. | Schema, provenance, metadata, labels, preprocessing fit scope, split disjointness, duplicate/window leakage, exclusion accounting, evaluation-only label separation, repeated-generation, path/hash, matched-key, and claim-tag gates pass or warn. | Blocking failures prevent clean handoff; non-blocking failures create diagnostic-only flags, narrowed scope, exclusions, or negative-result notes; label-leaking decision-time fields invalidate or downgrade affected downstream contexts. | [REG: ValidationReport] [EXEC: Phase 1 validation gates] [EVAL: diagnostic-only rules / leakage constraints] |
| 11 | Generate source-linked dataset and protocol cards. | Validated records, validation reports, limitation tags, inclusion/exclusion status. | Produce `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard` with provenance, task/protocol description, split/low-calibration/window/preprocessing notes, limitations, allowed/forbidden claims, risks, warnings, and compatibility status. | Cards are source-consistent, limitation-complete, and dashboard-readable without rewriting source evidence. | Missing or misleading limitations block claim-facing use and require Layer 0 review; cards may not overstate model or clinical evidence. | [REG: DatasetCard / ProtocolCard] [REG: MC-012] |
| 12 | Build manifest and ablation-readiness artifact. | Saved records, cards, reports, configs, hashes, validation statuses, matched keys, limitation tags. | Produce `Layer1Manifest` and `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` with source/record IDs, paths, checksums, schema versions, config hashes, seeds, protocol version, validation status, matched-key completeness, missing-key warnings, diagnostic reasons, limitation tags, and dashboard/export readiness. | Manifest/path/hash gate and readiness-artifact supported-field validation pass; unsupported readiness fields remain `requires_confirmation`. | Missing manifest blocks Phase 2 thesis-ready handoff; missing readiness artifact blocks A0–A13 evaluation readiness. | [REG: Layer1Manifest] [REG: layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json] [EXEC: output contract] |
| 13 | Emit diagnostic-only and negative-result signals where required. | Validation outcomes, exclusion lists, failed loads, missingness reports, readiness gaps, limitation tags. | Trigger or produce `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` and `NegativeResultNote` where grounded by validation failures, exclusions, leakage, insufficient metadata, missing matched keys, failed reproduction, or one-dataset fallback. | Every failure/partial state remains linked to affected records, datasets, splits, windows, and claim limitations. | Hidden negative outcomes invalidate claim-facing use; later positive results cannot erase Phase 1 diagnostic limitations. | [EVAL: diagnostic-only downgrade rules] [EVAL: negative-result interpretation] |
| 14 | Perform downstream compatibility checks without producing downstream evidence. | Validated Layer 1 handoff package, Phase 2/Layer 10 read expectations. | Verify that Phase 2 can read source records and that Layer 10 can read cards/manifests/reports; record compatibility status only. | Read compatibility passes for required `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, labels, preprocessing IDs, source IDs, cards, and manifest links. | Compatibility failures require schema/export repair and rerun validation; no decoder performance or dashboard-derived primary evidence is produced in Phase 1. | [ARCH: Layer 1 exit conditions] [REG: Layer1ToLayer2DecoderSourceInterface / Layer1ToLayer10DashboardSourceInterface] |
| 15 | Freeze validated source records and package the Phase 2+ handoff. | Validated records/cards/reports/manifest/readiness artifact and open-issue ledger. | Promote validated Layer 1 records to clean-source status; package handoff contents and unresolved issues; preserve versioning and lineage. | Handoff includes required records, validation status, matched keys, diagnostic flags, limitation tags, source IDs, hashes, and downstream-consumer notes. | Repairs after promotion require new protocol/record versions with lineage; downstream mutation invalidates or downgrades affected evidence. | [REG: Clean Source-Record Immutability] [FRAME: immutable/versioned record discipline] |

**Procedure integrity rule:** Phase 1 protocol choices must be made before downstream model, policy, simulation, stress, embodiment, dashboard, or thesis-preference signals can influence them. Scientifically justified repairs are allowed only through validation-triggered reruns, new protocol versions, versioned/derived outputs, diagnostic flags, or formal correction requests. [ARCH: Layer 1 feedforward and loopback behavior] [FRAME: non-destructive record discipline]

**Immutability rule:** Clean validated Layer 1 source records are immutable. A correction, new dataset inclusion, changed preprocessing, changed label map, changed split, changed windowing, or repaired metadata produces a new version and a new `Layer1Manifest` lineage; it never silently overwrites validated source records. [REG: Clean Source-Record Immutability] [FRAME: immutable/versioned record discipline]

### 7A. Artifact immutability and versioning rules

Validated Phase 1 source records are evidence anchors, not mutable scratch artifacts. Once a `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `ValidationReport`, `DatasetCard`, `ProtocolCard`, `Layer1Manifest`, or supported readiness artifact is promoted for downstream use, later phases must consume it read-only unless the registry or a formal correction path authorizes a versioned replacement. [REG: Clean Source-Record Immutability] [FRAME: immutable/versioned record discipline]

| Situation | Required handling | Claim/evaluation effect |
|---|---|---|
| Validated clean source record | Treat as immutable upstream evidence; downstream phases consume by ID, hash, validation status, and limitation tags. | Claim-ready only within recorded public-data/proxy/low-calibration boundaries. |
| Validation failure before promotion | Repair by rerunning the responsible Phase 1 config/adapter and writing a new validation result; do not promote failed records. | Blocked or diagnostic-only until resolved. |
| Repair after protocol freeze or downstream consumption | Create a new protocol version and new record versions with lineage to superseded records; preserve old records for audit. | Comparisons mixing old/new protocols are diagnostic-only unless matched-version keys validate. |
| Dashboard, thesis, or downstream model detects missingness | Create a visible warning, diagnostic flag, derived overlay, or correction request; do not silently rewrite source records. | Layer 10/Layer 0 must display the limitation or invalidity. |
| Earlier Phase 0 foundation found absent/inconsistent during real execution | Do not edit Phase 0 inside Phase 1; issue a Back-Propagation Correction Request. | Current Phase 1 becomes blocked, partial, or diagnostic-only depending on severity. |

---

### 8. Validation gates and exit conditions

| Gate | Required check | Pass condition | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schema gate | Phase 1 records/artifacts conform to Phase 0 schemas or explicitly marked candidate/confirmation status | validators pass on real Layer 1 outputs | block promotion to clean validated source record |
| Source/provenance gate | public source, version/access/license/citation/source notes and dataset status recorded | dataset is reproducible enough for source/protocol use | exclude, optional/future status, or diagnostic-only |
| Metadata completeness gate | subject/session/run/trial/channel/sampling/timing metadata present or missingness documented | no unresolved blocking metadata gap | diagnostic-only or dataset/task exclusion |
| Label-map gate | all included labels map to normalized labels or documented exclusions | `LabelMapRecord` validates and proxy-intent note is present | exclude/repair affected label or block downstream use |
| Preprocessing fit-scope gate | preprocessing version, config hash, and legal train-only fit scope where required | no held-out/test fit leakage | invalid until rerun with new preprocessing version |
| Window-generation gate | timing, duration, stride, overlap, source/trial, label, preprocessing, and split lineage validate | usable windows pass lineage checks | block affected windows or mark diagnostic-only |
| Split-disjointness gate | train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation memberships are legal and non-overlapping as required | leakage status passes | block confirmatory evaluation until new split version validates |
| Subject/session/run/trial/window leakage gate | protocol level prevents leakage across required grouping levels and overlap groups | leakage audit passes | diagnostic-only or invalid for affected comparisons |
| Low-calibration budget gate | label budgets, calibration memberships, adaptation memberships, and split roles are consistent | budget table and `SplitRecord` validate | A0–A4 and adaptive contexts blocked/diagnostic-only |
| Decision-time/evaluation-only field separation gate | held-out/test labels, correctness helpers, future outcomes, and evaluation-only diagnostics are protected from downstream decision-time feature fields | validation report confirms legal visibility by split role and consumer context | affected downstream run invalid, oracle-only, or diagnostic-only until field visibility is repaired and rerun |
| Exclusion accounting gate | all dropped/excluded datasets, subjects, sessions, runs, trials, windows, labels, channels have reasons | exclusion report complete | claim-facing use blocked until accounted |
| Artifact/channel flag gate | artifact flags validate where present; missing flags are warned | flags present or warning state emitted | quality/artifact claims downgraded |
| Matched-key completeness gate | required A0–A13 source keys present or missing-key reasons logged | readiness artifact reports ready or explicit diagnostic gaps | matched comparisons diagnostic-only/blocked |
| Manifest/path/hash gate | `Layer1Manifest` links records, paths, hashes, seeds, configs, validation status, readiness artifact, limitations | manifest validates | reproducibility/export incomplete; downstream claims blocked |
| Card limitation gate | cards reflect records, validation state, known limitations, allowed/forbidden claims | cards pass source-consistency review | cards not thesis/dashboard export-ready |
| Claim-safety tag gate | public-data/proxy/non-clinical/diagnostic/invalid tags propagate | Layer 0-compatible tags present | claim-facing outputs blocked/downgraded |
| Layer 10 read-only preview gate | Layer 10 can inspect saved cards/manifests/reports without recomputing evidence | preview/source-lineage check passes | dashboard/export handoff diagnostic-only |
| Phase 2 compatibility gate | Phase 2 can read validated `WindowRecord` and `SplitRecord` package | smoke compatibility passes without producing Phase 2 evidence | Phase 2 blocked until format/manifest repair through Phase 1 versioning |

**Exit condition**

Phase 1 is complete only when at least one selected public EEG dataset has validated `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord` or missing-flag warnings, `ValidationReport`, `DatasetCard`, `ProtocolCard`, `Layer1Manifest`, `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json`, low-calibration budget support, leakage/metadata/matched-key reporting, decision-time/evaluation-only field-separation status, limitation tags, and a clean downstream handoff to Phase 2. [EXEC: Phase 1 exit condition]

If multi-dataset coverage is infeasible, a one-primary-dataset fallback may support only a narrowed initial C0 path if the dataset fully validates and the scope is explicit. It must not be described as broad multi-dataset robustness. [EXEC: Phase 1 fallback]

### 9. Matched-comparison key preservation

Phase 1 is the first phase that materializes the public-data source keys required for fair A0–A13 comparisons. Missing or inconsistent Phase 1 keys cannot be repaired by downstream overwrite; affected rows become diagnostic-only, blocked, or invalid. | Key or key family | Phase 1 source | Required for | Handling |

| `dataset_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `Layer1Manifest` | all comparisons and source grouping | required |
| `subject_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord` where supported | subject-level splits and grouping | required where dataset supports subject identity |
| `session_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord` where supported | cross-session protocols and leakage checks | required where sessions exist |
| `run_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, manifests where applicable | run-level lineage and reproducibility | required where applicable |
| `trial_id` / `parent_trial_id` | `WindowRecord` | trial/window lineage, overlap leakage, replay, stress pairing | required where trial/window structure exists; standalone `TrialRecord` unresolved |
| `window_id` | `WindowRecord` | decoder inputs, calibration, IHARQ, policy context, replay, stress, embodiment, dashboard | required |
| `split_id` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord`, manifests | split-safe evaluation | required |
| `split_role` / `split_membership` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord` | train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation legality | required |
| `label_budget_id` / `calibration_budget` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord`, budget table | low-calibration comparisons and adaptation contexts | required |
| `preprocessing_id` / `preprocessing_version` | `PreprocessingRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `DatasetRecord` | matched preprocessing and leakage control | required |
| `label_map_id` | `LabelMapRecord`, `WindowRecord` | label consistency and proxy-intent limitations | required |
| `artifact_flag_id` / `channel_mask_id` | `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `WindowRecord` where supported | quality, artifact, stress, and subgroup warnings | required where source supports; missingness warning otherwise |
| `config_hash` | configs, records, manifests | reproducibility and hidden-drift detection | required |
| `seed` | `SplitRecord`, manifests where applicable | generated split reproducibility | required for generated splits |
| `schema_version` | all records/artifacts | schema compatibility | required |
| `validation_status` | all records/artifacts | downstream eligibility and Layer 10/Layer 0 treatment | required |
| `claim_boundary_tags` | records, cards, manifests, readiness artifact | limitation inheritance | required |
| decision-time / evaluation-only field visibility status | `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `ValidationReport`, readiness artifact | protects downstream policies, thresholds, calibration, simulation, stress, and embodiment contexts from label/correctness leakage | required for thesis-ready downstream consumers |

**Forward key extension rule:** later phases may add `model_id`, `decoder_id`, `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `IHARQDecisionRecord` IDs, regime/trust IDs, readiness/policy/action IDs, transition/session/reward IDs, stress profile/schedule IDs, embodiment mode/outcome IDs, dashboard/export IDs, and final claim-evidence IDs. They may not mutate Phase 1 source keys. [DERIVED from EXEC+EVAL+REG]

### 11. Dashboard, card, and reproducibility obligations

Layer 10 is not active as a hidden empirical producer in Phase 1. It must later read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, export, card, and package saved Layer 1 artifacts without recomputing or repairing them. [ARCH: Layer 10] [REG: MC-011]

| Layer 10 obligation | Phase 1 handoff requirement | Boundary / failure rule |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard visibility | Mark `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `ValidationReport`, cards, manifest, readiness artifact, leakage reports, metadata reports, and matched-key status as dashboard-readable where valid. | Missing source lineage makes dashboard output diagnostic-only. |
| Cards | Produce source `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard`; Layer 10 may render/export them later but may not rewrite limitations. | Card without source/limitation linkage is not thesis-ready. |
| Metrics/status summaries | Provide validation, readiness, leakage, missingness, artifact-coverage, class-distribution, split, low-calibration, and matched-key status summaries. | Claim-facing numeric metrics require `MetricDictionaryEntry`; otherwise status remains diagnostic/reporting. |
| Matched-comparison reports | Provide source key envelope and completeness status for future `MatchedComparisonReport`. | Unmatched or missing keys must be visible and diagnostic-only/blocked. |
| Static figures/tables readiness | Provide source-linked data/card/report inputs; do not define final figure/table placement. | Final thesis figures/tables deferred to Paper/Thesis Evidence Map. |
| Artifact lineage | Preserve record IDs, source IDs, paths, checksums, schema versions, config hashes, seeds, validation status, and limitation tags. | Missing lineage blocks export/reproducibility claims. |
| Reproducibility manifests | Build `Layer1Manifest`; prepare inputs for later `ReproducibilityManifest` and export package. | `MC-009` concrete path caveat remains visible. |
| Warning visibility | Surface diagnostic-only flags, validation failures, missing metadata, missing artifact flags, leakage failures, decision-time/evaluation-only separation failures, negative-result notes, and limitation tags. | Hidden warnings invalidate dashboard-derived presentation. |
| Export readiness | Ensure all Phase 1 outputs needed by Phase 14/15 can be indexed by manifest and checksums. | Layer 10 cannot patch missing source records or claim tags. |

**Forbidden Layer 10 behavior for Phase 1 artifacts:** no hidden reloading/re-splitting, no preprocessing repair, no leakage repair, no label-map changes, no artifact-clean assertions from missing flags, no threshold/model tuning, no mutation of Layer 1 records, no suppression of diagnostic-only/negative-result warnings, and no conversion of cards/views into primary empirical evidence. [REG: Global dashboard obligations] [EVAL: Layer 10 obligations]

### 12. Claim-safety and limitation boundaries

Layer 0 receives Phase 1 source-lineage and limitation inputs but does not produce the empirical source evidence. [REG: MC-012] [EVAL: Layer 0 boundaries]

| Claim class | Phase 1 allowed wording boundary | Forbidden overclaim |
|---|---|---|
| Public-data protocol readiness | May claim a reproducible public EEG, split-safe, low-calibration-ready protocol substrate if gates pass. | Must not claim clinical rehabilitation validity or real BCI-FES safety. |
| Dataset/protocol cards | May describe dataset origin, task labels, protocol, limitations, and validation state. | Must not imply cards prove model or clinical performance. |
| Split/leakage validation | May state that declared splits/leakage checks passed for validated records. | Must not generalize beyond validated datasets/protocol versions. |
| Low-calibration setup | May state that label-budget/calibration/adaptation memberships are defined. | Must not claim low-calibration model performance before Phases 2–3. |
| Evaluation readiness | May state that source keys and readiness status support later evaluation contexts. | Must not claim A0–A13 results or comparative improvements. |
| Decision-time/evaluation-only separation | May state that the declared protocol protects held-out/test labels and correctness helpers from downstream decision-time feature use if the gate passes. | Must not imply downstream policies, thresholds, or controllers had legitimate access to evaluation-only labels. |
| Dashboard/reproducibility | May state records/cards/manifests are source-linked and export-ready where valid. | Must not treat dashboards/exports as primary empirical evidence. |

**Forbidden Phase 1 claim types**

- real patient safety;
- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- medical-device readiness;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real-time closed-loop performance;
- decoder/calibration/IHARQ/policy/stress/embodiment improvement;
- broad multi-dataset robustness if only a one-dataset fallback validates;
- artifact-clean data if artifact flags are merely absent;
- fair matched comparisons if required keys are missing;
- decision-time readiness, threshold, policy, simulation, stress, or embodiment claims if evaluation-only labels or correctness helpers leaked into decision-time fields. [ARCH: Layer 1 claim rule] [EVAL: invalid claim triggers]

**Layer 0 handoff requirements**

Phase 1 must hand off limitation tags, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result/exclusion notes, card limitations, validation statuses, matched-key statuses, readiness status, source IDs, and unresolved registry issues so Layer 0 can block, weaken, or invalidate unsupported claims. [EXEC: Phase 1 Layer 0 review]

### 13. Failure, missingness, and diagnostic-only handling

| Failure / missingness condition | Minimum status | Phase 1 handling | Downstream consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Missing public source/version/license/access note | `blocked` or `diagnostic_only` | Exclude dataset, mark optional/future, or record limitation | Cannot support confirmatory claims |
| Missing required metadata | `diagnostic_only` or `blocked` | Record in metadata-completeness report and cards | Affected comparisons blocked/diagnostic-only |
| Standalone `TrialRecord` requested | `requires_confirmation` | Do not promote; use `trial_id`/`parent_trial_id` in `WindowRecord` | Later trial-level schemas may need confirmation |
| Label ambiguity/unmapped labels | `blocked` for affected task | Exclude, repair with new label-map version, or diagnostic-only | Affected decoder/evaluation claims blocked |
| Illegal preprocessing fit scope | `invalid` for affected outputs | Create new preprocessing version and rerun | Downstream evidence invalid until repaired |
| Split leakage | `invalid` for confirmatory claims | Fail gate; create new split version if repaired | Downstream comparisons blocked/invalid |
| Missing calibration/adaptation membership | `blocked` or `diagnostic_only` | Mark readiness false for affected contexts | A1–A4/adaptive contexts blocked/diagnostic-only |
| Evaluation-only labels or correctness helpers visible as decision-time fields | `invalid` or `diagnostic_only` | Repair field partition and rerun, or mark affected analysis oracle/diagnostic-only | Downstream threshold/policy/simulation/stress/embodiment claims blocked |
| Untracked exclusions | `blocked` | Add exclusion reasons or downgrade | Thesis evidence not ready |
| Missing artifact flags | `warning` / possible `diagnostic_only` for quality claims | Emit missing-flag limitation | Artifact-clean or quality subgroup claims downgraded |
| Missing matched-comparison keys | `diagnostic_only` or `blocked` | Record in readiness artifact and completeness report | A0–A13 comparisons diagnostic-only/blocked |
| Missing `Layer1Manifest` | `blocked` | No thesis-ready handoff | Phase 2 may not make traceable claims |
| Missing readiness artifact | `blocked` for ablation readiness | Generate artifact or keep Phase 1 incomplete | A0–A13 evaluation readiness absent |
| Stale path/config hash | `blocked` or `diagnostic_only` | Fail manifest/path/hash gate | Layer 10 export and Phase 15 reproducibility incomplete |
| Missing claim-boundary tags | `blocked` for claim use | Add supported limitation tags; do not invent unsupported claims | Layer 0 downgrades/blocks claims |
| Dashboard repairs or recomputes source records | `invalid` | Treat as Layer 10 boundary violation | Dashboard output invalid for thesis evidence |
| Downstream phase mutates clean Layer 1 record | `invalid` | Require new versioned source record or derived record with lineage | Downstream evidence invalid/diagnostic-only |
| Negative validation outcome hidden | `blocked` or `weakened` | Create/trigger `NegativeResultNote` where applicable | Claim cannot omit failure/exclusion |

Diagnostic-only status must remain visible in records, validation reports, readiness artifacts, cards, dashboards, exports, and final claim-evidence links. Later positive model results must not erase Phase 1 diagnostic limitations. [EVAL: diagnostic-only preservation]

### 17. Definition of done

Phase 1 is done when all of the following are true:

- accepted Phase 0 foundation is present and consumed without mutation;
- selected public dataset(s) have source/provenance records and explicit inclusion/exclusion status;
- `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, and applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord` outputs validate or carry explicit diagnostic status;
- `ValidationReport` covers schema, provenance, metadata, labels, preprocessing, splits, leakage, low-calibration budgets, exclusions, artifact flags, matched keys, manifest/path/hash integrity, card limitation checks, and claim-safety tags;
- `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard` are source-linked and limitation-complete;
- `Layer1Manifest` indexes all Phase 1 records, reports, cards, configs, seeds, hashes, paths, validation status, warnings, and limitations;
- `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` reports matched-key completeness, missing-key warnings, diagnostic-only reasons, validation links, source IDs, config hashes, seeds, and protocol version for supported fields;
- no unresolved leakage, illegal preprocessing, label ambiguity, evaluation-only label exposure, untracked exclusion, missing manifest, missing readiness artifact, or missing claim tag remains hidden;
- any failed/partial/one-dataset fallback state is visible as diagnostic, narrowed, weakened, blocked, or negative-result status;
- Phase 2 can consume validated windows/splits without hidden assumptions;
- Layer 10 and Layer 0 handoff data are complete enough for later dashboard/export and claim-safety review;
- all unresolved registry/document-domain issues remain listed rather than silently resolved. [EXEC: Phase 1 definition of done] [FRAME: final audit requirements]

### 0A. Source Extraction Digest

This digest is the operational extraction for `Phase 2 — Baseline decoders`. It is intentionally phase-specific and does not substitute for the architecture, registry, execution plan, or evaluation protocol.

| Source anchor | Phase 2 extraction used in this playbook |
|---|---|
| `[FRAME: required phase structure / source extraction / non-interference]` | Every phase must include identity, capability relevance, inheritance, architecture objective, input/output contracts, execution procedure, lifecycle, validation gates, matched-key preservation, ablation/evaluation obligations, Layer 10 handoff, Layer 0 handoff, failure/diagnostic handling, repository/reproducibility expectations, handoff package, open issues, definition of done, machine-readable handoff, source ledger, domain non-interference, and final self-audit. `[DERIVED]` may synthesize procedure only from official sources and may not invent canonical names. |
| `[ARCH: Implementation Pipeline / Phase 2 Baseline decoders]` | Phase 2 is the measurement-spine gate after Phase 1. It consumes validated `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, Phase 0 model/config/seed foundations, low-calibration budgets, resource constraints, and a declared baseline-family list. It trains/runs classical, Riemannian/tangent-space, compact neural, optional compact SSL/foundation-style, and ordinary longer-window/multi-window/ensemble controls where feasible. |
| `[ARCH: Layer 2 / Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine]` | Layer 2 produces fair, reproducible, inspectable decoder evidence: per-window/per-trial predictions, model provenance, baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject/session summaries, ordinary A4 controls, failure indices, readiness reports, and card source material. It predicts and measures; it does not calibrate, threshold, make IHARQ decisions, estimate RegimeRisk, learn policies, simulate consequences, stress records, validate embodiment, or make readiness/safety/clinical claims. |
| `[ARCH: Layer 0 / claim safety]` | Phase 2 evidence may support only bounded public-data decoder-baseline measurement claims. It must carry `public_eeg_only`, `decoder_baseline_only`, `low_calibration_protocol`, `evaluation_only`, `diagnostic_only` when applicable, and non-clinical/non-deployment limitations. |
| `[ARCH: Layer 10 / dashboard, cards, reproducibility]` | Layer 10 may read, validate, summarize, warn, render, card, export, and package saved Phase 2 records. It must not train models, tune thresholds, recalibrate scores, repair split leakage, rewrite source records, hide failures, or create hidden primary evidence. |
| `[REG: Layer 2 modules]` | Official Phase 2/Layer 2 submodules are `Baseline trainer`, `Prediction logger`, `Low-calibration curve builder`, `Subject difficulty profiler`, `Model-family registry`, `Ensemble comparison builder`, optional/stretch `Compact SSL adapter`, and `Downstream readiness validator`. `Baseline metric evaluator` is an internal functional alias, not an official new submodule. |
| `[REG: Layer 2 input contracts]` | Required inputs are `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord` or split manifest, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, decoder/model config, label-budget configuration where low-calibration evidence is claimed, seed/config conventions, and held-out labels only as evaluation-only inputs. `ArtifactFlagRecord` is optional/required where present. Pretrained encoder checkpoints are optional/stretch only. |
| `[REG: Layer 2 output contracts]` | Official or registry-supported outputs are trained model artifacts, `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, `SubjectProfileRecord`, `EnsembleControlRecord`, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, training/inference/failed-run logs, and `ModelCard`/`BenchmarkCard` source bundles. `EnsembleControlRecord` is a normalized-candidate/evaluation artifact; `FailureCaseIndex` is normalized-candidate/final if schema fixed; card rendering belongs to Layer 10. |
| `[REG: required field envelope]` | `PredictionRecord` requires global lineage such as `record_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `producer_layer`, `validation_status`, `created_timestamp`, `config_hash`; required-if-applicable IDs including dataset/subject/session/run/trial/window/split/model/preprocessing/label-map/seed/ablation/source IDs; and record-specific `decoder_id`, `model_family`, `label_budget_id`, `score_type`, and `class_order`. It forbids future reward, policy action, embodiment outcome, and safety approval fields. |
| `[REG: immutability / derived governance]` | Validated upstream clean records are immutable. `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` become Layer 2 clean source records after validation. Metrics/profiles/control/failure/readiness/card records are derived/reporting/diagnostic artifacts that must preserve source IDs, schema versions, derivation configs, run IDs, seeds, config hashes, validation status, and inherited limitation tags. |
| `[REG: MC-001/MC-007/MC-008/MC-009/MC-010/MC-011/MC-012]` | Trial-level representation, dashboard metric/source-output boundaries, metric dictionary/schema path, repository paths/storage homes, lifecycle/status vocabulary, Layer 10 evidence boundary, and Layer 0 evidence boundary remain open or boundary-sensitive issues. Phase 2 must carry them forward rather than silently resolving them. |
| `[EXEC: Phase 2 identity and scope]` | Official identity is `Phase 2 — Baseline decoders`, status `measurement_spine_gate`, primary owner `Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine`, with Phase 0/1 as hard dependencies and Phase 3 as immediate downstream consumer. |
| `[EXEC: Phase 2 validation gate]` | Per-window or per-trial `PredictionRecord` outputs must exist for every selected dataset, subject, split, model family, seed, and label budget intended for downstream comparison. Missing logits/probabilities must be explicit. A0/A4 evidence must be matched on Layer 1 comparison keys or downgraded to diagnostic-only. |
| `[EVAL: A0 identity]` | A0 is the raw decoder / accept-all raw decoder reference in the narrow offline-evaluation sense. It measures raw decoder behavior before calibration, thresholding, selective prediction, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, policy learning, simulation, stress, or embodiment effects are credited. |
| `[EVAL: A4 identity]` | A4 covers longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls. A4 fairness requires declared aggregation/member rules, compatible score/class-order/label-map/split/budget lineage, failed/skipped member visibility, and delay/window burden disclosure. A4 must not be renamed IHARQ, thresholding, selective prediction, or policy evidence. |
| `[EVAL: A1–A3 dependency]` | Phase 2 does not produce A1 calibration, A2 registered threshold, or A3 uncertainty/selective-prediction outputs. It prepares raw scores/probabilities/logits, `score_type`, `class_order`, model IDs, split IDs, and prediction IDs required for Phase 3. |
| `[EVAL: A5–A13 dependency]` | A5–A13 consume Phase 2 lineage only through later phase-owned records. Phase 2 does not produce IHARQ decisions, learned evidence-quality estimates, RegimeRisk records, deferral/policy actions, transition records, stress profiles, embodiment outcomes, dashboard conclusions, or final thesis claims. |
| `[EVAL: diagnostic-only / negative results]` | Weak raw performance, strong raw performance, failed/skipped baselines, missing score fields, unmatched keys, metric-dictionary gaps, or leakage must remain visible through failure logs, `FailureCaseIndex`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, `NegativeResultNote` where required, dashboard warnings, and Layer 0 limitations. |
| `[PRIOR: Phase 0 accepted handoff]` | Phase 2 inherits schemas, config families, validators, mock fixtures, run identifiers, config hashes, seed conventions, manifest conventions, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, dashboard/export-readiness placeholders, and immutable/versioned record discipline. |
| `[PRIOR: Phase 1 accepted handoff]` | Phase 2 consumes validated public-data/protocol package: `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `ValidationReport`, `Layer1Manifest`, `manifests/layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json`, dataset/protocol cards, low-calibration budget table, matched-key completeness report, split-leakage report, missingness/exclusion metadata, and limitation tags. |
| `[ARCH: C0–C4 capability tiers]` | Phase 2 is a direct contributor to C0, the public-data reliability spine. C0 requires Phases 0–3, so Phase 2 alone cannot complete C0. C1–C4 may consume Phase 2 lineage but are not made valid by Phase 2 alone. |

**Items not found or requiring confirmation:** final concrete repository paths remain unresolved where `MC-009` applies; exact metric-dictionary schema/path remains unresolved where `MC-008` applies; final v1.0 run matrix/statistical tests are deferred to the final evaluation protocol; concrete implementation classes/CLI/test-suite names are deferred to the future Implementation Build Book; final thesis wording, figure numbering, and table placement are deferred to final thesis integration.

### 3. Architecture-grounded phase objective

Phase 2 creates the clean decoder-measurement spine for the rest of the IHARQ BenchGuard Stretch C system. Architecturally, it converts Phase 1 standardized public EEG records into reproducible decoder predictions, model provenance, baseline metric evidence, low-calibration summaries, subject/session heterogeneity descriptors, ordinary A4 controls, and downstream compatibility reports.

| Architectural concern | Phase 2 objective | Source anchors |
|---|---|---|
| Feed-forward path from Layer 1 to Layer 2 | Consume immutable public-data/split/window/preprocessing/label-map records; never mutate them. | `[ARCH: Phase 2 preconditions]` `[REG: L1→L2 interface]` |
| Feed-forward path from Layer 2 to Layer 3 | Provide raw probabilities/logits/decision scores or explicit missing-score flags, plus `score_type`, `class_order`, model ID, split ID, and prediction IDs. | `[EXEC: Phase 3 consumes raw probabilities/scores/logits]` |
| Feed-forward path to Layers 4–6 | Provide prediction/model/baseline lineage only; downstream records own IHARQ, RegimeRisk, and policy interpretations. | `[REG: downstream consumer clarification]` |
| Feed-forward path to Layers 7–9 | Provide optional provenance/readiness context only after simulation/stress/embodiment phases own their records. | `[ARCH: Layer 7–9 boundaries]` |
| Layer 10 interface | Prepare dashboard-readable source records, warnings, metric lineage, card source bundles, and reproducibility manifest inputs. | `[REG: dashboard-readable Layer 2 inputs]` |
| Layer 0 interface | Attach limitation labels, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result references, and forbidden-claim boundaries. | `[ARCH: Layer 0]` |
| Loopback restrictions | No test-driven protocol/model/budget/threshold tuning; no dashboard repair; no claim-safety rewriting of evidence; no downstream policy/simulation/stress feedback into clean Layer 2 source records. | `[REG: immutability rules]` `[EVAL: split/leakage constraints]` |

### 5. Execution procedure

Each step below is [DERIVED from `[ARCH: Phase 2 tasks]`, `[REG: Layer 2 module/input/output contracts]`, `[EXEC: Phase 2 gates]`, `[EVAL: A0/A4 obligations]`, and `[PRIOR: Phase 0/1 handoff]`]. It is procedural and does not define final code, CLI commands, class names, exact repository paths, or statistical run matrix.

#### Step 1 — Freeze and verify the Phase 2 input package

- **Step objective:** Establish a non-mutable, split-safe input package for decoder training/evaluation.
- **Inputs consumed:** Phase 0 schemas/config/seed/manifest conventions; Phase 1 `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `ValidationReport`, `Layer1Manifest`, `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json`, matched-key and leakage reports.
- **Action performed:** Verify all required inputs exist, have compatible schema versions, pass split/leakage checks, carry limitation tags, and are not marked invalid except where diagnostic-only use is explicit.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** Phase 2 input-freeze manifest or equivalent handoff manifest entry; no new canonical record name is introduced.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Input package passes schema, hash, split, label-map, budget, and limitation-tag checks.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Missing/invalid required input blocks affected dataset/model branch; diagnostic-only continuation allowed only with explicit flags and no confirmatory claim.
- **Source anchors:** `[PRIOR: Phase 1 handoff]` `[REG: Layer 2 input contracts]` `[EXEC: Phase 2 preconditions]`.

#### Step 2 — Declare baseline-family, resource, seed, and budget plan

- **Step objective:** Prevent cherry-picked or hidden model-family selection.
- **Inputs consumed:** Decoder/model configs, selected baseline-family list, seed registry, low-calibration budget table, training-resource constraints.
- **Action performed:** Declare core families and optional/stretch branches before final interpretation: classical baselines, Riemannian/tangent-space where data permits, compact neural where feasible, optional compact SSL/foundation-style where permitted, and A4 ordinary controls where feasible.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** Model-family plan captured in `ModelRegistryRecord` preparation fields and/or run manifest; optional/stretch skipped criteria documented.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Plan separates required, target, optional/stretch, unsupported, and skipped statuses; no final-test tuning or model selection is allowed.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Undeclared post-hoc model inclusion/exclusion downgrades affected comparison or blocks claim-ready use.
- **Source anchors:** `[ARCH: Phase 2 model families]` `[REG: Baseline trainer / Compact SSL adapter]` `[EVAL: A0 no-collapse rule]`.

#### Step 3 — Train/run declared decoder baselines under fixed protocols

- **Step objective:** Produce reproducible raw decoder outputs under fixed public-data/split constraints.
- **Inputs consumed:** Layer 1 records, decoder configs, budget configs, seed policy, training-resource constraints.
- **Action performed:** Train or run each declared baseline family on legal training partitions only; preserve train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation separation; log unsupported, failed, or skipped branches.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** Trained model artifacts, training logs, inference logs, failed/skipped-run logs, model-registry inputs.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Model status, config hash, seed, split role, artifact path/status, score availability, and failure/skipped reason are captured.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Failed or skipped baselines remain visible; optional/stretch failures do not invalidate core but cannot be claimed.
- **Source anchors:** `[ARCH: Phase 2 core implementation tasks]` `[REG: Baseline trainer]` `[EVAL: negative-result discipline]`.

#### Step 4 — Register model and run provenance

- **Step objective:** Prevent orphan predictions and irreproducible model outputs.
- **Inputs consumed:** Model artifacts/configs, decoder configs, training/inference logs, failed-run logs, label-map version, score type, class order, seed/config/environment hash.
- **Action performed:** Create `ModelRegistryRecord` entries for successful, failed, skipped, and unsupported branches as applicable.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `ModelRegistryRecord`; model-card source inputs.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Every model/prediction has model ID, decoder ID, family/name, implementation/artifact/prediction paths where available, training split, label budget, checkpoint/status, score schema, class order, seed, config hash, code/tool version where available, and failed/skipped reason if relevant.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Predictions without valid `ModelRegistryRecord` linkage are orphaned and not thesis-ready.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: ModelRegistryRecord]` `[EXEC: output consumers]`.

#### Step 5 — Emit prediction-level records

- **Step objective:** Create clean Layer 2 prediction source evidence for A0 and downstream phases.
- **Inputs consumed:** Model artifacts, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, optional `ArtifactFlagRecord`, held-out labels only as evaluation-only fields.
- **Action performed:** Emit per-window or per-trial `PredictionRecord` entries with predicted class, score/probability/logit or explicit fallback/missing status, `score_type`, `class_order`, model/decoder IDs, dataset/subject/session/run/trial/window/split IDs, label budget, seed, config hash, time/order where needed, and evaluation-only `label_true` where legal.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `PredictionRecord`; inference logs.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Required global and record-specific field envelope passes; labels/correctness are not exposed as decision-time features; no future reward/policy/embodiment/safety fields appear.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Missing score fields do not invalidate raw A0 categorically, but they block or downgrade calibration/A1–A3 eligibility and any score-dependent comparisons.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: PredictionRecord]` `[EXEC: Phase 2 validation gate]` `[EVAL: A1–A3 dependency]`.

#### Step 6 — Compute raw baseline metrics and A0 evidence

- **Step objective:** Produce raw decoder performance evidence without calibration, thresholding, rejection, or readiness logic.
- **Inputs consumed:** `PredictionRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, held-out labels under split policy, `MetricDictionaryEntry` where available, comparison keys.
- **Action performed:** Compute `BaselineMetricRecord` entries for accuracy, balanced accuracy, F1 or AUC where applicable, confusion-matrix lineage, aggregation level, label budget, split role, seed summaries, confidence intervals where available, and diagnostic flags.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `BaselineMetricRecord`; A0 raw-decoder tables; possible `MatchedComparisonReport` inputs; possible `NegativeResultNote`/`DiagnosticOnlyFlag` where required.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Metric dictionary linkage, denominator/class-order/split-role/aggregation consistency, and matched keys are present for thesis-facing use.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Missing metric dictionary, missing matched keys, or leakage makes affected metric claims diagnostic-only or invalid.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: BaselineMetricRecord]` `[EVAL: A0 metrics]` `[REG: MetricDictionaryEntry]`.

#### Step 7 — Build low-calibration and low-label budget evidence

- **Step objective:** Characterize decoder behavior under declared label-budget/low-calibration protocols.
- **Inputs consumed:** `PredictionRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, budget configs, split roles, seed/config lineage.
- **Action performed:** Build `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` values across legal budgets, with budget-failure notes and sparse/invalid-budget warnings.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`; low-calibration curve source data; dashboard-readable curve inputs.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Budget IDs, split legality, seed summaries, matched keys, and metric dictionary entries exist where thesis-facing.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Sparse/invalid budget evidence is preserved as diagnostic-only and cannot support low-calibration claims.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: LowCalibrationCurveRecord]` `[ARCH: low-calibration curves]`.

#### Step 8 — Build subject/session difficulty and heterogeneity summaries

- **Step objective:** Preserve subject/session variability without medical or physiological overinterpretation.
- **Inputs consumed:** `PredictionRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, subject/session metadata.
- **Action performed:** Create `SubjectProfileRecord` entries with subject/session IDs, baseline performance, difficulty metrics, low-label summaries, optional instability notes, and source provenance.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `SubjectProfileRecord`.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Source prediction and baseline metric lineage is complete; no diagnostic/medical labels or patient-safety wording are introduced.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Missing lineage or overinterpreted profile fields make profiles diagnostic-only or invalid.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: SubjectProfileRecord]` `[ARCH: thesis role / subject difficulty profiles]`.

#### Step 9 — Build A4 ordinary longer-window, multi-window, and ensemble controls where feasible

- **Step objective:** Provide ordinary-control comparators so later IHARQ/policy claims are not confused with simple aggregation benefits.
- **Inputs consumed:** Matched `PredictionRecord` families, `ModelRegistryRecord`, ensemble/control config, label-map/class-order/score-type compatibility, temporal/window lineage.
- **Action performed:** Create `EnsembleControlRecord` and control summaries for longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, ordinary ensemble/probability averaging, disagreement summaries, and delay-burden notes where feasible.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `EnsembleControlRecord`; A4 ordinary-control summaries; disagreement/control metric inputs.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Aggregation rule, member-selection rule, class order, score type, source prediction IDs, model IDs, window/trial alignment, temporal ordering, tie rule, and delay burden are explicit.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Hidden member selection, incompatible scores/class order, missing delay burden, or unmatched A4 keys makes affected A4 comparison diagnostic-only.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: EnsembleControlRecord]` `[EVAL: A4 fairness rules]`.

#### Step 10 — Index failures, missingness, and hard cases

- **Step objective:** Preserve negative evidence instead of hiding it.
- **Inputs consumed:** `PredictionRecord`, failed/skipped-run logs, `BaselineMetricRecord`, high-confidence wrong candidates where score fields allow, subject/session references.
- **Action performed:** Produce `FailureCaseIndex` entries and connect them to `NegativeResultNote`/`DiagnosticOnlyFlag` where evaluation governance requires them.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `FailureCaseIndex`; failed/skipped logs; negative-result/diagnostic inputs.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Source prediction/run/model/split IDs and limitation notes are present; correctness remains evaluation-only.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Hidden failed runs or omitted negative results invalidate fairness and block affected claims.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: FailureCaseIndex]` `[REG: NegativeResultNote]` `[EVAL: negative-result interpretation]`.

#### Step 11 — Validate downstream compatibility

- **Step objective:** Confirm that Phase 2 outputs are usable by Phase 3 and later phases without hidden reruns.
- **Inputs consumed:** All Layer 2 records, schemas, split/budget/score/class-order metadata, matched-key reports, metric dictionary status, consumer checklists.
- **Action performed:** Run downstream readiness validation and classify each output branch as pass, diagnostic-only, blocked, optional/stretch-only, unsupported, or requires confirmation.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** `Layer2ReadinessReport`; readiness warnings; consumer-compatibility matrix.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Phase 3 can join predictions to model registry, score schema, class order, split roles, labels where legal, and A0/A4 status.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Missing `Layer2ReadinessReport` blocks hidden downstream consumption.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: Downstream readiness validator]` `[REG: Layer2ReadinessReport]`.

#### Step 12 — Prepare Layer 10 dashboard/card/export source material

- **Step objective:** Make Phase 2 records visible and reproducible without allowing Layer 10 to generate or repair evidence.
- **Inputs consumed:** `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, `SubjectProfileRecord`, `EnsembleControlRecord`, `FailureCaseIndex`, logs, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, metric dictionary links, matched keys, config hashes, seeds.
- **Action performed:** Package dashboard-readable source records, warning inputs, model/benchmark card source bundles, and export-manifest inputs.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** Card source bundles for later `ModelCard`/`BenchmarkCard` rendering; export-manifest inputs; no primary dashboard evidence.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Every display/export input points back to source records, metric dictionary entries where needed, config hashes, seeds, validation status, and limitation tags.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Dashboard-derived repair, hidden recomputation, or missing lineage makes the dashboard output non-thesis-ready.
- **Source anchors:** `[REG: MC-011]` `[ARCH: Layer 10]`.

#### Step 13 — Attach Layer 0 claim-safety and diagnostic boundaries

- **Step objective:** Prevent baseline decoder evidence from being overclaimed.
- **Inputs consumed:** Phase 2 outputs, diagnostic flags, negative-result notes, limitation tags, Layer 0 claim-boundary vocabulary.
- **Action performed:** Attach allowed/forbidden claim labels, public-data/decoder-baseline/evaluation-only limitations, diagnostic-only triggers, and required stronger-evidence conditions.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** Claim-safety handoff inputs and later `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`/claim-audit inputs; no final thesis claim text.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** No Phase 2 output implies calibration, safety, clinical readiness, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, muscle stimulation control, deployment readiness, stress robustness, or embodiment consequence.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** Missing limitation tags or overclaim wording blocks claim-ready use until corrected by Layer 0 governance.
- **Source anchors:** `[ARCH: Layer 0]` `[REG: global claim-boundary tags]`.

#### Step 14 — Freeze Phase 2 outputs and hand off to Phase 3

- **Step objective:** Provide a versioned, traceable, immutable-enough package for Phase 3 and downstream consumers.
- **Inputs consumed:** Validated/diagnostic Phase 2 outputs and reports.
- **Action performed:** Freeze validated outputs, preserve diagnostic flags and open issues, document optional/stretch branch status, and produce the Phase 2 handoff package.
- **Records/artifacts produced:** Phase 2 handoff package; machine-readable handoff block in this playbook; no mutation of prior phases.
- **Validation/checkpoint:** Phase 3 receives prediction/model/score/class-order/split/metric/A0/A4/readiness/limitation package with complete lineage or explicit diagnostic status.
- **Failure/downgrade behavior:** If hard gates fail, Phase 3 cannot start except with mock/diagnostic records.
- **Source anchors:** `[EXEC: Phase 2 exit condition]` `[FRAME: phase handoff]`.

### 5A. Baseline-family coverage and fallback sufficiency rule

Phase 2 should attempt the architecture-supported model-family ladder, but it must not fabricate unavailable evidence or silently erase failed/skipped branches. The phase is valid when it produces a fair, traceable decoder spine with transparent coverage, not when every optional family succeeds. `[ARCH: Phase 2 model-family tiers]` `[EXEC: Phase 2 evidence-production logic]` `[EVAL: A0/A4 negative-result discipline]`

| Family or control branch | Phase 2 expectation | Required record/report handling | Downgrade or fallback rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sanity/lower-bound baseline | Core pipeline sanity check where supported. | `ModelRegistryRecord`, `PredictionRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, logs. | Missing sanity evidence weakens pipeline-validity interpretation and must be visible. |
| Classical CSP/LDA/SVM-style baseline | Core where compatible with source data and preprocessing. | Same matched source-record lineage as all other baseline families. | If incompatible, record skipped/unsupported reason; do not hide from denominator/coverage summaries. |
| Riemannian/tangent-space or robust classical baseline | Strongly recommended where data format and channel consistency allow. | Matched predictions/metrics or explicit failure/skipped status. | Absence is non-blocking only when feasibility limits are documented. |
| Compact neural baseline such as EEGNet/ShallowConvNet/temporal-convolutional family | Recommended where compute and data support it. | Model artifact/checkpoint status, seed/config hash, prediction records, metric records. | Non-convergence or infeasibility becomes `FailureCaseIndex`/log evidence, not a silent omission. |
| Optional compact SSL/foundation-style adapter | Optional/stretch only. | `ModelRegistryRecord` status plus predictions/metrics if feasible. | Skip is allowed for compute/license/input incompatibility; mark stretch-only and do not weaken core Phase 2. |
| A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Direct A4 obligation where alignment and compatible score/class-order/matched keys permit. | `EnsembleControlRecord`, control metrics, member-model links, aggregation config, delay/window burden notes, failure/skipped member visibility. | Incompatible or unmatched controls are diagnostic-only; do not rename them IHARQ, thresholding, selective prediction, or policy evidence. |
| Confidence-threshold rejection | Not Phase 2-owned A4 evidence. | Preserve raw scores/probabilities needed by Phase 3. | Registered threshold/confidence-threshold baseline remains A2 / Phase 3; Phase 2 must not collapse it into A4. |

**Fallback sufficiency discipline:** when complete family coverage is infeasible, Phase 2 should still proceed if it can produce validated A0 raw-decoder evidence, at least a documented core baseline set where feasible, explicit skipped/failed reasons, metric-dictionary or diagnostic status, matched-key status, low-calibration summaries, and a valid `Layer2ReadinessReport`. Stronger coverage improves thesis robustness, but missing optional/stretch branches must become visible limitations rather than invented outputs.

#### 6.2 Minimum `PredictionRecord` field envelope

The exact schema remains controlled by the Registry. Phase 2 must ensure every validated `PredictionRecord` has at least the grounded field families below where applicable:

| Field family | Required elements / rule | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Global record envelope | `record_id`, `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `producer_layer`, `validation_status`, `created_timestamp`, `config_hash`. | Missing global envelope. |
| Source and split lineage | dataset, subject, session, run, trial/window, split, preprocessing, label-map, seed, ablation/source IDs where applicable. | Missing source/split lineage or unresolved `MC-001` without recoverable `WindowRecord` lineage. |
| Decoder/model identity | `decoder_id`, `model_id`, `model_family`, `label_budget_id`. | Orphan prediction without `ModelRegistryRecord`. |
| Prediction payload | `predicted_class`, probability vector/logits/decision-score fallback or explicit missing score status, `score_type`, `class_order`. | Missing score schema blocks A1–A3 and score-dependent A4; label-only A0 may remain bounded/diagnostic depending claim. |
| Temporal payload | `time_start`/`time_end` where available and `timestamp_or_order` where temporal replay is required. | Temporal/replay/stress/simulation downstream use diagnostic-only. |
| Evaluation-only fields | `label_true` only when allowed by split policy and never as decision-time feature. | Label/correctness leakage blocks affected evidence. |
| Forbidden fields | Future reward, policy action, embodiment outcome, clinical safety approval, readiness decision, deployment status. | Record invalid for Phase 2 source use. |

#### 6.3 Output validation status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning in Phase 2 | Downstream use |
|---|---|---|
| `pass` / `validated` | Required schema, lineage, split, model, score/class-order, metric, and matched-key checks passed for the intended use. | Claim-eligible within Layer 0 limitations. |
| `diagnostic_only` | Record can be inspected but cannot support confirmatory or stronger comparison claims. | Visible in Layer 10 and Layer 0 limitations. |
| `blocked` | Required evidence is invalid, missing, leaked, orphaned, or unsafe to use. | Downstream consumption blocked except mock/development. |
| `optional_stretch_only` | Optional/stretch branch valid only for bounded stretch analysis. | Cannot be required for C0 core. |
| `skipped` / `unsupported` | Branch not run due to declared compute/license/input incompatibility or failure. | Must remain visible; no claim. |
| `requires_confirmation` | Source documents leave schema/path/statistical detail unresolved. | Carry open issue; diagnostic or claim-limiting until resolved. |

#### 6.4 Output consumers

| Consumer | Required Phase 2 handoff |
|---|---|
| Phase 3 | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, score/probability/logit availability, `score_type`, `class_order`, split IDs, label-map IDs, raw A0 status, A4 controls where feasible, and `Layer2ReadinessReport`. |
| Phase 4 | Prediction/model/baseline/A4/control/failure lineage for IHARQ-lite comparisons; no ownership transfer. |
| Phase 5 | Subject/session and temporal prediction lineage where allowed; no physiological diagnosis. |
| Phase 6–7 | Split-safe raw prediction/model context only through later readiness/policy records; evaluation-only fields excluded from decision-time policy state. |
| Phase 8–13 | Provenance/readiness context only after simulation/stress/embodiment phases own their records; Phase 2 does not prove those outcomes. |
| Phase 14 / Layer 10 | Read-only dashboard/card/export/reproducibility source bundle and warnings. |
| Phase 15 / Layer 0 | Claim-evidence inputs, limitation tags, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result references, and matched-key/metric status. |

### 7A. Artifact immutability and versioning rules

- Validated Phase 1 source records remain immutable. Phase 2 may exclude, flag, or request correction, but it must not rewrite them. `[REG: clean source-record immutability]`
- Validated `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` become clean Layer 2 source/provenance records. Later calibration, IHARQ, stress, simulation, embodiment, dashboard, policy, or claim-safety processes may derive from them but must not overwrite them. `[REG: Layer 2 clean source records]`
- `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, `SubjectProfileRecord`, `EnsembleControlRecord`, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, cards, views, figures, tables, and exports are derived/reporting/diagnostic artifacts. They require source IDs, source versions, derivation type/config, variant ID where applicable, run ID, seed, config hash, validation status, and inherited limitation tags. `[REG: derived-record governance]`
- Any repair after validation requires a new versioned record, supersession/repair log, exclusion record, diagnostic overlay, or BCR. Silent patching is forbidden. `[FRAME: immutability]`
- Claim-readiness is stricter than record existence: a record may validate as diagnostic/evaluation evidence while still being not thesis-ready due to metric dictionary gaps, matched-key gaps, unresolved open issues, or Layer 0 limitations. `[REG: shared output governance]`

### 8. Validation gates and exit conditions

#### 8.1 Phase-entry gates

| Gate | Pass condition | Diagnostic/blocking condition |
|---|---|---|
| Source package gate | Phase 0/1 handoff present; accepted prior content unchanged. | Missing prior package blocks Phase 2 except diagnostic draft. |
| Schema gate | Phase 0 schemas/validators available for Phase 2 records. | Missing schema blocks claim-ready outputs. |
| Public-data gate | Required Layer 1 records validate. | Missing/invalid source records block affected dataset. |
| Split/leakage gate | Split roles and leakage report pass. | Leakage invalidates affected evidence; unresolved split diagnostic-only/blocking. |
| Label-map/class-order gate | Label mapping and class order are compatible with model outputs. | Incompatible outputs invalid for metrics/comparisons. |
| Config/seed gate | Config hash and seed policy available. | Missing hash/seed downgrades reproducibility and comparison claims. |
| Budget gate | Budget table fixed before training where low-calibration evidence claimed. | Low-calibration branch diagnostic-only/invalid. |
| Metric dictionary gate | `MetricDictionaryEntry` exists for thesis-facing metric. | Metric claims diagnostic-only. |
| Dashboard/claim boundary gate | L10/L0 limitations and read-only boundaries available. | Dashboard/claim outputs non-thesis-ready. |

#### 8.2 Internal checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Required result | If failed |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline-family declaration | Core/target/stretch/optional model-family plan declared before final interpretation. | Post-hoc selection invalidates affected comparisons. |
| Model registry completeness | Every success/failure/skipped branch has `ModelRegistryRecord` or logged status. | Orphaned predictions or hidden failures block fairness. |
| Prediction schema completeness | `PredictionRecord` field envelope valid. | Downstream use blocked or diagnostic-only. |
| Score/class-order readiness | `score_type`, `class_order`, and score/probability/logit availability explicit. | A1–A3 and score-dependent A4 blocked/diagnostic. |
| A0 metric validity | Baseline metrics link to split, label map, metric dictionary, comparison key. | Metric claim diagnostic-only. |
| A4 fairness validity | Aggregation/member/window/delay/class-order/matched-key rules explicit. | A4 comparison diagnostic-only. |
| Low-calibration validity | Budget/split/seed/matched-key linkage complete. | Low-calibration claim diagnostic-only. |
| Subject-profile validity | No medical/physiological diagnosis; source lineage complete. | Profile excluded or diagnostic-only. |
| Failure visibility | Failed/skipped/unsupported branches and negative results visible. | Affected fairness/coverage claim invalid. |
| Readiness report | `Layer2ReadinessReport` generated. | Hidden downstream consumption blocked. |

#### 8.3 Exit criteria

Phase 2 exits as `ready_for_review` only when:

1. Required inputs validate or affected branches are explicitly excluded/diagnostic.
2. `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` exist for every selected dataset/subject/split/model family/seed/label budget intended for downstream comparison, or missing branches are logged with reason.
3. `BaselineMetricRecord` and A0 raw-decoder tables are produced for valid prediction branches and carry metric dictionary/matched-key status.
4. `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` and `SubjectProfileRecord` are produced where budgets/metadata support them, or are explicitly not applicable/diagnostic.
5. A4 `EnsembleControlRecord` and ordinary-control summaries are produced where feasible and matched; otherwise skipped/unsupported/diagnostic status is visible.
6. Missing logits/probabilities/decision scores are explicit and downstream eligibility is classified.
7. Failure, missingness, negative-result, and diagnostic-only artifacts are visible.
8. `Layer2ReadinessReport` validates downstream compatibility for Phase 3 and later consumers.
9. Layer 10 dashboard/card/export source material has source-record lineage and no derived repair.
10. Layer 0 limitation tags and forbidden-claim boundaries are attached.
11. No unresolved canonical-name mismatch is hidden.

#### 8.4 Blocking conditions

- unresolved split leakage in affected source records;
- missing required `PredictionRecord` for a claim-bearing branch;
- orphan predictions without `ModelRegistryRecord`;
- illegal preprocessing fit scope or label leakage;
- metric dictionary absence for thesis-facing metric claims;
- missing matched-comparison keys for comparison claims;
- missing `Layer2ReadinessReport` before Phase 3 handoff;
- hidden failed/skipped branches;
- dashboard recomputation or source-record repair;
- Phase 2 wording that implies readiness, safety, clinical, deployment, stress, simulation, or embodiment claims.

### 9. Matched-comparison key preservation

Phase 2 must preserve the keys below so A0/A4 and later A1–A13 comparisons remain fair. Missing keys downgrade the affected comparison to `diagnostic_only` or block it.

| Key family | Required Phase 2 keys | Applicability / non-applicability note |
|---|---|---|
| Source identity | `source_record_ids`, `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `run_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `parent_trial_id` where available. | Required for A0/A4 and downstream. Standalone `TrialRecord` remains unresolved; use `WindowRecord` lineage without inventing new record. |
| Split and budget | `split_id`, `split_role`, train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation partition, `label_budget_id`, budget version. | Required; no test-driven tuning. |
| Preprocessing | `preprocessing_id`, preprocessing version, fit scope, config hash. | Required to prevent leakage and mismatched inputs. |
| Label mapping | `label_map_id`, `label_map_version`, `class_order`. | Required for metrics, probabilities, and A4 member alignment. |
| Prediction/model provenance | `prediction_record_id`, `model_id`, `decoder_id`, `model_family`, checkpoint/artifact path or status, model config hash, training status, failed/skipped reason. | Required for `PredictionRecord`/`ModelRegistryRecord` closure. |
| Score schema | score availability, `score_type`, probability/logit/decision-score fallback, class-order mapping. | Required for Phase 3 and score-dependent A4. |
| Seed/config | seed ID, seed value where stored, config hash, environment/tool version where available. | Required for reproducibility and seed summaries. |
| Metric identity | `metric_dictionary_id`/`MetricDictionaryEntry`, metric name/family, denominator, aggregation level, split role, CI/seed summary where available. | Required for thesis-facing metric claims; absence diagnostic-only. |
| A0 identity | `ablation_id: A0`, raw/accept-all decoder reference status, no calibration/threshold/selective/IHARQ/policy credit. | Required for A0 evidence. |
| A4 identity | `ablation_id: A4`, aggregation/control family, number of windows/members, tie rule, averaging rule, member-selection rule, delay-burden note. | Required where ordinary controls are produced. |
| Comparison identity | `comparison_key`, comparator A-ID, matched source IDs, matched operating point where applicable, diagnostic-only flag. | Required for comparison claims. |
| Layer 10 lineage | export/readiness source IDs, config hash, seed, validation status, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result notes. | Required for cards/views/exports. |
| Layer 0 lineage | claim-safety tags, limitation labels, claim-evidence references where later generated, forbidden-claim audit status. | Required before stronger wording. |
| Calibration ID / threshold ID | Not produced by Phase 2. | Must be `not_applicable` in Phase 2 outputs; Phase 3 creates these IDs. |
| Policy/simulation/stress/embodiment IDs | Not produced by Phase 2. | Must be `not_applicable` unless used later by downstream phases as consumers. |
