### 9. Matched-comparison key preservation

Phase 3 must preserve the following key envelope for every A1–A3 row where applicable:

```text
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id where available
run_id
trial_id where available
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
label_budget_id
model_id
decoder_id
model_family
score_type
class_order
seed
schema_version
config_hash
prediction_record_id
model_registry_record_id
calibration_id where applicable
calibration_method where applicable
calibration_scope where applicable
calibration_split_id where applicable
uncertainty_record_id where applicable
uncertainty_feature where applicable
uncertainty_feature_config_id where applicable
selective_prediction_record_id where applicable
threshold_registry_id where applicable
threshold_selection_split_id where applicable
threshold_version where applicable
operating_point_id where applicable
metric_dictionary_id or metric_dictionary_entry_id
matched_comparison_key
coverage_or_cost_target_id where applicable
ablation_id
source_record_ids
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
diagnostic_only_flag where applicable
negative_result_note_id where applicable
layer10_export_id where exported
```

| Comparison family | Required preservation rule | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A0 → A1 raw-vs-calibrated | Same source predictions, model family, split, label budget, seed/config, and metric definitions where possible | Different underlying predictions without legal matched key |
| A1 calibration method comparisons | Same calibration split role, method config, budget, metric dictionary, and source records | Method selected or tuned on test labels |
| A2 simple registered threshold | Same threshold registry ID, selected-on split, target constraint, feature source, model/budget, and evaluation split | Unknown threshold, test-selected threshold, missing allowed-consumer list |
| A3 uncertainty feature comparisons | Same feature definition, class order, probability/calibration source, uncertainty-feature config, and aggregation unit | Missing feature definition, class-order mismatch, label-derived feature in decision-time field |
| A3 selective-prediction curves | Same risk/coverage denominator, metric dictionary, coverage/cost target, split role, source IDs, and threshold lineage | Missing metric dictionary, coverage collapse hidden, incompatible denominators |
| A4 ordinary-control context | Ordinary longer-window/voting/averaging/ensemble controls stay labeled A4 and must preserve window/class/model alignment | Rebranding ordinary controls as A3 or IHARQ |
| High-confidence wrong analysis | Evaluation split, confidence threshold, correctness source, model/subject/class grouping, diagnostic status | Used as decision-time feature or missing correctness source |

If a key is unavailable but the row remains useful for inspection, preserve it as `diagnostic_only` with missing-key reason and expose the warning to Layer 10 and Phase 15. Do not invent placeholder IDs to create apparent matchability. `[EVAL: A3 matched-key handling]` `[REG: MC-001]`

### 10. Ablation and evaluation obligations

| Ablation ID | Correct identity | Phase 3 obligation | Directly produced / prepared / consumed / preserved | Diagnostic-only triggers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A0` | Raw decoder baseline | Consume as raw comparator from Phase 2; do not modify raw predictions | Consumed/preserved | Missing A0 matched keys or metric dictionary weakens A1 deltas |
| `A1` | Calibrated decoder baseline | Directly produce calibration visibility evidence through `CalibrationRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, calibration metrics, and negative-result notes | Directly produced/enabled | Calibration leakage, invalid method, missing probabilities, missing metric dictionary, insufficient eligibility |
| `A2` | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Directly prepare and produce registered threshold/selective threshold evidence through `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, simple threshold rows, and matched operating points | Directly produced/enabled | Unregistered threshold, test-selected threshold, missing allowed-consumer/version/leakage status, unmatched operating point |
| `A3` | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Directly produce `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, risk-coverage/accuracy-coverage evidence, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, and selective-prediction matched keys | Directly produced/enabled | Label leakage into decision-time features, missing feature definitions, missing metric dictionary, coverage collapse hidden, unmatched keys |
| `A4` | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Preserve as Phase 2 comparator context where compatible; do not relabel as A3/IHARQ | Consumed/preserved | Misaligned windows/class order/models; ordinary control mislabeled |
| `A5` | IHARQ-lite | Prepare calibrated/uncertainty/threshold evidence consumed by Phase 4; do not produce IHARQ decisions | Prepared only | Missing Phase 3 source lineage blocks or downgrades Phase 4 use |
| `A6` | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Prepare upstream calibration/uncertainty context only; Phase 6 owns evidence-quality-estimator outputs | Prepared only | Phase 6 cannot use label-leaking diagnostics as decision-time features |
| `A7` | IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Prepare optional temporal uncertainty summaries only if order lineage valid; Phase 5 owns RegimeRisk outputs | Prepared only | Missing temporal order or leakage marks summaries diagnostic |
| `A8` | Learning-to-defer | Prepare reliability context for later deferral comparisons; no deferral records | Prepared only | Deferral claims unavailable |
| `A9` | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Prepare split-safe features for Phase 6 supervised policy; no policy records | Prepared only | Target leakage or missing context blocks policy use |
| `A10` | Contextual bandit | Preserve upstream lineage only | Lineage only | No bandit claim from Phase 3 |
| `A11` | RL policy | Preserve upstream lineage only | Lineage only | No RL claim from Phase 3 |
| `A12` | Stress tests | Preserve clean baseline reliability lineage for later stress comparison | Lineage only | Stress-conditioned claims require Phase 9/A12 records |
| `A13` | MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demonstration | Preserve upstream reliability lineage only | Lineage only | No embodiment claim from Phase 3 |

**Metric families Phase 3 must prepare or validate for Layer 10 and evaluation**

- Calibration/reliability: ECE-style summaries, Brier score, NLL, reliability-bin summaries, confidence histograms, high-confidence-wrong rate. `[EVAL: A1 metric families]`
- Uncertainty: confidence, entropy, normalized entropy, margin, variation ratio, disagreement where supported, conformal set size/proxy where declared. `[EVAL: A3 metric families]`
- Selective prediction: coverage, rejection rate, retained accuracy, retained error, risk, risk at coverage, coverage at target risk, accepted/wrong-accept rate where defined, class/subject/session coverage. `[EVAL: A2/A3 metric families]`
- Optional uncertainty-analysis summaries such as AUROC-style error detection or AURC-style metrics may be used only when defined in the metric dictionary with denominator, aggregation unit, directionality, split role, and claim boundary; they must not be framed as safety guarantees. `[ARCH: Layer 3 / core metrics]` `[REG: MC-008]`
- Matched comparisons: matched coverage/cost rows, metric dictionary IDs, diagnostic-only rate, threshold sufficiency, calibration failure/sufficiency notes. `[REG: Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable]`


**Local sub-ablation policy for Phase 3 A1–A3 evidence**

These local labels are evaluation-organization aids only. They are not official global ablation IDs, must not create `A14`, and must remain `candidate`, `optional_only`, `not_run`, or `requires_confirmation` unless the final protocol/run matrix explicitly activates them. They must preserve matched keys, metric dictionary linkage, split legality, and Layer 0/Layer 10 limitations. `[EVAL: A1 local sub-ablation policy]` `[EVAL: A2 local sub-ablation policy]` `[EVAL: A3 local sub-ablation policy]`

| Local family | Source-supported or candidate variants Phase 3 may prepare | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| A1 calibration-method children | `A1.0` no-calibration method anchor; temperature scaling; Platt/binary-compatible calibration; isotonic where legal data permit; vector/declared feasible method; pooled/global versus per-model scope; subject/session-aware diagnostics; calibration-budget sensitivity | Preserve method/scope/budget/split/model lineage; mark sparse or unsupported methods diagnostic-only; exact final method grid deferred. |
| A2 threshold children | raw-confidence threshold, calibrated-confidence threshold, matched-coverage operating point, matched-cost operating point, threshold-selection-rule comparison | Every threshold must have `ThresholdRegistryRecord` lineage, selected-on split, target constraint, allowed consumers, version, leakage status, and metric dictionary support; exact labels/grid deferred. |
| A3 uncertainty/selective children | confidence uncertainty profile, entropy/normalized entropy, margin, variation ratio, optional model disagreement, optional conformal proxy, matched-coverage/matched-cost operating point, groupwise selective-prediction audit | Decision-time fields must be label-free; optional disagreement/conformal rows remain optional/stretch or diagnostic unless source support and split safety are complete; A4 ordinary ensemble controls must not be rebranded as A3. |

Final run counts, exact statistical tests, and final reporting tables are not defined in Phase 3 and remain deferred to the final Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol and Phase 15 evidence map. `[FRAME: Experiment Protocol boundary]`

### 11. Dashboard, card, and reproducibility obligations

Layer 10 must receive Phase 3 source evidence in read-only, reproducible form. It may render, filter, card, export, and audit; it must not recalibrate, tune thresholds, select operating points, repair split issues, hide negative results, or treat dashboard plots as primary evidence. `[ARCH: Layer 10]` `[REG: MC-011]`

| Layer 10 handoff family | Required Phase 3 source package | Validation requirement | Prohibited Layer 10 action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calibration overview | `CalibrationRecord`, calibration method report, reliability-bin source data, metric dictionary refs | Source IDs, calibration split, method/config hash, validation status | Refit calibration or select method |
| Reliability diagrams and confidence histograms | `ReliabilityAuditReport`, figure-source data, bin definitions | Metric dictionary, source records, seed/config, split role | Use screenshots as evidence or hide sparse bins |
| Uncertainty views | `UncertaintyRecord`, feature definitions, missing-feature warnings | Feature config, class-order, source probability/calibration lineage | Fill missing features as if measured |
| Risk-coverage and selective-prediction views | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, risk/coverage curve source data, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` | Denominators, split roles, threshold registry IDs, matched keys | Tune threshold from dashboard view |
| Threshold registry view | `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, threshold summary table | Version, selected-on split, leakage status, allowed consumers | Approve unknown thresholds silently |
| High-confidence-error views | `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, diagnostic flags, correctness source | Evaluation-only labels and split role explicit | Feed high-confidence wrong flags into decision-time policy |
| Group-wise reliability view | `ReliabilityAuditReport`, group filters, subject/session/class/model/budget keys | Group count/instability warnings | Hide group-specific failure pockets |
| Calibration-budget view | `CalibrationEligibilityTable`, low-calibration context, budget metadata, calibration stability, threshold variability where available | Sparse/missing-class warnings and budget-lineage completeness | Convert sparse-budget diagnostics into success claims or final run-matrix claims |
| Reliability cards | ReliabilityCard source inputs from Phase 3; rendered later by Layer 10 | Source records, warning banners, diagnostic status, claim boundaries | Treat card text as primary empirical evidence |
| Reproducibility/export | Phase 3 handoff manifest, config snapshots, metric dictionary refs, seeds, hashes, source paths, validation overlays | Complete lineage and source-location availability | Repair or recompute source artifacts without a versioned rerun |

`CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` remains a dashboard-readable metric source candidate with unresolved schema/path status; it should be exported with explicit source lineage and must not be promoted into a Layer 10-owned empirical record. `[REG: CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord / MC-007]`

### 12. Claim-safety and limitation boundaries

#### 12.1 Allowed claim classes after Phase 3

Phase 3 may support only bounded claims such as:

- Public EEG decoder confidence can be made calibration-visible under declared splits and budgets. `[EVAL: A1 allowed claims]`
- Calibration may improve, fail to improve, or reveal limitations in confidence reliability according to declared metrics. `[EVAL: A1 negative-result rule]`
- Label-free uncertainty features and selective-prediction baselines can be evaluated under matched coverage/cost and legal split constraints. `[EVAL: A3]`
- Registered thresholds and operating points can serve as fair baselines for later IHARQ/adaptive-policy comparisons. `[EVAL: A2/A3]`
- High-confidence wrong cases and group-wise reliability failures can be exposed as diagnostic limitation evidence. `[REG: HighConfidenceWrongTable]`
- Phase 0–3 may satisfy the C0 public-data reliability spine only if all C0 gates and limitations are satisfied. `[ARCH: C0]`

#### 12.2 Forbidden overclaims

Phase 3 must not claim:

- clinical validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real-time deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- rehabilitation efficacy;
- that calibration alone makes decisions safe;
- that uncertainty features are safety guarantees;
- that thresholds are clinical or deployment safety thresholds;
- IHARQ readiness decisions or RegimeRisk trust states;
- learned evidence-quality, policy, deferral, bandit, RL, stress, simulation, or embodiment improvement;
- dashboard-generated figures/cards as independent evidence.

#### 12.3 Required limitation labels

At minimum, Phase 3 claim-facing outputs must carry relevant labels such as:

```text
public_eeg_only
offline_evaluation_only
calibration_visibility_only
uncertainty_proxy_only
selective_prediction_baseline_only
registered_threshold_not_safety_threshold
high_confidence_wrong_evaluation_only
not_decision_time_label_feature
matched_keys_required
metric_dictionary_required
diagnostic_only_where_triggered
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_deployment_readiness
dashboard_source_not_primary_evidence
negative_result_visible
```

Any stronger claim requires downstream evidence from the appropriate phase and must preserve Phase 3 lineage, metric dictionary links, matched keys, diagnostic flags, negative-result notes, and the strictest inherited limitation tags. `[REG: ClaimEvidenceMatrix / DiagnosticOnlyFlag]` `[ARCH: Layer 0]`

---

### 13. Failure, missingness, and diagnostic-only handling

| Failure mode | Required handling | Diagnostic-only / blocking effect | Source anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Missing or invalid `PredictionRecord` | Exclude affected rows or request upstream versioned repair | Blocks Phase 3 outputs for affected rows | `[REG: PredictionRecord]` |
| Missing `ModelRegistryRecord` linkage | Do not promote calibrated/uncertainty records | Blocks affected calibration/uncertainty claims | `[REG: ModelRegistryRecord]` |
| Missing probability/logit/decision score fields | Mark explicit missing-score status | A1–A3 calibration/uncertainty rows diagnostic or ineligible | `[PRIOR: Phase 2 score readiness]` |
| Invalid `score_type` or `class_order` | Fail eligibility check; do not infer class order | Blocks affected rows | `[REG: PredictionRecord]` |
| Calibration/threshold/test leakage | Emit `LeakageWarningRecord`; block final claims | Blocking unless rerun/versioned repair | `[REG: LeakageWarningRecord]` |
| Test-selected calibration method or threshold | Mark oracle/exploratory diagnostic only | Cannot serve as fair baseline | `[ARCH: split discipline]` |
| Sparse or missing-class calibration split | Record in `CalibrationEligibilityTable` and use declared fallback if legal | Method-specific claim diagnostic or blocked | `[REG: CalibrationEligibilityTable]` |
| Calibration does not improve ECE/Brier/NLL | Preserve `NegativeResultNote` | Claim narrows; result remains useful | `[EVAL: negative-result discipline]` |
| Missing metric dictionary entries | Attach `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`; preserve metric definitions needed | Metric claims diagnostic-only | `[REG: MC-008]` |
| Missing matched keys | Keep rows visible but non-confirmatory | Improvement/sufficiency claims diagnostic-only | `[EVAL: matched-comparison rule]` |
| Label-derived uncertainty feature in decision-time field | Repartition fields and revalidate | Severe leakage; downstream decision use invalid | `[REG: UncertaintyRecord / HighConfidenceWrongTable]` |
| High-confidence wrong table used as policy feature | Block downstream use; add diagnostic/claim warning | Decision run invalid | `[REG: HighConfidenceWrongTable]` |
| Unregistered or unknown threshold | Fail final run or mark exploratory | A2/A3 and downstream threshold use invalid | `[REG: ThresholdRegistryRecord]` |
| Coverage collapse hidden by selective prediction | Produce warning and matched coverage/cost reporting | Selective-success claim diagnostic-only | `[EVAL: A3 metric families]` |
| Dashboard export lacks source IDs/config hash | Exclude from reproducibility package or diagnostic-export only | Dashboard claim not thesis-ready | `[REG: CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord / MC-011]` |
| Hidden failed/skipped/sparse/ineligible cases | Restore failure visibility through notes/flags | Claim readiness blocked | `[EVAL: negative-result discipline]` |
| Overclaiming safety/clinical/deployment | Apply Layer 0 downgrade/invalid-claim flag | Claim blocked | `[REG: MC-012]` |

Negative outcomes must be preserved, not silently omitted. Where evidence is invalid but still informative, Phase 3 should produce diagnostic artifacts with explicit limitations rather than deleting the row. `[FRAME: failure/missingness discipline]`

---

### 14. Repository, storage, and reproducibility expectations

Where source documents provide architecture-supported storage families, Phase 3 should use them as conceptual or implementation-guiding expectations without inventing final repository layout. Final concrete paths remain subject to `MC-009` and the future Implementation Build Book. `[REG: MC-009]` `[FRAME: Implementation Build Book boundary]`

| Artifact family | Source-supported expectation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 3 source module family | `src/layer3_calibration_uncertainty/` or repository module C equivalent | Architecture/registry supported, but final implementation details deferred |
| Calibration configs | `configs/layer3/calibration_methods.yaml` where used | Source-supported config expectation; exact final config schema deferred |
| Uncertainty configs | `configs/layer3/uncertainty_features.yaml` where used | Source-supported config expectation |
| Selective-prediction configs | `configs/layer3/selective_prediction.yaml` where used | Source-supported config expectation |
| Threshold registry config/artifact | `configs/layer3/threshold_registry.yaml`, `threshold_registry.yaml`, records/registries family | Source-supported; every threshold version must retain selected-on split and allowed consumers |
| `CalibrationRecord` | `records/calibration_records/`; run-local `results/layer3/calibration_records.parquet` supported as examples | Source-supported/run-local; concrete final path unresolved |
| `UncertaintyRecord` | `records/uncertainty_records/`; run-local `results/layer3/uncertainty_records.parquet` supported as examples | Source-supported/run-local; concrete final path unresolved |
| `SelectivePredictionRecord` | `records/selective_prediction_records/`; run-local selective file | Architecture-supported family/run-local |
| `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | `records/threshold_registry_records/`, `registries/`, threshold registry file | Explicit supported family |
| Reliability/split/leakage reports | Reports/records conceptual or run-local with `split_integrity_rules.yaml` and `groupwise_audit.yaml` inputs where used | Conceptual/run-local; exact path deferred |
| `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` | Layer 3 export area or `records/dashboard_metric_records/` after Layer 10 merge | Unresolved with Layer 10; candidate source metric record |
| Cards/figures/tables/manifests | Source records for cards/figures/thesis tables/manifests/dashboard exports | Layer 10/final integration renders; Phase 3 exports source data only |

Every stored Phase 3 output must retain source IDs, schema version, producer layer/module, phase ID, run ID, seed, config hash, validation status, split/leakage status, metric dictionary references where metrics are used, diagnostic-only flags where needed, negative-result note references where applicable, and claim-safety tags. `[REG: required lineage envelope]`

---

### 15. Phase handoff package

When Phase 3 completes, it hands forward a validated or explicitly diagnostic reliability evidence package.

#### 15.1 Required handoff contents

| Handoff item | Downstream consumer | Required status |
|---|---|---|
| `CalibrationRecord` bundle | Phase 4, Phase 6, L10, Phase 15 | Validated or diagnostic-only with reason |
| `UncertaintyRecord` bundle | Phase 4, Phase 6, optional Phase 5, L10 | Label-free features validated; optional fields marked |
| `SelectivePredictionRecord` bundle | Phase 4, Phase 6, L10, evaluation | Legal split and threshold registry status present |
| `ThresholdRegistryRecord` bundle | Phase 4, Phase 6, L10, experiment controller | Every downstream threshold registered/versioned |
| `ReliabilityAuditReport` | L10, Phase 15, negative-result/claim review | Metric/source/bin/group lineage present |
| `SplitIntegrityReport` and `LeakageWarningRecord` where any | Experiment controller, L10, L0, downstream phases | Claim eligibility and leakage status explicit |
| `CalibrationEligibilityTable` | Phase 4/6/L10/evaluation | Sparse/missing-class/fallback status visible |
| `HighConfidenceWrongTable` | L10, L4/L6 offline failure analysis, Phase 15 | Evaluation-only; not decision-time feature |
| `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` and ReliabilityCard source inputs | Phase 14 / L10 | Source IDs/config/metric/diagnostic status present |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` | Evaluation, L10, Phase 15, Phase 4/6 comparisons | Matched/unmatched status explicit |
| `NegativeResultNote` and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` references | L0, L10, Phase 15 | All affected rows linked and visible |
| Phase 3 handoff manifest | Phases 4–15, L10, L0 | Complete IDs, paths, hashes, validations, limitations, open issues |

#### 15.2 Immediate next-phase handoff to Phase 4

Phase 4 may begin IHARQ-lite evidence verification only for rows with valid or explicitly diagnostic Phase 3 handoff status. It requires calibrated probabilities or declared raw/no-calibration context, uncertainty features, threshold registry entries, source prediction/model/split lineage, matched keys, and claim-safety tags. If Phase 3 records are missing, label-leaking, unregistered, unmatched, or leakage-affected, Phase 4 must block affected final comparisons or run them diagnostic-only. `[EXEC: Phase 4 dependency]` `[ARCH: Layer 4 input contract]`

#### 15.3 Later-phase handoff

- Phase 5 may consume temporal uncertainty summaries only where time/order lineage is valid; Phase 3 does not produce `RegimeStateRecord`. `[ARCH: Layer 5 optional input]`
- Phase 6 may consume label-free calibration/uncertainty/threshold context; Phase 3 does not produce `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `ReadinessContextRecord`, or `PolicyActionRecord`. `[EVAL: A6/A9 ownership boundary]`
- Phase 14/Layer 10 receives source records and card inputs only; final dashboard views/cards/exports are derived. `[REG: MC-011]`
- Phase 15 receives claim-bounded evidence, diagnostic flags, negative results, metric dictionary links, and matched-comparison status for final thesis integration. `[EXEC: Phase 15 integration context]`

### 16. Open issues and requires-confirmation items

| Open issue | Classification | Phase 3 impact | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MC-001` `TrialRecord` / trial-level source representation | Non-blocking but claim-limiting | Ambiguous trial identity can weaken high-confidence-wrong traceability and matched operating points | Use `WindowRecord`/`PredictionRecord` trial fields where present; mark missing trial identity diagnostic for affected comparisons |
| `MC-007` dashboard metric boundary | Non-blocking but claim-limiting | `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` may be confused with Layer 10 dashboard outputs | Preserve as dashboard-readable source input only |
| `MC-008` `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema/path | Diagnostic-only risk | ECE/Brier/NLL/risk/coverage metrics may not be thesis-ready if definitions/paths absent | Require metric dictionary references or mark metrics diagnostic-only |
| `MC-009` repository paths and storage homes | Implementation-detail deferred | Concrete loaders/export paths may be unstable | Use conceptual/source-supported storage families; finalize in Implementation Build Book/dashboard integration |
| `MC-010` lifecycle/schema maturity and branch status | Non-blocking but claim-limiting | Candidate artifacts could be promoted silently | Preserve candidate/normalized statuses explicitly |
| `MC-011` Layer 10 evidence boundary | Claim-limiting | Dashboard cards/figures could be mistaken for empirical evidence | Keep Layer 10 read/export/derived-only boundary |
| `MC-012` Layer 0 evidence boundary | Claim-limiting | Claim-audit artifacts could be mistaken for empirical evidence | Keep Layer 0 as audit/governance only |
| `CalibrationEligibilityTable` status | Diagnostic-only risk | Candidate status may be confused with final schema | Keep `normalized_candidate`; include source lineage and validation status |
| `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` schema/path | Diagnostic-only risk | Dashboard ingestion/export may need later reconciliation | Export as source metric candidate and carry unresolved schema/path |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` storage path | Implementation-detail deferred | Fair-comparison table location may be unresolved | Link through handoff manifest until final path confirmation |
| Optional conformal, disagreement, and temporal uncertainty fields | Optional/stretch clarification | Optional features may be overclaimed | Mark optional/proxy-only and split-safe when implemented; omit without weakening core Phase 3 |
| Final statistical run matrix | Implementation/evaluation-detail deferred | Cannot finalize significance testing or final run counts here | Defer to final Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol and Phase 15 |

### 17. Back-Propagation Correction Request handling

No Back-Propagation Correction Request is required for this generated Phase 3 section at document-generation time. The accepted Phase 0–2 playbook already states Phase 2 prepares A1–A3 and produces A0/A4 context, carries registry issues forward, and preserves the A0–A13 corrected identities. `[PRIOR: Phase 2 final audit]`

If implementation or review reveals a real prior-phase defect, Phase 3 must create a request using this structure and continue only under the stated diagnostic effect:

```yaml
back_propagation_request:
  request_id: "BCR-P3-<sequence>"
  discovered_in_phase: "Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty"
  affected_prior_phase: "Phase 0 | Phase 1 | Phase 2"
  affected_artifact_or_record: "<canonical artifact/record name>"
  issue_type: "schema_gap | split_leakage | missing_lineage | alias_conflict | metric_dictionary_gap | matched_key_gap | claim_boundary_gap | other_grounded_issue"
  severity: "blocking | non_blocking_claim_limiting | diagnostic_only_risk | implementation_detail_deferred"
  source_conflict: "<specific [ARCH]/[REG]/[EXEC]/[EVAL]/[PRIOR] anchors>"
  downstream_risk: "<effect on Phase 3 and later phases>"
  required_action: "<versioned upstream repair, validation overlay, explicit diagnostic flag, or confirmation>"
  whether_current_phase_can_continue: "yes_with_diagnostic_limits | no_blocked_until_repair | yes_no_effect"
  diagnostic_only_effect: "<affected rows/comparisons/claims>"
  claim_safety_effect: "<Layer 0 limitation/downgrade>"
```

Back-propagation must not silently modify prior accepted prose or overwrite validated upstream records. `[FRAME: Back-Propagation Correction Request template]`

### 18. Definition of done

Phase 3 is complete when the following checklist is satisfied or explicitly downgraded:

| Checklist item | Required status |
|---|---|
| Prior Phase 0–2 handoff consumed without mutation | Complete |
| Required Phase 1 source records join to predictions | Complete or diagnostic missing-key report |
| Required Phase 2 `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` inputs validated | Complete for claim-facing rows |
| `score_type`, `class_order`, probability/logit/decision-score availability validated | Complete or affected rows ineligible/diagnostic |
| Calibration/threshold/test split separation checked | Complete; leakage emits `LeakageWarningRecord` |
| At least no-calibration baseline and one feasible declared calibration method evaluated where data permit | Complete or sparse/missing-class diagnostic |
| `CalibrationRecord` produced for eligible rows | Complete with source IDs/config/hash/status |
| `UncertaintyRecord` produced with label-free decision-time fields | Complete; label-derived fields excluded |
| `SelectivePredictionRecord` produced for declared selective/threshold baselines | Complete or diagnostic with reason |
| `ThresholdRegistryRecord` exists for every downstream-used threshold | Complete; unknown/test-tuned thresholds blocked/diagnostic |
| `ReliabilityAuditReport` and reliability source data produced | Complete with metric dictionary references or diagnostic flags |
| `HighConfidenceWrongTable` produced where legal labels permit | Complete and evaluation-only |
| `SplitIntegrityReport` and `CalibrationEligibilityTable` or equivalent eligibility reporting produced | Complete; candidate status preserved where applicable |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` produced or missing-matchability flags attached | Complete or diagnostic |
| `NegativeResultNote` and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` attached where required | Complete |
| Layer 10 source bundle exported | Complete with source IDs, hashes, metrics, warnings, and limitations |
| Layer 0 claim-safety tags attached | Complete |
| Handoff manifest created and downstream-readable | Complete |
| Open issues carried forward | Complete |
| No unsupported canonical names, phases, ablations, modules, metrics, claims, paths, commands, classes, or tests introduced | Complete |

Phase 3’s completion statement: when done, Phase 3 hands forward a validated reliability evidence set containing calibrated probabilities, label-free uncertainty features, selective-prediction and threshold baselines, threshold registry entries, reliability audits, split-integrity/eligibility reports, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, matched operating points, negative-result notes, dashboard-readable source bundles, and claim-safety limitations. This enables Phase 4 and later phases while preserving the boundary that Phase 3 provides reliability evidence only, not readiness decisions, clinical safety, deployment readiness, real assistive control, or rehabilitation efficacy. `[EXEC: Phase 3 completion statement]`

### 0A. Source Extraction Digest

This digest operationalizes the source facts needed to execute Phase 4. It intentionally condenses, rather than reproduces, the source documents.

#### 0A.1 Master Architecture Specification extraction

- Phase 4 activates **Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification**, the post-decoder/post-calibration readiness-control layer that asks whether current neural-intent evidence is strong, stable, calibrated, and safe enough to support a simulated or proxy readiness action now. [ARCH: Layer 4 / problem solved]
- Layer 4 sits after Layer 2 predictions and Layer 3 calibration/uncertainty, before learned adaptive policy layers and simulated/embodiment layers. It transforms saved calibrated prediction evidence into action candidates, reason codes, costs, and traces for downstream layers without rerunning or retraining upstream models. [ARCH: Layer 4 / position in architecture]
- The canonical stored Layer 4 action tokens are `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, and `unsafe`. Human-facing labels may differ, but stored Phase 4 records must not drift to aliases such as `combine`, `request-evidence`, `hold`, or `no_action`. [ARCH: Layer 4 / action vocabulary]
- Active Layer 4 module responsibilities include evidence feature building, input validation, window stability checking, channel-subset checking, model-family agreement checking, IHARQ rule-engine execution, evidence combination, fallback routing, unsafe-state monitoring, decision logging, ablation/matched-comparison export, and dashboard/claim-evidence export. [ARCH: Layer 4 / submodules]
- Layer 5 RegimeRisk can later feed Layer 4 through explicitly bounded, ablatable feedback, but core Phase 4 precedes Phase 5 and must therefore produce a regime-unaware IHARQ-lite baseline unless valid Phase 5 records are present in a later versioned analysis. [ARCH: Layer 4 / RegimeRisk feedback integration] [EXEC: Phase 4 before Phase 5]
- Layer 10 may read, validate, warn, summarize, visualize, export, and package Phase 4 records, but it must not recompute IHARQ decisions, retune thresholds, repair split leakage, or create hidden primary evidence. [ARCH: Layer 10 / dashboard and reproducibility]
- Layer 0 limits Phase 4 claims to public-data/offline/proxy evidence-verification findings. Phase 4 cannot establish clinical safety, real-time BCI deployment, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle-stimulation control, or real assistive-control safety. [ARCH: Layer 0 / claim boundaries]

#### 0A.2 Canonical Registry extraction

- Phase 4 canonical or registry-recognized output families are `IHARQDecisionRecord`, rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, `UnsafeEventRecord`, `IHARQAblationRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, and claim-evidence artifacts such as `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` where applicable. [REG: Layer 4 output family]
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` is a shared-producer issue: Phase 4 may produce rule-derived evidence-quality or compatibility records, while Phase 6 owns learned evidence-quality-estimator outputs. Phase 4 outputs must therefore include producer module, phase ID, branch/variant, source IDs, and target-construction boundary fields where applicable. [REG: MC-002 EvidenceQualityRecord]
- `EnsembleControlRecord` is a normalized/candidate Layer 2 ordinary-control artifact for A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls. Phase 4 may consume it for matched A4 comparisons but must not treat it as IHARQ. [REG: EnsembleControlRecord normalized_candidate]
- Local helper views such as `WindowHistoryRecord`, `ChannelSubsetStabilityRecord`, and `ModelAgreementRecord` are not promoted to global canonical records unless a later registry reconciliation does so. Phase 4 may use them as local/precomputed helper views derived from canonical upstream records, with schema maturity and missingness declared. [REG: local helper view warning]
- Validated upstream records are immutable. Phase 4 may write derived/versioned records, overlays, diagnostics, manifests, comparison rows, and handoff bundles, but it must not mutate `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, or `EnsembleControlRecord`. [REG: artifact lifecycle / immutability]
- Thesis-facing metrics require `MetricDictionaryEntry` or `MetricDictionary` support; missing metric definitions, missing matched keys, or missing source lineage force diagnostic-only treatment. [REG: MetricDictionaryEntry / MC-008]
- Known open issues include `TrialRecord` or trial-level source representation, `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` versus `ClaimEvidenceManifest`, dashboard metric/card boundary, exact metric dictionary schema/path, exact repository/storage homes, lifecycle/status vocabulary, Layer 10 evidence boundary, Layer 0 evidence boundary, and final local A5 sub-ablation numbering. [REG: MC issue ledger]

#### 0A.3 Execution and Evidence Plan extraction

- Phase 4 officially follows `Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty` and precedes `Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust`. [EXEC: Phase 0–15 phase ladder]
- Phase 4 consumes Phase 0 infrastructure, Phase 1 public-data/split/window/source lineage, Phase 2 prediction/model/baseline/ordinary-control evidence, and Phase 3 calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction/threshold/matched-operating-point evidence. [EXEC: Phase 4 input contract] [PRIOR: Phase 3 handoff]
- Phase 4 produces deterministic/rule-based IHARQ-lite evidence-verification records and A5-ready matched evaluation artifacts. It does not train decoders, recalibrate probabilities, select new test-tuned thresholds, create RegimeRisk records, learn adaptive policies, run closed-loop simulation, generate stress profiles, create embodiment records, render final dashboard cards, or approve final thesis claims. [EXEC: Phase 4 output contract]
- Phase 4 must not use `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, future labels, future outcomes, rewards, or oracle correctness as ordinary decision-time inputs. Those may support evaluation-only or diagnostic/headroom analysis only if separated and labeled. [EXEC: Phase 3 handoff to Phase 4]
- Phase 4 must enforce validation gates for upstream completeness, split/leakage legality, threshold registration, canonical action-token use, deterministic IHARQ-lite boundaries, matched-comparison eligibility, metric dictionary coverage, Layer 10 audit/export readiness, and Layer 0 claim-safety readiness. [EXEC: Phase 4 validation gates]
- Phase 4 must hand off regime-unaware IHARQ-lite evidence to Phase 5 and preserve compatibility with Phase 6 and later phases through records, keys, action costs, reason codes, limitation tags, and diagnostics. [EXEC: Phase 4 downstream handoff]

#### 0A.4 Evaluation Protocol v0.1 extraction

- Phase 4 directly enables **A5 = IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification**. A5 is an evaluation context, not a phase, layer, module, record owner, learned policy, dashboard, clinical-safety mechanism, or embodiment-validation claim. [EVAL: A5 identity]
- Phase 4 must consume/preserve matched comparator evidence for **A0 = raw decoder baseline**, **A1 = calibrated decoder baseline**, **A2 = simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline**, **A3 = uncertainty and selective prediction**, and **A4 = longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls**. [EVAL: A0–A4 comparator identities]
- Phase 4 prepares but does not complete **A6 = IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator**. Phase 6 directly produces learned evidence-quality-estimator outputs and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ evidence; Phase 4 only supplies upstream IHARQ/evidence records and rule-derived compatibility context. [EVAL: A6 boundary]
- Phase 4 prepares lineage for **A7–A13** but does not complete RegimeRisk, learning-to-defer, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, contextual bandit, RL, stress-test, or embodiment-demo evidence. [EVAL: A7–A13 downstream status]
- A5 metric families include accepted-decision accuracy/reliability where applicable, wrong-accept proxy rate, coverage/accepted fraction, request rate, combine rate and success/failure, fallback rate/burden, unsafe proxy rate, uncertain rate, action/evidence/delay cost, reason-code distribution, trace completeness, matched deltas against A0–A4, high-confidence-wrong diagnostic relation, and degraded-evidence frequency. Exact denominators/statistical tests remain deferred unless canonical metric entries fix them. [EVAL: A5 metric families]
- A5 requires local negative-result discipline: if A2, A3, A4, fallback-only, or other source-supported simpler controls match or outperform A5 under matched conditions, that is a valid `NegativeResultNote`, not a result to hide. [EVAL: A5 negative results]
- The supplemental `eval_A5_full.md` cross-check confirms the A5 producer-consumer boundary, local A5 labels, Layer 10 warning obligations, Layer 0 forbidden-claim list, and v0.1-versus-v1.0 deferral language already used here. [EVAL-FULL: A5 sections 7–22]

#### 0A.5 Previously accepted phase extraction

- Phase 0 supplies schema/config/validator/metric/manifest/claim/dashboard infrastructure and open issue tracking. Phase 4 inherits these controls and may not bypass unresolved Phase 0 gaps. [PRIOR: Phase 0 handoff]
- Phase 1 supplies public-data identity, split/protocol records, window/source lineage, artifact/source flags, and public-data limitation tags. Phase 4 depends on those identifiers to build matched decisions and comparisons. [PRIOR: Phase 1 handoff]
- Phase 2 supplies `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, baseline metric evidence, low-calibration/profile/failure artifacts, and A4 ordinary-control evidence where available. Phase 4 consumes but does not repair or retrain these. [PRIOR: Phase 2 handoff]
- Phase 3 supplies `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, `SplitIntegrityReport`, `LeakageWarningRecord`, `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord`, and `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` where accepted. Phase 4 consumes legal decision-time parts and treats high-confidence-wrong labels/correctness as diagnostic/evaluation-only. [PRIOR: Phase 3 handoff]
- The accepted Phase 3 handoff to Phase 4 requires calibrated confidence, uncertainty features, threshold registry IDs, selective-prediction baselines, split-integrity status, metric dictionary references, matched-comparison keys, negative-result notes, and diagnostic-only flags to remain visible. [PRIOR: Phase 3 immediate downstream handoff]

| Later downstream consumers | Phase 6, Phase 7, Phase 8, Phase 9, Phase 10, Phase 11, Phase 12, Phase 13, Phase 14, Phase 15 through later readiness, policy, evaluation, stress, embodiment, dashboard, and final-thesis handoffs |
| Claim status after phase | Conditional computational/proxy IHARQ-lite evidence-verification evidence only; claim-ready only for matched, limitation-tagged, metric-defined, trace-complete comparisons |

#### 1.2 In-scope work

Phase 4 is in scope to:

- validate upstream source/prediction/calibration/uncertainty/threshold/ordinary-control inputs before IHARQ-lite execution; [EXEC: Phase 4 input validation]
- assemble decision-time evidence features from legal upstream records and declared local helper views; [ARCH: Layer 4 evidence feature builder]
- run deterministic, rule-based IHARQ-lite decision logic using canonical stored action tokens; [ARCH: Layer 4 rule engine]
- emit reason-coded `IHARQDecisionRecord` and `IHARQTraceRecord` rows with source IDs, rule paths, configuration hashes, matched-comparison keys, metric references, limitation tags, and diagnostic flags; [REG: IHARQDecisionRecord / IHARQTraceRecord]
- emit `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, and `UnsafeEventRecord` only when the corresponding behavior is actually active and traceable; [REG: Layer 4 output family]
- emit rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord` only with producer/variant tags that prevent confusion with Phase 6 learned evidence-quality outputs; [REG: MC-002 EvidenceQualityRecord]
- prepare `IHARQAblationRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry` references, `NegativeResultNote`, and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` material for A5 and Layer 10/Layer 0 review; [EVAL: A5 required artifacts]
- preserve A0–A4 comparator lineage and matched-comparison keys for valid A5 interpretation; [EVAL: A5 comparators]
- produce a Phase 4 handoff package to Phase 5 and later phases without silently upgrading claims. [EXEC: Phase 4 downstream handoff]

#### 1.3 Explicit non-scope

Phase 4 must not:

- create or modify public data splits, label maps, windows, preprocessing records, or artifact flags; [ARCH: Layer 1 boundary]
- train, repair, or select decoders; [ARCH: Layer 2 boundary]
- fit calibration, compute new uncertainty features, or choose final thresholds from test labels; [ARCH: Layer 3 boundary]
- create RegimeRisk, trust-state, stop-loss, or temporal regime records as core Phase 4 outputs; [EXEC: Phase 4 before Phase 5]
- produce learned evidence-quality-estimator outputs or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ records; [EVAL: A6 ownership boundary]
- produce learning-to-defer, contextual-bandit, RL, stress-test, simulated closed-loop, or embodiment-demo results; [EVAL: A8–A13 downstream]
- render final dashboard cards, final static figures/tables, or final export packages as Layer 10 products; [ARCH: Layer 10 boundary]
- approve final thesis claims, final paper wording, table/figure numbering, or clinical/deployment claims; [ARCH: Layer 0 boundary] [FRAMEWORK: paper/thesis non-interference]
- invent repository paths, classes, CLI commands, final seeds, final statistical tests, or a final run matrix. [FRAMEWORK: implementation and evaluation-protocol non-interference]

### 1A. Capability-tier and thesis-validity relevance

| Capability tier | Phase 4 relevance | Claim maturity after Phase 4 |
|---|---|---|
| `C0 — public-data reliability spine` | Consumes and preserves source/split/prediction/calibration/threshold lineage from Phases 0–3. | Strengthened only if upstream records remain validated and matched; otherwise diagnostic-only. |
| `C1 — IHARQ and RegimeRisk reliability control` | Directly implements the IHARQ-lite portion of C1 and prepares a regime-unaware baseline for Phase 5. | IHARQ-lite evidence may become conditionally thesis-supporting; RegimeRisk portion remains incomplete until Phase 5. |
| `C2 — adaptive readiness policy` | Provides decision traces, rule-derived evidence-quality context, action labels/costs, fallback/unsafe/uncertain flags, and matched keys for Phase 6/7. | Prepared only; no adaptive or learned-policy claim. |
| `C3 — contextual bandit / RL stretch` | Preserves action, reward-proxy, cost, and trace lineage needed later by bandit/RL phases. | Prepared only; no bandit/RL claim. |
| `C4 — dashboard / embodiment / final thesis integration` | Supplies source records, warnings, metrics, lineage, and limitation tags for Layer 10 and final integration. | Dashboard/export/embodiment/final-thesis claims remain downstream and conditional. |

Phase 4 improves thesis validity only when the IHARQ-lite behavior is compared fairly against A0–A4 under matched keys and when negative/null results are preserved. It does not require A5 to outperform every baseline. A simpler baseline sufficiency finding is still thesis-useful if documented through `NegativeResultNote`, limitation tags, and matched metric definitions. [EVAL: A5 baseline sufficiency]

### 3. Architecture-grounded phase objective and active layers/modules

#### 3.1 Objective

Phase 4 creates the interpretable IHARQ-lite evidence-verification baseline. Its objective is to convert validated, saved upstream evidence into deterministic, reason-coded readiness actions and comparison-ready A5 artifacts while preserving exact lineage, matched-comparison keys, metric definitions, limitation tags, negative results, and diagnostic-only downgrades. [ARCH: Layer 4 / decision control] [EXEC: Phase 4 objective] [EVAL: A5 identity]

[DERIVED from ARCH+EXEC+EVAL] The operational objective can be expressed as:

1. **verify input legality** before any decision row exists;
2. **build evidence features** only from legal decision-time records;
3. **apply deterministic IHARQ-lite logic** using canonical action tokens;
4. **log traceable decisions and local ablations** without altering upstream records;
5. **compare A5 against A0–A4** only under matched, leakage-safe keys;
6. **handoff source bundles** to Layer 10 and claim-safety summaries to Layer 0.

This objective intentionally controls the deeper bottleneck of forced acceptance under incomplete evidence: a prediction may be confident but wrong, calibrated but unstable, spatially fragile, contradictory across model families, or too weak/unsafe in a computational proxy sense to accept. [ARCH: Layer 4 / forced acceptance bottleneck]

#### 3.2 Active layer participation

| Layer | Phase 4 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews/receives claim-boundary evidence, limitation tags, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result notes, and forbidden-claim blocks. | Does not produce empirical A5 results and does not approve stronger claims inside Phase 4. |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Provides immutable dataset/window/split/preprocessing/label/artifact/source lineage. | Phase 4 reads and validates references only; no public-data mutation. |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Provides prediction/model/raw baseline evidence and A4 ordinary-control evidence where available. | Phase 4 does not train, tune, or repair decoders or ordinary controls. |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Provides immediate calibrated confidence, uncertainty, selective-prediction, threshold, reliability, leakage, and operating-point evidence. | Phase 4 does not recalibrate, recompute uncertainty, or retune thresholds. |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Primary producing layer for deterministic IHARQ-lite decisions, traces, and A5 source artifacts. | Must remain non-learned, traceable, reason-coded, and deterministic in core Phase 4. |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Immediate downstream phase and later optional/bounded context for regime-aware IHARQ. | Not active as a core Phase 4 producer; core A5 has `regime_aware=false` unless a later versioned analysis has valid Phase 5 records. |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Later consumer of IHARQ decisions, rule-derived evidence-quality context, action costs, and labels. | Phase 4 does not learn policies or produce learned evidence-quality-estimator outputs. |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Later consumer of action/cost/fallback/unsafe behavior. | Phase 4 does not create transitions, rewards, or closed-loop results. |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite Stress Generator | Later optional stress consumer/context. | Phase 4 does not create stress profiles or stress-test results. |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim Embodiment Demo | Later proxy/embodiment consumer through simulation/policy records. | Phase 4 does not validate embodiment or real muscle control. |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility | Reads Phase 4 source records and renders dashboard/card/export/reproducibility artifacts later. | Phase 4 hands off source bundles; Layer 10 rendering is not Phase 4 evidence production. |

### 4. Input contract

#### 4.1 Required input records and artifacts

| Input family | Required records/artifacts | Required Phase 4 use |
|---|---|---|
| Source/protocol identity | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `ArtifactFlagRecord` where available | Provides public-data, split, window/trial, preprocessing, label-map, artifact, and limitation lineage for every decision and comparison row. |
| Decoder evidence | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, `SubjectProfileRecord`, `FailureCaseIndex`, `Layer2ReadinessReport` where available | Provides raw decoder outputs, model provenance, A0 evidence, low-calibration/failure context, and model-family identity. |
| A4 ordinary-control evidence | `EnsembleControlRecord` or ordinary-control summaries where available | Provides matched longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls; never treated as IHARQ. |
| Calibration and uncertainty evidence | `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `ReliabilityAuditReport`, `SplitIntegrityReport`, `LeakageWarningRecord`, `CalibrationEligibilityTable`, `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` where applicable | Provides calibrated probabilities, uncertainty/selective evidence, thresholds, leakage status, reliability warnings, and matched operating points. `HighConfidenceWrongTable` remains diagnostic/evaluation-only. |
| Metric and evaluation definitions | `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary`, comparator IDs, matched-comparison key schema or envelope, prior `NegativeResultNote` / `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` references | Ensures A5 comparisons and metric outputs are interpretable, reproducible, and claim-bounded. |
| Claim/dashboard foundations | Claim limitation tags, claim-evidence matrix/manifest references where available, Layer 10 source/export manifest conventions where available | Ensures outputs carry claim and dashboard readiness boundaries without final card rendering. |

#### 4.2 Conditional or helper inputs

| Conditional input | Status | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| `WindowHistoryRecord` or equivalent window-history helper view | Local/precomputed helper view unless registry later promotes it | Use for stability only with source lineage; otherwise log missing/degraded stability evidence. |
| `ChannelSubsetStabilityRecord` or equivalent channel helper view | Local/precomputed helper view unless registry later promotes it | Use for spatial robustness only with source lineage; otherwise log missing/degraded channel-subset evidence. |
| `ModelAgreementRecord` or equivalent agreement helper view | Local/precomputed helper view unless registry later promotes it | Use for model-family agreement only with source model/class-order lineage; otherwise log unavailable agreement evidence. |
| Fallback route/config | Conditional | Required before producing `FallbackDecisionRecord` or claiming fallback behavior. |
| Combination eligibility/config | Conditional | Required before producing `CombinedEvidenceRecord` or claiming combine behavior. |
| Unsafe/proxy block criteria | Conditional | Required before producing `UnsafeEventRecord` or claiming unsafe/proxy block behavior. |
| Phase 5 `RegimeStateRecord` or `TrustStateRecord` | Not core Phase 4 | If absent, core Phase 4 must mark `regime_aware=false`; any regime-aware analysis is deferred/versioned after Phase 5. |
| Simulation, stress, embodiment, reward, or policy context | Downstream-only | Not ordinary Phase 4 input; may appear only in later explicitly labeled simulation/stress/embodiment contexts. |

#### 4.3 Explicitly forbidden ordinary decision-time inputs

Phase 4 ordinary IHARQ-lite decisions must not use:

- true labels, future correctness, future windows, future outcomes, simulated reward, embodiment outcome, or downstream policy outcome as decision-time evidence; [EXEC: Phase 4 leakage constraints]
- final test labels for threshold selection, rule tuning, evidence-request tuning, fallback tuning, unsafe-trigger tuning, or local sub-ablation optimization; [EVAL: A5 split/leakage constraints]
- Layer 10 dashboard summaries, thesis draft text, plotted figures, or reviewer-desired claim wording as input to decision logic; [ARCH: Layer 10 read-only boundary]
- Layer 0 claim approval or claim wording as empirical evidence; [ARCH: Layer 0 boundary]
- learned evidence-quality-estimator predictions from Phase 6 as if they were Phase 4 core IHARQ-lite evidence; [EVAL: A6 boundary]
- RegimeRisk outputs as core Phase 4 evidence when Phase 5 has not yet produced valid records; [EXEC: Phase 4 before Phase 5]
- hidden notebooks, manual labels, untracked thresholds, unregistered rule changes, or undocumented preprocessing variants. [FRAMEWORK: reproducibility / no hidden state]

#### 4.4 Required matching-key envelope

Every Phase 4 decision/comparison row must carry a `matched_comparison_key` or equivalent key envelope sufficient to reproduce matching. At minimum, the key envelope must include the following where available/applicable, and must explicitly declare missingness where public datasets do not provide a field:

| Key family | Required fields or checks |
|---|---|
| Public-data identity | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `run_id` where available, `trial_id` or trial-level source reference where available, `window_id` or horizon identifier where available, source-record IDs, declared missingness. |
| Split and budget legality | `split_id`, `split_role`, `label_budget_id`, calibration/threshold/test separation, leakage-warning status. |
| Preprocessing and labels | preprocessing ID/hash, label-map version, class order, artifact/source flags where available. |
| Model/decoder identity | `model_id`, `decoder_id`, `model_family`, score type, seed, model/config hash. |
| Calibration/threshold lineage | `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, selected-on split, allowed consumer, operating point ID. |
| Uncertainty/selective lineage | `uncertainty_id`, `selective_prediction_id`, coverage/rejection/cost denominator. |
| Ordinary-control/A4 lineage | aggregation rule, aggregation unit, source window universe, number of windows/members, voting/averaging/probability-average rule, delay/evidence burden, class-order mapping. |
| A5 decision lineage | `iharq_decision_id`, `iharq_trace_id`, canonical action token, reason code, rule path, config hash, evidence/action budget. |
| Metric and claim lineage | `metric_dictionary_id`, `negative_result_note_id` where applicable, `diagnostic_only_flag`, claim-boundary tags, dashboard/export ID where rendered later. |

Decide BPCR and exit status | Close Phase 4 without retroactively editing accepted predecessors. | Gate results; validation overlays; open issues; source-conflict findings; handoff package. | If a real source-grounded predecessor issue is discovered, emit a BPCR. Otherwise finalize Phase 4 with validation status, downstream handoff, unresolved issues, diagnostic outputs, and definition-of-done status. | BPCRs are used only for grounded prior-phase problems. Without such a problem, current BPCR status remains none; unresolved future-document details are carried as open issues instead. | [FRAMEWORK: BPCR handling] [EXEC: Phase 4 handoff] |

Append/version only; must identify route, reason, availability, cost, compatibility, and evaluation result where applicable. Proxy fallback only. |

Must include trigger, blocked action, evidence state, recommended conservative outcome, and non-clinical limitation labels. Not a real patient-safety record. |

#### 6.2 Minimum `IHARQDecisionRecord` field envelope

Phase 4 must require at least the following field families on every `IHARQDecisionRecord`; exact schema syntax remains controlled by the registry and later implementation specifications.

| Field family | Minimum required content |
|---|---|
| Record identity | `iharq_decision_id`, `record_id` if separate, `schema_version`, `producer_layer=Layer 4`, `producer_module`, `phase_id=Phase 4`, `created_timestamp`, `validation_status`. |
| Source identity | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `run_id` where available, `trial_id` or trial-level source reference where available, `window_id` / horizon ID where available, source-record IDs. |
| Split/protocol identity | `split_id`, `split_role`, `label_budget_id`, preprocessing ID/hash, label-map version, artifact/source flags where available. |
| Model/calibration identity | `model_id`, `decoder_id`, `model_family`, `score_type`, class order, `calibration_id`, `uncertainty_id`, `threshold_registry_id` where applicable. |
| Decision fields | `predicted_class`, `accepted_class_if_any`, canonical `action`, `reason_code`, `reason_text`, `rule_path`, fallback/unsafe/uncertain flags, evidence-request count, combined-window count, action/evidence/delay cost. |
| Evidence fields | confidence, entropy, margin, calibrated top-1 probability where available, window stability score, channel stability score, model agreement score, signal-quality flag, degraded-evidence flags, regime-aware flag. |
| Evaluation/comparison fields | `global_ablation_id=A5`, optional local sub-ablation label, `system_variant_id`, `matched_comparison_key`, comparator IDs, `metric_dictionary_id`, `negative_result_note_id` where applicable. |
| Claim/dashboard/reproducibility fields | limitation tags, `diagnostic_only_flag`, claim boundary, dashboard/export source reference where rendered later, configuration hash, deterministic seed if applicable, manifest ID. |

#### 6.3 Outputs explicitly not produced by Phase 4

Phase 4 does not produce:

- new `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, or `ArtifactFlagRecord` source records;
- new decoder models, `PredictionRecord` outputs, model-training artifacts, or repaired `ModelRegistryRecord` entries;
- new fitted `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, or test-tuned `ThresholdRegistryRecord` rows;
- core `RegimeStateRecord` or `TrustStateRecord` outputs;
- learned Phase 6 evidence-quality-estimator outputs, learned Adaptive-IHARQ outputs, learning-to-defer outputs, contextual-bandit/RL policies, `PolicyUpdateTrace`, or reward/transition records;
- StressForge-Lite stress profiles or stress-test results;
- MyoSuite/OpenSim embodiment outcomes or real muscle-stimulation control evidence;
- final Layer 10 rendered `CardRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, final figure/table placements, or final thesis export package;
- final Layer 0 claim approval or final paper/thesis claims.

### 8. Validation gates and exit criteria

#### Gate 4.1 — Upstream input completeness

Required records from Phases 0–3 must exist or be explicitly marked unavailable with declared missingness and downgrade status. Missing required prediction/source/split identity blocks affected rows. [EXEC: Phase 4 input gates]

#### Gate 4.2 — Split, leakage, and decision-time legality

All calibration, threshold, selective-prediction, and IHARQ rule inputs must respect split roles. Test labels/future correctness/rewards/outcomes may not enter ordinary decision-time logic. Leakage or test-tuned thresholds block thesis-ready A5 claims and may invalidate affected runs. [EVAL: A5 split constraints]

#### Gate 4.3 — Threshold and operating-point registration

Any threshold-dependent rule or comparison must reference a valid `ThresholdRegistryRecord` and, where relevant, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` entry with selected-on split, allowed consumer, coverage/cost context, leakage status, and operating-point ID. [REG: ThresholdRegistryRecord] [PRIOR: Phase 3 handoff]

#### Gate 4.4 — Canonical action-token validation

Every stored action token must be one of `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, or `unsafe`. Invalid aliases require rerun/repair before validation or diagnostic-only rejection; silent normalization after evidence generation is not allowed. [ARCH: Layer 4 action vocabulary]

#### Gate 4.5 — Deterministic non-learned IHARQ-lite boundary

Core Phase 4 must be deterministic, reason-coded, and non-learned. Learned estimator outputs, policy updates, bandit/RL choices, simulation rewards, and RegimeRisk-aware logic cannot be credited as core Phase 4 results. [EXEC: Phase 4 scope]

#### Gate 4.6 — Trace and reason-code completeness

Every valid decision must have `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, reason code, reason text, rule path, feature/source lineage, config hash, and diagnostic status. Missing reason/trace blocks interpretable IHARQ claims. [REG: IHARQTraceRecord]

#### Gate 4.7 — Matched-comparison eligibility

A5 rows can be compared to A0–A4 only when matched keys pass for dataset/split/window/model/calibration/threshold/uncertainty/ordinary-control/action-cost/metric lineage. Unmatched rows remain visible as diagnostic-only. [EVAL: A5 matched-comparison]

#### Gate 4.8 — Metric dictionary coverage

Every reported metric family or metric value must have `MetricDictionaryEntry` support or be explicitly marked diagnostic-only/requires-confirmation. Final formulas/statistical tests remain deferred unless fixed by the protocol/metric dictionary. [REG: MetricDictionaryEntry] [EVAL: v0.1 boundary]

#### Gate 4.9 — Negative-result preservation

If a simpler baseline/control is sufficient or if A5 imposes excessive cost, fallback, delay, coverage collapse, or no combine advantage, a `NegativeResultNote` must be generated and linked. Missing negative-result notes block claim integration. [EVAL: A5 negative-result handling]

#### Gate 4.10 — Layer 10 audit/export readiness

Layer 10 source bundle must include source IDs, validation statuses, metric references, matched keys, diagnostic flags, negative notes, warning candidates, configs, seeds where applicable, and manifest references. Layer 10 must be able to audit without rerunning decisions. [ARCH: Layer 10]

#### Gate 4.11 — Layer 0 claim-safety readiness

Every output must carry limitation tags and forbidden-claim boundaries. Claim-evidence summaries must separate allowed computational/proxy claims from forbidden clinical/deployment/real-control claims. [ARCH: Layer 0]

#### Phase 4 exit criteria

Phase 4 reaches `conditional_pass_pending_actual_execution_records` in this playbook when:

1. the input manifest and immutable upstream lineage are defined;
2. input legality, split/leakage, threshold registration, action-token, trace, matched-key, metric, negative-result, Layer 10, and Layer 0 gates are defined;
3. output record families and lifecycle/versioning rules are specified;
4. A5 is directly enabled and A6/A7–A13 are preparation-only;
5. open issues and deferred items are explicitly carried;
6. the machine-readable handoff block is complete.

Actual Phase 4 execution reaches thesis-ready status only after real records pass these gates. [EXEC: Phase 4 definition of done]

### 9. Matched-comparison preservation requirements

#### 9.1 Comparators consumed or preserved

| Comparator | Phase 4 treatment | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A0 raw decoder / accept-all reference | Compare A5 against raw prediction acceptance using matched source/prediction/model/split/window keys. | Missing prediction/source identity, model lineage, or class-order compatibility. |
| A1 calibrated decoder | Compare against calibrated decoder evidence under matched calibration lineage and split legality. | Missing calibration ID, invalid calibration, or calibration/test leakage. |
| A2 simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Compare against registered threshold baseline with same threshold selection legality, coverage/cost context, and operating point. | Missing/invalid threshold registry, test-tuned threshold, or unmatched cost/coverage. |
| A3 uncertainty and selective prediction | Compare against uncertainty/selective-prediction behavior using same uncertainty features, selective policy, coverage, and source rows. | Missing uncertainty/selective lineage or conflation with A2 thresholding/A4 controls. |
| A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Compare against ordinary aggregation/ensemble controls with same source window universe, aggregation rule, class order, delay/evidence cost, and model-family compatibility. | Missing `EnsembleControlRecord`/ordinary-control lineage, hidden delay, or incompatible aggregation universe. |
| Fallback-only baseline | Compare when fallback route/config exists and eligible cases are matched. | Missing fallback availability/cost or incomparable eligible-case universe. |
| Local A5 sub-ablations | Compare full A5 against source-supported local module removals or simplified rules. | Missing helper views, source lineage, metric definitions, or local configuration trace. |
| Oracle/headroom diagnostic | May use labels/future outcomes only after decision-time separation. | Any use as ordinary decision-time evidence invalidates run; otherwise diagnostic-only. |

#### 9.2 Preservation rules

- Preserve comparator identity; do not collapse A2, A3, and A4 into one threshold/uncertainty/ensemble bucket. [EVAL: corrected A2/A3/A4 identities]
- Preserve coverage, request budget, action cost, delay/evidence burden, fallback burden, and unsafe/uncertain frequency alongside accuracy-like metrics. [EVAL: A5 metric families]
- Preserve unmatched and missing comparator cells explicitly; do not impute or hide missing baselines. [EVAL: matched-comparison pass/fail rule]
- Preserve negative/null results and baseline sufficiency with `NegativeResultNote`. [EVAL: negative-result handling]
- Preserve upstream diagnostic-only flags; Phase 4 cannot upgrade a diagnostic upstream comparison into a thesis-ready A5 claim. [REG: DiagnosticOnlyFlag]

### 10. Ablation and evaluation obligations

#### 10.1 Directly produced or enabled

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 4 obligation |
|---|---|---|
| A5 | IHARQ-lite / rule-based evidence verification | Directly enabled by Phase 4. Produce A5-ready `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, `IHARQAblationRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, matched-comparison material, metric references, negative-result notes, and diagnostic flags. |

#### 10.2 Consumed or preserved comparators

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 4 use |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder baseline | Raw accept-all comparator. |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder baseline | Calibrated-confidence comparator and input context. |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Threshold/coverage/cost comparator. |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Uncertainty/selective comparator and input context. |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Ordinary aggregation/ensemble comparator, not IHARQ. |

#### 10.3 Prepared but not completed

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 4 boundary |
|---|---|---|
| A6 | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Prepared by source IHARQ decisions, traces, and rule-derived compatibility records; learned estimator outputs are Phase 6. |
| A7 | IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Prepared by core regime-unaware A5 decisions and histories; RegimeRisk evidence is Phase 5. |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer | Prepared through action/cost/uncertain/fallback labels; learning-to-defer is downstream. |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Prepared through traces and possible pseudo-label context; supervised adaptive outputs are Phase 6. |
| A10 | Contextual bandit | Prepared through action/cost/reward-proxy lineage; no bandit policy in Phase 4. |
| A11 | RL policy | Prepared through action/cost state labels; no RL policy in Phase 4. |
| A12 | Stress tests | Prepared through source lineage and limitation tags; no stress results in Phase 4. |
| A13 | MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demonstration | Prepared through later gating/action lineage; no embodiment evidence in Phase 4. |

Phase 4 must not introduce `A14` or new global ablation IDs. [EVAL: A0–A13 official ladder]

#### 10.4 Local A5 sub-ablation policy

The evaluation protocol allows local A5 children only as local labels, not new global ablations. Where source-supported and matched, Phase 4 may prepare:

| Local A5 label | Purpose | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `A5.local.confidence_only` | Tests confidence-only IHARQ-like rule path. | Local A5 child; metric dictionary/matched keys required. |
| `A5.local.entropy_only` | Tests entropy-only rejection/rule path. | Local A5 child; not A3 replacement. |
| `A5.local.margin_only` | Tests margin-only rule path. | Local A5 child; matched source rows required. |
| `A5.local.no_stability` | Removes window-stability checker. | Diagnostic-only if window-history helper view unavailable. |
| `A5.local.no_combination` | Disables `combine_evidence` behavior. | No combine claim if combination record missing. |
| `A5.local.no_fallback` | Removes fallback router. | Does not imply real safety fallback. |
| `A5.local.no_unsafe` | Removes unsafe-state monitor. | Unsafe remains proxy/non-clinical. |
| `A5.local.fallback_only` | Tests conservative fallback-only behavior. | Must report coverage/cost collapse if present. |
| `A5.local.no_channel_subset` | Disables channel-subset checker. | Requires helper-view availability or diagnostic-only status. |
| `A5.local.no_model_agreement` | Disables model-family agreement checker. | Requires model-family alternatives and class-order compatibility. |
| `A5.local.regime_unaware` | Marks core Phase 4 without Phase 5 temporal trust. | Used as baseline for later A7; no RegimeRisk claim. |

Exact numeric local labels such as A5.1/A5.2 remain `requires_confirmation` unless a later official source fixes them. [EVAL: A5 local sub-ablation policy]

#### 10.5 Metric families to prepare for Layer 10

Phase 4 must prepare metric dictionary support and evaluation rows for applicable A5 metric families:

- accepted-decision accuracy/reliability where applicable;
- wrong-accept proxy rate / unsafe-accept proxy;
- coverage / accepted fraction;
- request rate and evidence-request burden;
- combine rate and combine success/failure;
- fallback rate, fallback burden, and fallback correctness where evaluable;
- unsafe/proxy block rate;
- uncertain rate;
- action cost, evidence cost, and delay cost;
- reason-code distribution;
- trace completeness and source-lineage completeness;
- matched deltas against A0–A4;
- high-confidence-wrong diagnostic relation, evaluation-only;
- degraded-evidence / helper-missingness frequency.

No clinical, real-safety, medical-device, rehabilitation, real muscle-stimulation, or real-world deployment metric may be introduced. [EVAL: A5 metric families] [ARCH: Layer 0]

### 11. Dashboard, card, reproducibility, and export obligations

#### 11.1 Layer 10 dashboard visibility

Phase 4 must hand off dashboard-readable source material for:

- IHARQ action distributions by canonical token;
- reason-code distributions and rule-path summaries;
- accepted/wrong-accept proxy summaries where matched and metric-defined;
- request/combine/fallback/uncertain/unsafe rates and costs;
- trace-completeness and source-lineage completeness;
- A5 versus A0–A4 matched comparison summaries;
- local A5 sub-ablation summaries where source-supported;
- diagnostic-only, leakage, invalid-token, missing-metric, missing-key, and negative-result counts;
- limitation tags and forbidden-claim warning surfaces.

Layer 10 must render from saved source records and must not recompute IHARQ decisions, retune thresholds, modify action tokens, infer missing reason codes, hide negative results, or repair leakage. [ARCH: Layer 10]

#### 11.2 Card-source bundle

Phase 4 prepares the source material for later IHARQ reliability cards. The bundle must include:

| Card-source need | Phase 4 source material |
|---|---|
| Reliability claim context | Matched A5 metrics, limitation tags, diagnostic flags, metric dictionary references. |
| Behavior traceability | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, reason-code and rule-path summaries. |
| Request/combine/fallback/unsafe visibility | `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, `UnsafeEventRecord` where active. |
| Baseline honesty | A0–A4 matched comparator summaries and `NegativeResultNote` entries. |
| Warning banners | Missing source lineage, invalid action tokens, missing metric dictionary, unmatched comparisons, proxy-only and non-clinical labels. |
| Reproducibility | Source manifests, config hashes, seeds where applicable, schema versions, validation statuses, export source IDs. |

Rendered cards remain Layer 10 derived outputs. [REG: card/dashboard boundary] [ARCH: Layer 10]

#### 11.3 Reproducibility and export readiness

Phase 4 must provide:

- source input manifest and output manifest;
- schema versions, producer modules/layers, config hashes, deterministic seeds where applicable;
- action-token vocabulary validation results;
- threshold and operating-point registration references;
- matched-comparison key definitions and pass/fail status;
- metric dictionary references;
- diagnostic-only flags and negative-result notes;
- open issue references and deferred item notes;
- Layer 0 limitation tags and claim-boundary labels.

Exact repository paths, dashboard routes, static figure/table IDs, CLI commands, and final thesis export names remain deferred unless supplied by future Implementation Build Book / Layer 10 specifications. [FRAMEWORK: implementation non-interference]
