### 12. Claim-safety and limitation boundaries

#### 12.1 Allowed claim level after Phase 4

If all gates pass, Phase 4 may support a bounded claim of the following kind:

> Phase 4 evaluates deterministic, rule-based IHARQ-lite evidence verification under public-data/offline/proxy Stretch C constraints and compares it against matched A0–A4 baselines using traceable records, metric definitions, negative-result handling, and diagnostic-only flags.

Allowed claims remain computational/proxy and matched-comparison-bound. They may discuss evidence-verification behavior, accepted-decision reliability under matched metrics, wrong-accept proxy reduction under matched metrics, request/combine/fallback/uncertain/unsafe proxy behavior, reason-coded interpretability, trace completeness, and baseline sufficiency. [ARCH: Layer 0] [EVAL: A5 claim boundary]

#### 12.2 Forbidden overclaims

Phase 4 must not claim or imply:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle-stimulation control;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real-time online BCI deployment reliability;
- clinical fatigue or neurological-state diagnosis;
- causal superiority outside matched comparisons;
- generalized robustness beyond source datasets/splits/models;
- completion of A6 learned evidence-quality estimation;
- completion of RegimeRisk-aware IHARQ/A7;
- completion of adaptive, learning-to-defer, bandit, RL, stress, simulation, embodiment, dashboard, or final-thesis integration phases.

#### 12.3 Required limitation labels

Phase 4 outputs and claim-evidence summaries must carry relevant labels, including:

```text
public_eeg_only
proxy_readiness
computational_evidence_verification
evaluation_only
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
diagnostic_only where matching/lineage/metric completeness fails
simulation_only where later simulation records are used
stress_conditioned where later stress records are used
embodiment_proxy_only where later embodiment records are used
```

#### 12.4 Diagnostic-only claim triggers

Layer 0 must downgrade or block claims when there is missing source lineage, missing matched keys, missing metric definitions, leakage, test-tuned thresholds, invalid action tokens, missing reason codes/traces, missing negative-result notes, unseparated `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants, RegimeRisk contamination of core Phase 4, forbidden clinical/deployment wording, or unsupported extrapolation beyond public-data/proxy conditions. [REG: DiagnosticOnlyFlag] [ARCH: Layer 0]

#### 12.5 Evidence required before stronger claims

Stronger claims require later evidence:

- A7 / RegimeRisk claims require valid Phase 5 records and matched regime-aware comparisons;
- A6/A9 learned evidence-quality/adaptive claims require valid Phase 6 outputs and producer/variant separation;
- learning-to-defer, bandit, RL claims require their downstream phases and update/frozen-evaluation separation;
- stress claims require Phase 8/12 stress evidence with clean/stressed lineage;
- embodiment claims require Phase 9/13 static-replay/proxy evidence with embodiment limitation tags;
- dashboard/export/final-thesis claims require Layer 10 and Phase 14/15 completion plus Layer 0 review.

---

### 13. Failure, missingness, diagnostic-only handling, and BPCR behavior

#### 13.1 Phase 4 failure modes

| Failure mode | Required response | Claim effect |
|---|---|---|
| Missing/invalid `PredictionRecord` | Block affected A5 decision row. | No A5 result for affected case. |
| Missing `ModelRegistryRecord`, class order, or score type | Block or mark comparison diagnostic-only. | No fair model/comparator claim. |
| Missing calibrated probabilities in calibrated mode | Use declared uncalibrated fallback only if configured; otherwise block calibrated A5 claim. | Calibrated IHARQ claim blocked. |
| Missing uncertainty/selective records where used | Disable/downgrade corresponding rule and record missingness. | No uncertainty/selective A5 claim. |
| Missing/invalid `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Block threshold-dependent rule/comparison. | No A2/threshold comparison claim. |
| Split leakage or test-tuned thresholds | Reject run or diagnostic-only. | No thesis-ready claim. |
| Evaluation-only labels/future outcomes used in decision | Reject ordinary run; allow only separated oracle diagnostic. | Ordinary A5 invalid. |
| Invalid stored action token | Reject record or rerun before validation. | No valid A5 decision. |
| Stored `combine` instead of `combine_evidence` | Alias violation; repair through rerun/validation before acceptance or reject. | No silent normalization. |
| Missing reason code/rule path | Block or diagnostic-only. | No interpretable IHARQ claim. |
| Missing `IHARQTraceRecord` | Block or diagnostic-only. | No reproducible A5 claim. |
| Missing matched-comparison key | Diagnostic-only. | No comparative improvement claim. |
| Missing `MetricDictionaryEntry` | Diagnostic-only. | No metric-based claim. |
| Missing `NegativeResultNote` where required | Block claim integration. | Cherry-picking risk. |
| Missing behavior-specific logs for active combine/fallback/unsafe behavior | Block behavior-specific claim. | No combine/fallback/unsafe claim. |
| Unseparated Phase 4 vs Phase 6 `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants | Diagnostic-only for A6/quality comparisons. | Learned-quality claim blocked. |
| RegimeRisk absent but regime-aware claim attempted | Block/defer A7 claim. | Core A5 remains regime-unaware. |
| Forbidden clinical/deployment/safety wording | Layer 0 block. | No public claim until corrected. |

#### 13.2 Diagnostic-only downgrade behavior

Diagnostic-only records are not deleted. They must remain visible with reason, source IDs, affected rows/metrics/claims, and downstream limitation effects. Diagnostic-only status is required for unmatched comparisons, incomplete metric definitions, source-missing helper evidence, unresolved schema maturity, public-dataset missingness that affects matching, and any downstream-only context used before its producing phase exists. [FRAMEWORK: diagnostic-only discipline] [REG: DiagnosticOnlyFlag]

#### 13.3 Back-Propagation Correction Request handling

If Phase 4 discovers that a previous accepted phase is incomplete, inconsistent, or insufficient in a way that affects current validity, it must emit a Back-Propagation Correction Request instead of editing previous phase text. The required structure is:

```yaml
back_propagation_request:
  request_id: "BPCR-Phase4-<sequence>"
  discovered_in_phase: "Phase 4"
  affected_prior_phase: "Phase <0|1|2|3>"
  affected_artifact_or_record: "<canonical record/artifact>"
  issue_type: "<schema_conflict|missing_required_input|lineage_gap|split_leakage|metric_gap|claim_boundary_gap|other>"
  severity: "<low|medium|high|blocking>"
  source_conflict: "<source anchors and contradiction/gap>"
  downstream_risk: "<effect on Phase 4 and later phases>"
  required_action: "<non-destructive correction required>"
  whether_current_phase_can_continue: "<yes|yes_diagnostic_only|no>"
  diagnostic_only_effect: "<affected outputs/claims>"
  claim_safety_effect: "<affected claim boundary>"
```

#### 13.4 Current BPCR status

No BPCR is emitted by this generated playbook section because no grounded contradiction requiring retroactive correction was found in the accepted Phase 0–3 predecessor text. The real Phase 4 execution must emit BPCRs if actual upstream records, schemas, matched keys, or diagnostic flags contradict the Phase 4 requirements. [FRAMEWORK: BPCR audit]

### 14. Repository, storage, and reproducibility expectations

Phase 4 storage expectations are conceptual because exact repository paths, package layout, class names, CLI commands, dashboard routes, and storage homes are deferred to the future Implementation Build Book / Layer 10 specifications. [FRAMEWORK: implementation non-interference]

#### 14.1 Conceptual storage groups

| Storage group | Contents | Required invariant |
|---|---|---|
| Input manifests | References to immutable Phase 0–3 source records. | Must contain source IDs, schema versions, validation status, config hashes, and limitation tags. |
| Decision records | `IHARQDecisionRecord` and `IHARQTraceRecord`. | Must be reproducible from saved inputs and declared configuration. |
| Behavior records | `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, `UnsafeEventRecord` where active. | Must preserve behavior-specific source lineage and cost/trigger fields. |
| Evaluation records | `IHARQAblationRecord`, `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric references. | Must preserve matched keys and diagnostic/negative-result status. |
| Claim/governance artifacts | `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, limitation tags, claim-evidence summary. | Must propagate to Layer 0 and Layer 10. |
| Dashboard/export source bundle | Source records and manifest material for Layer 10. | Must be read-only source for later rendering/export. |

#### 14.2 Reproducibility invariants

- Every output has a producer layer/module, phase ID, schema version, validation status, source-record IDs, config hash, and limitation tags.
- Every decision has canonical action token, reason code, rule path, trace, and matched key.
- Every metric has a metric dictionary reference or diagnostic-only status.
- Every comparator row has a matchability status.
- Every negative/null/baseline-sufficiency result remains linked.
- Every derived output can be regenerated from immutable upstream records and declared Phase 4 configuration.
- Dashboard/card/figure/table outputs remain downstream derived products and cannot be used as primary evidence.

### 15. Phase handoff package

#### 15.1 Handoff to Phase 5

Phase 4 hands Phase 5 a regime-unaware IHARQ-lite baseline and decision history:

- validated `IHARQDecisionRecord` and `IHARQTraceRecord` rows;
- canonical action-token distributions and reason-code summaries;
- rule-derived evidence-quality context where produced, clearly separated from learned variants;
- fallback/unsafe/uncertain/combine/request/wait histories and costs;
- matched A5 versus A0–A4 comparison material;
- metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and limitation tags;
- explicit `regime_aware=false` status for core Phase 4;
- open issues relevant to temporal trust integration.

Phase 5 must not treat missing RegimeRisk in core Phase 4 as a Phase 4 defect. It is the expected ordering boundary. [EXEC: Phase 4 to Phase 5 handoff]

#### 15.2 Handoff to Phase 6 and later phases

Phase 4 provides downstream compatibility material:

| Downstream phase/context | Handoff material | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 6 / A6/A9 | IHARQ decisions, traces, rule-derived evidence-quality context, action labels/costs, source IDs, diagnostic flags. | Learned evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ outputs are Phase 6. |
| Phase 7 / A8 | Action tokens, wait/request/fallback/unsafe/uncertain behavior and costs. | Learning-to-defer and simulation outcomes are downstream. |
| Phase 8 / A12 | Clean source and IHARQ decision lineage for later stress conditioning. | No stress evidence in Phase 4. |
| Phase 9 / A13 | Proxy action/gating lineage for later static-replay/embodiment context. | No embodiment validation or real muscle-control claim. |
| Phases 10–13 / A10–A13 | Decision/action/cost/reward-proxy compatibility where later phases define it. | No bandit/RL/stress/embodiment completion in Phase 4. |
| Phase 14 / Layer 10 | Dashboard/source bundle, metric references, matched reports, warnings, reproducibility material. | Final cards/views/exports are Layer 10 outputs. |
| Phase 15 / final thesis | Claim-bounded evidence packages, limitation tags, negative results, and diagnostic-only status. | Final thesis claims require final integration and Layer 0 review. |

#### 15.3 Handoff integrity status

`conditional_pass_pending_actual_execution_records`. The playbook defines all required records, gates, outputs, and boundaries; actual handoff integrity depends on real Phase 4 execution passing validation. [EXEC: Phase 4 definition of done]

### 17. Definition of done

#### 17.1 Playbook-section definition of done

This generated Phase 4 playbook section is complete when:

- official phase identity and ordering are preserved;
- Source Extraction Digest covers architecture, registry, execution plan, evaluation protocol, and prior phases;
- active layers/modules, entry conditions, inputs, procedure, outputs, lifecycle, validation gates, evaluation obligations, matched keys, Layer 10 handoff, Layer 0 claim safety, failure modes, BPCR handling, and downstream handoff are specified;
- no canonical records, phases, modules, metrics, ablations, repository paths, or claims are invented;
- previous Phase 0–3 content is preserved exactly in the cumulative file;
- YAML handoff is complete and explicit about not-applicable/deferred fields.

#### 17.2 Actual Phase 4 execution definition of done

Actual execution of Phase 4 is complete only when:

1. upstream Phase 0–3 input manifest passes completeness and immutability checks;
2. split/leakage/decision-time legality gates pass or affected rows are downgraded;
3. canonical action-token validation passes;
4. every accepted decision has reason code, rule path, trace, source lineage, config hash, matched key, and diagnostic status;
5. behavior-specific records are present where behavior is active;
6. A5 versus A0–A4 matched comparisons are complete or diagnostic-only missingness is visible;
7. metrics have dictionary support or are diagnostic-only;
8. negative/null/baseline-sufficiency results are linked;
9. Layer 10 source bundle and Layer 0 claim-safety summary are complete;
10. open issues and BPCRs, if any, are documented;
11. downstream Phase 5 and Phase 6+ handoffs are usable without hidden state.

### 0A. Source Extraction Digest

**Architecture facts used**

- The official architecture uses `Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring` as the temporal trust layer for drift-risk, fatigue-like degradation, instability, dropout risk, changing reliability, model/source trust, and stop-loss warnings. It feeds bounded context into Layers 4 and 6 and read-only evidence into Layer 10. [ARCH: revised layer numbering / Layer 5]
- Layer 5 does not train decoders, calibrate probabilities, replace IHARQ decision rules, learn adaptive policy outputs, run stress protocols, execute embodied control, or render final dashboards. Its outputs must remain derived, traceable, causal, and proxy-bounded. [ARCH: Layer 5 scope and boundaries]
- Layer 5 primary output families are `RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, `regime_timelines.csv`, `trust_scores.csv`, and `stop_loss_warnings.csv`, with source-record provenance, configuration lineage, validation status, and claim-boundary tags. [ARCH: Layer 5 output contract]
- RegimeRisk-to-IHARQ feedback is allowed only as explicit, bounded, ablatable context such as threshold tightening, stricter evidence, trusted-set restriction, fallback/no-action/unsafe/cooldown/recovery recommendation, or stop-loss warning. It must not use future labels, future correctness, future rewards, future stress outcomes, or future embodiment outcomes as ordinary decision-time features. [ARCH: Layer 5 feedforward / loopback restrictions]
- Layer 10 is a read-only dashboard, card, audit, export, and reproducibility layer. It may render `RegimeCard` views and export Layer 5 evidence packages, but it cannot create primary RegimeRisk evidence, retune thresholds, repair missing source records, or convert diagnostic-only rows into claim-ready evidence. [ARCH: Layer 10 dashboard boundary]
- Layer 0 controls claim safety. Phase 5 evidence cannot justify clinical fatigue detection, neurological-state diagnosis, patient-risk monitoring, medical-device readiness, real assistive-control safety, real muscle-stimulation control, real rehabilitation efficacy, or real deployment readiness. [ARCH: Layer 0 claim-safety boundary]

**Registry facts used**

- `RegimeStateRecord` is the primary Layer 5 canonical/derived record family for regime label/probability, RegimeRisk score, risk trend, volatility-like and drawdown-like scores, drift/fatigue-like/dropout/failure-risk scores, trust summary, trusted set, optional `trust_state_record_ids`, stop-loss status, recommendation, reason codes, optional downstream context IDs, and provenance. [REG: RegimeStateRecord]
- `TrustStateRecord` is canonical/derived but conditional: it is required when trust allocation has an independent lifecycle, target identity, policy use, dashboard view, or thesis-facing trust timeline. Otherwise compact trust summaries may remain inside `RegimeStateRecord` without claiming an independent trust timeline. [REG: TrustStateRecord]
- `regime_timelines.csv`, `trust_scores.csv`, `stop_loss_warnings.csv`, Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `ClaimEvidenceManifest`/`ClaimEvidenceMatrix`, `RegimeCard lineage`, and `ReproducibilityManifest` are the relevant Layer 5/evaluation/dashboard/claim-governance artifact families. [REG: Layer 5 and evaluation/dashboard lineage artifacts]
- Required validation includes temporal ordering, causal cutoff legality, split isolation, finite scores, source-ID linkage, controlled-vocabulary fields, simulation/proxy tags where applicable, optional trust-state linkage, stop-loss trigger traceability, matched-comparison key preservation, metric-dictionary linkage, negative-result visibility, and claim-boundary tags. ### 3. Architecture-grounded phase objective and active layers/modules

#### 3.1 Objective

Phase 5 converts ordered, split-safe, causally available public-data/proxy histories into RegimeRisk temporal-trust evidence. Its objective is to test whether temporal operating-state context can identify unstable reliability periods, explain failure bursts, allocate trust across evidence sources, and conservatively recommend stricter evidence, fallback, no-action, unsafe mode, cooldown, or recovery monitoring under matched comparisons. [ARCH: Layer 5 problem solved] [EVAL: A7 purpose]

The phase addresses a specific bottleneck: confidence, calibration, uncertainty, selective prediction, and IHARQ-lite are local or static controls unless they are paired with causal temporal trust. Phase 5 adds temporal regime awareness without claiming clinical fatigue detection or real-world safety validation. [ARCH: Layer 5 thesis role]

#### 3.2 Active layer participation

| Layer | Phase 5 role | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, forbidden claims, negative-result visibility, and claim-evidence linkage. | Does not produce empirical RegimeRisk evidence. |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Supplies dataset/window/split/protocol/subject/session/temporal-order lineage. | Read-only source; Phase 5 cannot change splits or windows. |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Supplies prediction/model/baseline histories and subject-profile context where available. | Read-only source; Phase 5 cannot retrain or repair decoders. |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Supplies calibration, uncertainty, threshold, selective-prediction, and leakage-audit evidence. | Read-only source; no test-tuned or future correctness features. |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Supplies regime-unaware A5 decision histories and may later consume bounded regime-aware context in versioned reruns. | Phase 5 cannot overwrite Phase 4 core A5 rows. |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Primary producing layer for Phase 5 records, timelines, trust scores, stop-loss warnings, and evaluation artifacts. | Must remain causal, traceable, and proxy-bounded. |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Downstream consumer of RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss context in Phase 6+. | Phase 5 does not produce Phase 6 learned policy or A6/A9 outputs. |
| Layer 7–9 | Optional downstream simulation/stress/embodiment contexts where official later records exist. | Simulation/stress/embodiment contexts remain proxy-only and cannot be assumed present during core Phase 5. |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Reads, validates, renders, cards, exports, and packages saved Phase 5 source records. | Derived/read-only reporting; no hidden retuning or source mutation. |

#### 3.3 Primary and supporting modules

| Module/submodule | Status in Phase 5 | Required output or decision |
|---|---|---|
| Module E: Temporal regime and trust engine / RegimeRisk | Primary module | Drives Layer 5 execution and output lineage. |
| Temporal feature builder | Required | Causal rolling features from ordered histories with split/cutoff validation. |
| Volatility-like monitor | Required where feature support exists | Volatility scores/components/trends and reason codes. |
| Drawdown-like monitor | Required where feature support exists | Drawdown scores/durations/recovery indicators and reason codes. |
| Regime classifier | Required | `RegimeStateRecord` fields: regime label/probability/risk band/recommendation/reason codes. |
| Failure-risk predictor | Required when legal labels/outcomes exist for evaluation; otherwise diagnostic/proxy | Failure-risk score/bin and risk calibration diagnostics without decision-time leakage. |
| Trust allocator | Conditional | `TrustStateRecord` and `trust_scores.csv` when independent trust timelines are consumed or claimed. |

| Sequence-model regime estimator | Optional/future-work only | May appear only as versioned optional/diagnostic variant unless validated and source-supported. |

#### Step 1 — Freeze Phase 0–4 intake and create Phase 5 intake manifest

Read the accepted upstream handoff manifests and source-record inventories. Record source artifact hashes, schema versions, config hashes, seeds where applicable, validation statuses, and unresolved issue references. Treat all upstream records as immutable read-only inputs. [FRAME: immutable record discipline]

#### Step 2 — Validate temporal identity and split/cutoff legality

Construct the ordered sequence envelope using available `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, subject/session/run metadata, and Phase 4 decision lineage. Reject, block, or downgrade rows with missing temporal identity, ambiguous trial/window representation, forbidden split crossing, or non-causal feature access. [REG: temporal ordering / causal cutoff]

#### Step 3 — Canonicalize upstream feature sources without mutating them

Join `PredictionRecord`, `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `EvidenceQualityRecord`, and `IHARQDecisionRecord` by source IDs and matched keys. Preserve producer/phase tags and distinguish Phase 4 rule-derived evidence quality from later Phase 6 learned evidence quality. [REG: EvidenceQualityRecord boundary]

#### Step 4 — Audit Phase 4 action histories before RegimeRisk use

Verify canonical Layer 4 action tokens, action costs, reason codes, rule paths, `IHARQTraceRecord` links, fallback/unsafe/uncertain histories, A5 matched reports, negative-result notes, and `regime_aware=false` baseline status. Alias or trace gaps must downgrade affected A7 rows rather than being repaired silently. [PRIOR: Phase 4 handoff]

#### Step 5 — Build causal rolling temporal features

[DERIVED] Generate rolling short-, medium-, long-, and session-level temporal feature groups from legal current/past data only. Feature families may include confidence trends, uncertainty trends, calibration-error trends, agreement/disagreement trends, artifact/dropout proxies, evidence-quality trends, IHARQ action histories, request/fallback/unsafe burden, missingness, and recovery indicators. Mark every feature as label-free, label-based, proxy-based, simulation-derived, or evaluation-only. [ARCH: Layer 5 temporal feature builder]

#### Step 6 — Produce volatility-like and drawdown-like monitors

Compute volatility components and trends for confidence, entropy, margin, agreement, decision switching, missingness, and evidence stability where supported. Compute drawdown indicators for sustained degradation from a declared reference state and recovery rules. Save formula/config lineage and reason codes. [ARCH: volatility-like monitor / drawdown-like monitor]

#### Step 7 — Estimate operating regime and RegimeRisk fields

Use fixed, validation-safe, configuration-declared rule-based or source-supported learned logic, without treating this playbook as a final algorithm specification, to produce `regime_label`, `regime_probability` or confidence estimate, risk band, RegimeRisk score, risk trend, drift/fatigue-like/dropout/failure-risk components, recommendation, reason codes, and source-record provenance. [ARCH: regime classifier] [REG: RegimeStateRecord]

#### Step 8 — Produce failure-risk evaluation outputs without decision-time leakage

Where legal labels or outcomes exist, evaluate failure-risk score alignment against wrong accepts, error bursts, high-confidence wrong cases, fallback clusters, or simulated unsafe proxies. Ensure all label/outcome-dependent fields are evaluation-only unless legally past. If no legal targets exist, keep failure-risk evaluation diagnostic or proxy-only. [EVAL: A7 risk-error alignment]

#### Step 9 — Allocate trust and decide whether `TrustStateRecord` is required

If trust allocation is independently consumed, plotted, used by policy context, used by dashboard, or claimed as a separate timeline, produce `TrustStateRecord` and `trust_scores.csv` with source RegimeStateRecord IDs, trust target type/ID, trust score/trend/band, trusted-set membership, update source, decay/recovery state, reason codes, and provenance. If trust remains compact inside `RegimeStateRecord`, document that no independent trust timeline is claimed. [REG: TrustStateRecord]

#### Step 10 — Generate stop-loss warnings and conservative recommendations

When stop-loss logic is active, produce `stop_loss_warnings.csv` with status, trigger, severity, affected IDs, conservative recommendation, cooldown/recovery, timestamp or simulated step, simulation/proxy boundary label, and reason codes. Report over-abstention and false stop-loss burden rather than hiding it. [ARCH: stop-loss module]

#### Step 11 — Run A7 matched comparisons and negative controls

Evaluate A7 against matched A5 regime-unaware IHARQ-lite and relevant A0–A4 controls under identical ordered sequences, splits, decoder/calibration/threshold/IHARQ configurations, costs, budgets, and metric dictionaries. Include shuffled RegimeRisk and random-risk negative controls where an A7 improvement or temporal-signal claim is made. Candidate local A7 sub-ablations may be described as v0.1 planning labels only. [EVAL: A7 matched comparison / negative controls]

#### Step 12 — Preserve negative results and baseline sufficiency

If A7 fails to improve over A5, is matched or beaten by A2/A3/A4, helps only under synthetic stress, over-abstains, produces unstable regimes, or is matched by shuffled/random controls, save the result as negative, null, diagnostic-only, or baseline-sufficient rather than suppressing it. [EVAL: A7 negative-result discipline]

#### Step 13 — Prepare Layer 10 dashboard/card/export source material

Assemble dashboard-readable source bundles: regime timelines, risk trends, trust scores, stop-loss warnings, A7 matched summaries, negative-control summaries, diagnostic-only counts, metric dictionary references, lineage completeness summaries, and `RegimeCard lineage`. Do not render final dashboard routes or final thesis figure/table placement in this phase playbook. [ARCH: Layer 10 read-only boundary]

#### Step 14 — Attach Layer 0 claim-safety and limitation boundaries

Attach claim-safety tags and limitation labels such as `public_eeg_only`, `temporal_trust_proxy`, `proxy_readiness`, `not_clinical_validation`, `not_real_patient_safety`, and simulation/stress/embodiment tags where applicable. Block forbidden wording and downgrade any output that lacks limitation tags. [REG: claim-boundary tags]

#### Step 15 — Create the Phase 5 handoff package

Freeze Phase 5 outputs with lineage, validation status, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result notes, metric dictionary references, matched keys, Layer 10 source bundle references, Layer 0 summary, open issues, and any BPCRs. Hand Phase 6 a traceable temporal-trust context package without claiming Phase 6 evidence-quality estimator or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ outputs are complete. [EXEC: Phase 5 handoff]

### 5A. Causal feature and recommendation discipline

Phase 5 must keep feature construction, evaluation labels, and downstream recommendations separated so RegimeRisk remains temporal-trust evidence rather than hindsight scoring.

| Partition | Allowed examples | Required boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Decision-time / label-free temporal features | Current/past confidence, entropy, margin, variation ratio, disagreement, threshold status, action history, request/fallback/unsafe burden, artifact/dropout proxies, missingness, recovery markers, evidence-quality context with producer tags. | May feed `RegimeStateRecord`, trust allocation, stop-loss warning, and regime-aware rerun only under declared causal cutoff. |
| Evaluation-only targets or diagnostics | Wrong accepts, correctness clusters, high-confidence wrong cases, future rewards, future simulated unsafe proxies, future stress effects, future embodiment outcomes. | May evaluate risk-error alignment after record emission; cannot become ordinary decision-time features unless legally past under a declared protocol. |
| Optional downstream/proxy context | Stress-conditioned context, simulated transition/reward context, embodiment-proxy state/outcome context, policy/action histories. | May be used only when official later records exist and carry `simulation_only`, `stress_conditioned`, or `embodiment_proxy_only` tags; cannot define core Phase 5 public-data evidence. |
| Recommendations | `normal`, `stricter_evidence`, `trusted_set_restriction`, `fallback`, `no_action`, `unsafe`, `cooldown`, `recovery_monitoring`. | Recommendations are proxy temporal-risk controls or downstream context; they are not final policy actions unless a later phase consumes them through its own records. |

For every feature table or saved temporal feature set, Phase 5 must record source IDs, feature family, availability flag, causal cutoff, split role, rolling-window configuration, feature dictionary/config hash, evaluation-only indicator where applicable, and limitation tags. Any feature without this envelope is diagnostic-only.

[DERIVED] This section is an operational guardrail derived from Layer 5 architecture, registry record envelopes, and A7 leakage/downgrade rules. It does not prescribe a final algorithm, formula, classifier, threshold, rolling-window length, or code structure.

#### 6.2B Output-claim readiness states

| State | Meaning for Phase 5 outputs |
|---|---|
| `claim_ready` | Schema/lineage/causal/matched/metric/negative-control/Layer 0/Layer 10 gates pass for the specific output and claim. |
| `dashboard_source_ready` | Saved records are valid and auditable for Layer 10 rendering/export, but final dashboard/card output is not yet produced by Phase 5. |
| `diagnostic_only` | Output may support debugging, failure analysis, or limitations but cannot support thesis-facing comparative or temporal-trust claims. |
| `stretch_only` | Output depends on optional stress, simulation, embodiment, or downstream context and must carry corresponding proxy tags. |
| `requires_confirmation` | Exact schema/path/metric/run-matrix/dashboard details remain open in the supplied sources and must not be silently resolved. |

#### 6.3 Outputs explicitly not produced by Phase 5

Phase 5 does not produce:

- new `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PredictionRecord`, `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, or core Phase 4 A5 baseline records;
- Phase 6 learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants, `ReadinessContextRecord` final policy outputs, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ outputs, or A9 evidence;
- `DeferralRecord`, contextual-bandit records, reinforcement-learning records, closed-loop simulation records, StressForge stress evidence, MyoSuite/OpenSim embodiment evidence, or final dashboard records;
- final statistical run matrix, final metric formulas where not already canonical, final thesis claims, final paper text, final figure/table numbering, final dashboard routes, command lines, or implementation class names.

### 8. Validation gates and exit criteria

#### Gate 5.1 — Upstream completeness and immutability

All required Phase 0–4 inputs must exist, be schema-valid or explicitly diagnostic-only, and be consumed read-only. Missing required source IDs block or downgrade affected outputs. [EXEC: Phase 5 input contract]

#### Gate 5.2 — Temporal ordering and sequence identity

`WindowRecord`/trial or ordered-sequence references must support deterministic ordering by dataset, subject, session, split, trial/window, model/run, and time/replay index. Ambiguous sequence identity blocks claim-ready A7 use. [REG: temporal ordering]

#### Gate 5.3 — Split and causal cutoff legality

Rolling features must not cross forbidden split boundaries and must not use future labels, correctness, rewards, stress outcomes, or embodiment outcomes as decision-time inputs. Violations block or force diagnostic-only. [EVAL: A7 temporal constraints]

#### Gate 5.4 — Phase 4 action-token and trace integrity

Canonical action tokens, reason codes, costs, trace links, and `regime_aware=false` baseline status must be valid before Phase 4 histories can support A7. Alias or trace gaps downgrade affected rows. [PRIOR: Phase 4 handoff]

#### Gate 5.5 — Regime/trust/stop-loss schema and finite-score validation

`RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, `regime_timelines.csv`, `trust_scores.csv`, and `stop_loss_warnings.csv` must pass schema, finite-value, controlled-vocabulary, source-ID, reason-code, and limitation-tag validation. [REG: Layer 5 validation rules]

#### Gate 5.6 — Matched-comparison eligibility

A7 rows must preserve required keys for matched A5/A7/control comparisons. Missing required keys mark affected rows diagnostic-only and block improvement claims. [EVAL: A7 matched-comparison key requirements]

#### Gate 5.7 — Negative-control sufficiency

Shuffled RegimeRisk and random-risk controls, or explicit diagnostic-only explanation for their absence, are required for strong A7 temporal-signal or improvement claims. [EVAL: A7 negative controls]

#### Gate 5.8 — Metric dictionary and denominator visibility

Every reported metric must reference a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or equivalent metric dictionary lineage. Missing exact definitions or denominators require diagnostic-only status. [REG: MC-008]

#### Gate 5.9 — Negative-result visibility

Null, harmful, over-abstaining, baseline-sufficient, shuffled/random-competitive, and stress-only improvements must be saved and handed off; they must not be filtered out. [EVAL: A7 negative-result discipline]

#### Gate 5.10 — Layer 10 audit/export readiness

Layer 10 source bundles must contain saved records, lineage, metrics, matched reports, warnings, diagnostic flags, and reproducibility manifests sufficient for read-only dashboard/card/export generation. [ARCH: Layer 10]

#### Gate 5.11 — Layer 0 claim-safety readiness

Layer 0 limitation tags and forbidden-claim checks must be attached before any thesis-facing or dashboard-facing Phase 5 summary is considered claim-ready. [ARCH: Layer 0]

#### Phase 5 exit criteria

Phase 5 exits only when:

1. input completeness, temporal ordering, split legality, and causal cutoff checks pass or affected rows are explicitly diagnostic-only;
2. `RegimeStateRecord` exists for valid temporal trust states, with `TrustStateRecord` where independent trust timelines are consumed or claimed;
3. `regime_timelines.csv`, `trust_scores.csv` where applicable, `stop_loss_warnings.csv` where active, and Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` are produced with lineage;
4. A7 matched comparisons and negative controls are complete or diagnostic-only limitations are explicit;
5. metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, limitation tags, and Layer 10/Layer 0 handoffs are complete;
6. Phase 6 handoff can consume temporal-trust context without hidden state.

### 9. Matched-comparison preservation requirements

#### 9.1 Required matched-key envelope

Phase 5 must preserve or explicitly mark `not_applicable` for the A7 matched-key family below:

```text
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id or unresolved trial representation reference
window_id / ordered window sequence ID
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
label_budget_id
model_id
decoder_id
model_family
run_id
config_hash
seed
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
prediction_record_id
uncertainty_record_id
selective_prediction_record_id where applicable
iharq_config_id
iharq_decision_record_id / iharq_trace_record_id where applicable
evidence_quality_record_id where applicable
rolling_window_config_id
regime_config_id
risk_threshold_config_id
trust_allocator_config_id
stop_loss_config_id
negative_control_id where applicable
stress_profile_id where applicable
stress_schedule_id where applicable
policy_id where applicable downstream only
embodiment_mode_id where applicable
ablation_id
matched_comparison_key
metric_dictionary_id
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
diagnostic_only_flag
```

[EVAL: A7 matched-comparison key requirements]

#### 9.2 Required comparisons

| Comparison | Required matching condition | Downgrade rule |
|---|---|---|
| A5 IHARQ-only versus A7 IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Same ordered sequence, split, decoder, calibration, threshold registry, IHARQ config, request/evidence/action-cost budget, and metric dictionary. | Diagnostic-only if unmatched; no A7 improvement claim. |
| Full RegimeRisk versus shuffled RegimeRisk | Same records/sequence except declared shuffle assignment; seed/config logged. | If shuffled is competitive, temporal-trust claim is downgraded. |
| Full RegimeRisk versus random risk score | Same records/budget except random-risk generation; seed/config logged. | If random is competitive, RegimeRisk-specific claim is downgraded. |
| With versus without trust allocator | Same temporal features/risk thresholds/stop-loss settings except trust allocation disabled. | Diagnostic-only if other configs differ. |
| With versus without stop-loss | Same temporal features/trust allocation except stop-loss disabled. | Diagnostic-only if costs/budgets differ without disclosure. |
| Clean versus stress-conditioned context | Same source IDs and declared stress profile/schedule. | Stress-only/proxy-only; no real fatigue or safety claim. |
| Simulation/embodiment-context variants | Same source sequence, simulator/replay config, and embodiment mode where applicable. | Simulation-only/proxy-only; diagnostic-only if mapping incomplete. |

#### 9.3 Preservation rules

- Do not compare Phase 5 A7 outputs against a silently altered Phase 4 baseline.
- Do not treat A4 longer-window or ensemble controls as RegimeRisk.
- Do not compare learned Phase 6 evidence-quality outputs as if they were Phase 5 RegimeRisk outputs.
- Do not remove high-cost, over-abstaining, null, or negative A7 rows from matched reports.
- Preserve diagnostic-only and missingness flags at the row/comparison level.

#### 11.1 Layer 10 dashboard visibility

Phase 5 must hand Layer 10 source material for:

- regime timeline views by dataset/subject/session/sequence;
- risk trend, volatility, drawdown, drift-risk, fatigue-like-risk, dropout-risk, and failure-risk summaries;
- trust scores, trusted-set membership, trust band/trend, and trust allocation shifts where independent trust outputs exist;
- stop-loss warnings, severity, cooldown, recovery, recommendation, and affected IDs;
- A7 matched comparison and negative-control summaries;
- diagnostic-only counts, missingness, leakage warnings, and open issues;
- metric dictionary coverage and unmatched-key status;
- limitation tags and claim-safety warnings.

Layer 10 may read, validate, render, warn, export, card, and package. It may not create primary Layer 5 evidence or repair invalid source records. [ARCH: Layer 10 dashboard boundary]

#### 11.2 Card-source bundle

Phase 5 prepares `RegimeCard lineage` with:

- source `RegimeStateRecord` IDs;
- optional `TrustStateRecord` IDs;
- timeline/trust/stop-loss artifact IDs;
- matched/negative-control IDs;
- limitations and warning tags;
- config hashes and source record hashes;
- export IDs where Layer 10 later renders them.

The final rendered `RegimeCard` remains Layer 10 responsibility. Phase 5 provides source lineage only. [REG: RegimeCard lineage]

#### 11.3 Reproducibility and export readiness

Phase 5 outputs must be reproducible from saved records and versioned configurations. Required reproducibility fields include run ID, schema version, config hash, source record IDs, seed status where randomization or learned variants are used, causal cutoff, split role, feature dictionary, risk/trust/stop-loss config IDs, validation status, diagnostic-only flag, metric dictionary ID, and limitation tags. [ARCH: reproducibility and artifact structure]

#### 11.4 Layer 10 prohibited actions

Layer 10 must not:

- recalculate hidden RegimeRisk source records without writing traceable derived records;
- tune thresholds, trust allocations, or stop-loss settings;
- hide negative or over-abstaining A7 outcomes;
- convert diagnostic-only rows into claim-ready evidence;
- edit upstream records through dashboard interactions;
- present simulation/stress/embodiment proxies as clinical or deployment evidence.

### 12. Claim-safety and limitation boundaries

#### 12.1 Allowed claim level after Phase 5

After successful execution, Phase 5 may support bounded statements such as:

- RegimeRisk produced traceable temporal-trust records from public-data/proxy histories;
- matched A7 comparisons tested whether RegimeRisk context changed or improved IHARQ-family behavior relative to regime-unaware A5 and relevant controls;
- temporal risk, trust, and stop-loss outputs can explain or flag instability under the tested public-data/proxy/simulation conditions;
- Layer 10 can render RegimeRisk evidence from saved records, and Layer 0 can review claims and limitations.

These remain public-data/proxy/simulation-bounded computational reliability statements, not clinical or deployment claims. [ARCH: Layer 5 claim-safety]

#### 12.2 Forbidden overclaims

Phase 5 must not claim:

- clinical fatigue detection, neurological-state estimation, diagnosis, or health-state monitoring;
- real patient safety, medical-device readiness, deployment readiness, real assistive-control safety, or real muscle-stimulation control;
- real rehabilitation efficacy or real-world BCI-FES validation;
- that RegimeRisk improves every subject/session/model without matched evidence;
- that dashboard cards are primary empirical evidence;
- that Phase 5 completes Phase 6 learned evidence-quality, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, bandit, RL, stress, or embodiment evidence;
- that stress-conditioned or embodiment-proxy improvements validate physiological fatigue, real stress robustness, or real-world rehabilitation. [REG: forbidden aliases / claim-boundary tags]

#### 12.3 Required limitation labels

Phase 5 outputs must carry relevant tags, including:

- `public_eeg_only`;
- `temporal_trust_proxy`;
- `proxy_readiness`;
- `evaluation_only` where labels/outcomes are used only after the fact;
- `not_clinical_validation`;
- `not_real_patient_safety`;
- `not_medical_device_readiness`;
- `not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy`;
- `not_real_muscle_stimulation_control`;
- `not_real_deployment_readiness`;
- `simulation_only`, `stress_conditioned`, or `embodiment_proxy_only` where applicable.

#### 12.4 Diagnostic-only claim triggers

Phase 5 outputs must be diagnostic-only if any of the following affects the result:

- temporal leakage or future label/outcome use in decision-time features;
- forbidden split crossing or ambiguous temporal sequence identity;
- missing source IDs or missing upstream validation status;
- missing Phase 4 action-token/reason-code/trace integrity for action-history features;
- missing A7 matched-comparison keys;
- missing shuffled/random negative controls for an A7 improvement claim;
- missing metric dictionary references or metric denominators;
- missing limitation tags;
- unseparated Phase 4 rule-derived and Phase 6 learned evidence-quality variants;
- dashboard-derived values treated as primary evidence;
- stress/simulation/embodiment outputs overclaimed as real clinical or deployment evidence.

#### 12.5 Evidence required before stronger claims

Stronger claims require later validated evidence from Phase 6 for evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, Phase 7–11 for deferral/bandit/RL simulation-bounded policy claims, Phase 9/12/13 for stress and embodiment contexts according to official ordering, Phase 14 for dashboard/export closure, Phase 15 for final thesis integration, and final Layer 0 claim-safety review. [EXEC: Phase 0–15 order]

### 13. Failure, missingness, diagnostic-only handling, and BPCR behavior

#### 13.1 Phase 5 failure modes

| Failure mode | Risk | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Future-information leakage | Invalid temporal-trust evidence | Block affected decision-time rows; diagnostic-only or invalid comparison. |
| Split leakage in rolling histories | Inflated or invalid performance | Block claim-ready use; preserve leakage warning. |
| Ambiguous sequence identity | Invalid temporal matching | Require manifest-level sequence key or downgrade. |
| Phase 4 token/trace gaps | Invalid action-history features | Downgrade affected A7 rows; do not rewrite Phase 4. |
| Evidence-quality variant conflation | A6/A7 boundary error | Require producer/phase tags; diagnostic-only if ambiguous. |
| Missing trust-state rows when independent timeline claimed | Untraceable trust claims | Produce `TrustStateRecord` or downgrade trust timeline claim. |
| Stop-loss unlogged or post-hoc tuned | Unsafe or non-reproducible conservative behavior | Require warning log/config; diagnostic-only otherwise. |
| Random/shuffled controls competitive or missing | Weak temporal-signal claim | Downgrade or mark negative/null result. |
| Over-abstention / false stop-loss | Apparent improvement hides cost | Report as negative result with cost/coverage burden. |
| Proxy label overclaim | Claim-safety violation | Apply Layer 0 downgrade and forbidden-claim block. |
| Dashboard/source boundary violation | Hidden evidence mutation | Reject dashboard-created source evidence; rerun from saved records. |

#### 13.2 Diagnostic-only downgrade behavior

Downgrade must be applied at the most specific affected granularity: row, subject/session, sequence, metric, comparison, sub-analysis, or whole Phase 5 run. The downgrade must write diagnostic-only flags, reason codes, missingness source, impacted metrics, and claim-safety effect. Valid unaffected rows may remain usable only if matched keys, source lineage, and limitation tags are intact. [FRAME: diagnostic-only handling]

#### 13.3 Back-Propagation Correction Request handling

Phase 5 must emit a BPCR instead of editing accepted prior text when actual execution reveals that a prior accepted phase output is incomplete, inconsistent, or insufficient in a way that cannot be handled by local diagnostic-only marking.

Required BPCR structure:

```yaml
back_propagation_request:
  request_id: <stable_request_id>
  discovered_in_phase: Phase 5
  affected_prior_phase: <Phase 0|Phase 1|Phase 2|Phase 3|Phase 4>
  affected_artifact_or_record: <canonical artifact or record name>
  issue_type: <schema_gap|lineage_gap|matched_key_gap|validation_gap|alias_conflict|claim_safety_gap|other>
  severity: <blocking|claim_limiting|diagnostic_only|non_blocking>
  source_conflict: <source anchors or not_applicable>
  downstream_risk: <specific downstream risk>
  required_action: <repair or clarification needed>
  whether_current_phase_can_continue: <yes|yes_with_diagnostic_only|no>
  diagnostic_only_effect: <affected records/metrics/comparisons>
  claim_safety_effect: <allowed claim reduction or forbidden claim risk>
```

#### 13.4 Current BPCR status

No BPCR is emitted by this generated playbook section because no grounded contradiction requiring mutation of accepted Phase 0–4 text was identified during generation. Known upstream risks are carried forward as open issues and diagnostic-only conditions. Actual Phase 5 execution must emit BPCRs if concrete upstream artifacts fail required contracts in a way that local downgrading cannot safely handle.

### 14. Repository, storage, and reproducibility expectations

#### 14.1 Conceptual storage groups

Phase 5 must preserve conceptual storage separation between:

- immutable upstream source records from Phases 0–4;
- Phase 5 derived temporal feature tables;
- `RegimeStateRecord` and conditional `TrustStateRecord` outputs;
- timeline/trust/stop-loss artifacts;
- Layer 5 evaluation outcomes and A7 matched reports;
- negative-control reports and negative-result notes;
- validation reports and diagnostic-only ledgers;
- Layer 10 source bundles and card lineage;
- Layer 0 claim-safety summaries and limitation tags.

#### 14.2 Path-status rule

The architecture and registry mention repository anchors and canonical homes, but `MC-009` preserves path/storage ambiguity. This playbook therefore treats exact paths, package names, CLI names, class names, and test-suite names as deferred implementation details unless already fixed by the supplied source. Manifests must map every produced artifact to its actual storage location and hash during implementation. [REG: MC-009] [FRAME: Implementation Build Book boundary]

#### 14.3 Reproducibility invariants

Every Phase 5 output must be reproducible from source records plus saved configuration and validation manifests. Required invariants:

- no source-record mutation;
- deterministic ordering and causal cutoff reconstruction;
- feature dictionary and rolling-window config captured;
- risk, regime, trust, and stop-loss thresholds/configs captured;
- random seeds captured where random/shuffled/learned variants are used;
- metric dictionary references captured;
- matched comparison keys captured;
- diagnostic-only and negative-result notes preserved;
- dashboard/card outputs regenerable from saved Phase 5 source artifacts.

---

### 15. Phase handoff package

#### 15.1 Handoff to Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ

Phase 5 hands Phase 6 a temporal-trust context package:

- validated `RegimeStateRecord` rows with risk/trend/regime/recommendation/reason-code/source lineage;
- conditional `TrustStateRecord` and `trust_scores.csv` where independent trust timelines are available;
- `stop_loss_warnings.csv` where stop-loss is active;
- regime/trust/stop-loss summaries suitable for `ReadinessContextRecord` assembly, while preserving Phase 6 ownership of learned policy/evidence-quality outputs;
- A7 matched/negative-control/diagnostic-only status, so Phase 6 can avoid building policy conclusions on invalid temporal-trust evidence;
- Layer 10 source bundle references and Layer 0 limitation tags.

Phase 6 must not treat Phase 5 missing or diagnostic-only RegimeRisk outputs as proof that adaptive policy claims are complete. It must consume only validated or explicitly diagnostic temporal context. [EXEC: Phase 5 to Phase 6 handoff]

#### 15.2 Handoff to later phases

| Downstream phase/context | Handoff material | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 7 / A8 | Regime/trust/stop-loss context for learning-to-defer comparisons. | No `DeferralRecord` or deferral claim in Phase 5. |
| Phase 8 / simulation | Regime state and stop-loss context for simulated closed-loop readiness where official simulation records exist. | Simulation-only; no deployment claim. |
| Phase 9 / stress | Regime timelines and stress-conditioned context where official stress artifacts exist. | Stress evidence belongs to stress phase/A12; no physiological fatigue claim. |
| Phases 10–11 / A10–A11 | Temporal-trust context for bandit/RL policy state where simulation-bounded protocols exist. | No bandit/RL policy improvement claim in Phase 5. |
| Phases 12–13 / A13 | Optional embodiment-proxy risk context and gating recommendations where official embodiment records exist. | Embodiment-proxy only; no real muscle control/rehabilitation claim. |
| Phase 14 / Layer 10 | Source records, metrics, matched reports, warnings, RegimeCard lineage, reproducibility manifests. | Final rendered dashboard/cards/exports are Layer 10 outputs. |
| Phase 15 / final thesis | Claim-bounded evidence package, negative results, diagnostic-only flags, limitations, and open issues. | Final thesis wording requires final integration and Layer 0 review. |

#### 15.3 Handoff integrity status

`conditional_pass_pending_actual_execution_records`. This playbook defines the Phase 5 handoff package, but actual integrity depends on real Phase 5 execution passing validation gates, producing required artifacts, preserving matched keys, and carrying diagnostic-only limitations forward.

### 17. Definition of done

#### 17.1 Playbook-section definition of done

This generated Phase 5 playbook section is complete when:

- official phase identity and order are preserved;
- Source Extraction Digest covers architecture, registry, execution plan, evaluation protocol, and accepted prior phases;
- active layers/modules, scope/non-scope, entry conditions, input/output contracts, procedure, lifecycle, validation gates, matched keys, A7 obligations, Layer 10 handoff, Layer 0 claim safety, failure modes, BPCR handling, and downstream handoff are specified;
- no new canonical records, artifacts, phases, modules, ablation IDs, metrics, repository paths, or claims are invented;
- previous Phase 0–4 content is preserved exactly in the cumulative file;
- open issues and deferred items are visible rather than silently resolved;
- YAML handoff is complete.

#### 17.2 Actual Phase 5 execution definition of done

Actual Phase 5 execution is complete only when:

1. Phase 0–4 input completeness, immutability, and validation status are confirmed;
2. temporal ordering, split legality, and causal cutoff gates pass;
3. Phase 4 action-token, reason-code, cost, trace, and `regime_aware=false` baseline integrity are validated;
4. legal rolling temporal features are generated with feature provenance and availability flags;
5. `RegimeStateRecord` outputs are produced and validated;
6. `TrustStateRecord` and `trust_scores.csv` are produced where independent trust timelines are consumed or claimed;
7. `stop_loss_warnings.csv` is produced where stop-loss is active;
8. Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A7 matched comparisons, negative controls, metric dictionary references, and negative-result notes are complete or diagnostic-only limitations are explicit;
9. Layer 10 source bundle and `RegimeCard lineage` are ready for read-only rendering/export;
10. Layer 0 claim-safety tags and forbidden-claim checks are complete;
11. downstream Phase 6 handoff is usable without hidden state;
12. BPCRs, if any, are recorded rather than editing accepted prior phases.

### 0A. Source Extraction Digest

**Architecture facts used:**

- Layer 6 is the **Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer** and implements evidence-quality estimation, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, contextual bandit, and RL readiness policy, but Phase 6 itself focuses on the evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ portions. [ARCH: Layer 6 / Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer]
- Module F is the Adaptive policy module: it learns or compares supervised, deferral, contextual-bandit, and RL policies from readiness contexts, costs, rewards, and simulation records under split control. Phase 6 uses the supervised/evidence-quality subset only. [ARCH: Module F]
- Layer 6 consumes Layers 2–5 records and optional later simulation/stress/embodiment context only when declared; it must not replace Layer 4 IHARQ or Layer 5 RegimeRisk. [ARCH: Layer 6 boundary with Layers 4–9]
- The policy action space preserves Layer 4 stored tokens such as `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, and `unsafe`; Layer 6 policy-only tokens such as `defer` and `no_action` require declared action-space and alias-map governance. [ARCH: Layer 6 policy action space]
- Public EEG labels are task labels, not readiness labels; Layer 6 therefore requires explicit target-construction routes, pseudo-label cards/source bundles, cost models, leakage guards, and claim boundaries. [ARCH: Layer 6 target construction]
- Layer 10 may read, validate, warn, visualize, export, and package records but must not create hidden primary evidence, retune policies, repair split leakage, or rewrite source records. [ARCH: Layer 10 read-only audit/export boundary]
- Layer 0 constrains Phase 6 to offline/proxy public-EEG computational readiness-policy evidence; no clinical, deployment, real-patient safety, rehabilitation, or real muscle-control claim is permitted. [ARCH: Layer 0 claim safety]

**Registry facts used:**

- `ReadinessContextRecord` is the Layer 6 decision-time policy-context record derived from source `PredictionRecord`, calibration/uncertainty/threshold records, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord`/conditional `TrustStateRecord`, `EvidenceQualityRecord`, split/dataset identity, and optional stress/embodiment context only when declared. [REG: ReadinessContextRecord]
- Learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants are produced by Layer 6 when learned evidence-quality estimation is enabled; rule-derived variants may exist from Layer 4, so producer module, phase ID, branch/variant tag, target-construction lineage, source IDs, and schema version must remain distinguishable. [REG: EvidenceQualityRecord / MC-002]
- `PolicyActionRecord` is the Layer 6 policy output record for selected readiness action, policy identity/family, action-space version, legality mask, source IHARQ token where applicable, expected cost/reward, context hash, config hash, and claim boundary. [REG: PolicyActionRecord]
- `DeferralRecord` is a Phase 7/A8 output, not a Phase 6 direct output; Phase 6 may prepare policy context for deferral comparison but must not claim A8 completion. [REG: DeferralRecord]
- `PolicyUpdateTrace` belongs to simulation-authorized update-enabled contextual-bandit/RL runs and is created in later phases; ordinary Phase 6 A9 evidence must remain frozen supervised evaluation unless a later simulation branch is explicitly invoked and traced. When update-capable hooks exist but evaluation is meant to be frozen, the source stack requires disabled-update/no-mutation audit status rather than silent trust in the absence of updates. [REG: PolicyUpdateTrace] [REG: disabled-update audit governance] [EXEC: Disabled-update audit fixture]
- `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, dashboard records, `CardRecord`, and `ReproducibilityManifest` provide evaluation, Layer 10, and Layer 0 governance. [REG: evaluation/dashboard/reproducibility artifacts]

**Execution-plan facts used:**

- Official phase identity is `Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ`. [EXEC: Phase 6 identity]
- Phase 6 consumes validated Phase 1–5 outputs, especially Phase 4 IHARQ-lite records and Phase 5 RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss context where available and decision-time legal. [EXEC: Phase 6 input contract]
- Phase 6 produces `ReadinessContextRecord`, learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants, `PolicyActionRecord`, Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A6/A9 matched comparison and evaluation artifacts, pseudo-label/target-construction/cost/action-space/legality artifacts, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, card source bundles, and a handoff manifest. [EXEC: Phase 6 output contract]
- Phase 6 exit requires schema validation, split/leakage validation, decision-time/evaluation-only partitioning, target-construction lineage, legality-mask validation, frozen held-out policy evaluation, matched comparisons, metric dictionary references, negative-result visibility, Layer 10 source-bundle readiness, and Layer 0 claim-safety tags. [EXEC: Phase 6 gates]
- Phase 6 hands policy/evidence-quality context to Phase 7 learning-to-defer, Phase 8 simulated closed-loop readiness, Phase 9 StressForge-Lite, Phases 10–11 update-enabled policy learning, Phases 12–13 embodiment-proxy demos, Phase 14 dashboard/export, and Phase 15 final thesis integration. [EXEC: Phase 6 downstream handoff]

**Evaluation-protocol version used:** `v0.1`; final run-matrix and final statistical choices are deferred to a later official protocol. [EVAL: v0.1 authority]

**Evaluation-protocol facts used:**

- A6 is `IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator`; Phase 6 directly produces the learned evidence-quality-estimator source records used by A6, while Phase 4 remains the A5 IHARQ-lite source. [EVAL: A6 identity and producer boundary]

### 1. Phase identity, scope, and non-scope

#### 1.1 Identifier and official title

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 6` |
| Official title | `Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ` |
| Official order | After Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust; before Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer. |
| Primary layer | Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer. |
| Primary functional module | Module F — Adaptive policy. |
| Primary submodules in this phase | 6.1 Evidence-quality estimator; 6.2 Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ. |
| Direct evaluation obligations | A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator; A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ. |
| Primary output families | `ReadinessContextRecord`, learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A6/A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, target-construction/pseudo-label/cost/action-space/legality artifacts, card source bundles, and Phase 6 handoff manifest. |

#### 1.2 Purpose

Phase 6 converts validated upstream reliability and temporal-trust evidence into split-safe, auditable learned readiness-policy evidence. It first assembles `ReadinessContextRecord` rows that define what a policy is allowed to know at decision time. It then produces learned evidence-quality estimates for A6 and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ policy actions for A9 using declared pseudo-label, cost-model, action-space, and legality-mask rules. [ARCH: Layer 6 purpose] [EXEC: Phase 6 purpose] [EVAL: A6/A9 identities]

#### 1.3 In-scope work

Phase 6 may perform the following phase-level work:

- validate and freeze upstream Phase 1–5 inputs without mutating them;
- assemble `ReadinessContextRecord` from decision-time-legal features;
- create feature-provenance and observable-field-set documentation for policy contexts;
- construct split-safe reliability targets and cost-based pseudo-labels for training/evaluation, keeping target/evaluation fields separate from decision-time features;
- train/evaluate the evidence-quality estimator and produce learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants;
- define and validate the supervised Adaptive-IHARQ action space, action alias map, legality mask, and cost model;
- train/select supervised Adaptive-IHARQ only on train/validation material and evaluate it frozen on held-out rows;
- produce `PolicyActionRecord` outputs and Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` rows;
- produce A6/A9 matched-comparison reports, metric-dictionary-linked outputs, diagnostic-only flags, and negative-result notes;
- prepare Layer 10 card/dashboard/export source bundles and Layer 0 claim-safety summaries.

#### 1.4 Explicit non-scope

Phase 6 must not:

- overwrite, rewrite, silently normalize, or repair upstream Phase 0–5 canonical records;
- replace Layer 4 IHARQ-lite or Layer 5 RegimeRisk ownership;
- create `DeferralRecord` or claim A8 completion;
- create `TransitionRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, contextual-bandit results, or RL results unless a later simulation-authorized phase exists and traces updates appropriately;
- claim A10/A11 contextual-bandit/RL learning, A12 stress robustness, or A13 embodiment success;
- use `true_label`, decoder correctness, future evidence, future reward, oracle costs/actions, future stress outcomes, future embodiment outcomes, or dashboard-derived metrics as ordinary decision-time policy features;
- claim clinical readiness labels, validated patient safety, medical-device readiness, real deployment readiness, rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation, or real assistive-control safety from public EEG data.

### 1A. Capability-tier and thesis-validity relevance

| Capability tier / thesis role | Phase 6 relevance | Failure or diagnostic-only effect |
|---|---|---|
| C0 public-data reliability spine | Consumes C0/C1 upstream lineage, split identities, model/calibration/IHARQ/RegimeRisk context, and limitation tags. | C0 evidence may remain valid if upstream phases are valid, but Phase 6 cannot upgrade it. |
| C1 IHARQ + RegimeRisk reliability/trust controls | Consumes Phase 4 IHARQ-lite and Phase 5 RegimeRisk/trust outputs as context and comparators. | If Phase 6 fails, C1 evidence remains upstream-only; learned policy claims are not supported. |
| C2 adaptive policy layer | Directly advances C2 through learned evidence-quality estimation and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ under proxy targets/costs. | A6/A9 and C2 adaptive-policy claims become diagnostic-only or blocked. |
| C3 bandit/RL simulation layer | Prepares frozen supervised policy context for later simulation but does not complete C3. | Later C3 phases must not treat missing/invalid Phase 6 policy outputs as claim-ready. |
| C4 embodiment/dashboard/final demo layer | Prepares source bundles and policy records that Layer 10 and later embodiment demos may read. | Dashboard/export can still show diagnostic records, but no stronger adaptive-policy or embodiment claim is allowed. |

Minimum defensible thesis core does not require Phase 6 superiority, but Phase 6 is a target learned-policy contribution for demonstrating that the architecture can move beyond rule-only IHARQ toward adaptive readiness decisions. Negative Phase 6 results remain thesis-valid if recorded honestly as baseline sufficiency or policy limitations. [EVAL: negative-result discipline]

#### 2.2 Immutable upstream records

All accepted upstream source records are read-only for Phase 6. Phase 6 may create derived records, versioned overlays, validation overlays, diagnostic flags, exclusion ledgers, or BPCRs, but it must not mutate upstream records in place. [FRAME: immutable record discipline]

#### 2.3 Carry-forward issues affecting Phase 6

| Issue | Phase 6 effect | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| `MC-001` trial/window representation | Missing trial/window identity breaks matched comparisons. | Mark affected rows diagnostic-only or exclude from claim-ready comparisons. |
| `MC-002` `EvidenceQualityRecord` shared producer nuance | Learned and rule-derived variants may be confused. | Require producer layer/phase, variant/branch, target-construction ID, source IDs, schema version. |
| `MC-003` `combine` vs `combine_evidence` alias | Invalid action-token lineage corrupts policy-action mapping. | Preserve canonical stored source token and validate alias map. |
| `MC-004` `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/Layer 7 boundary | Later simulation may materialize compatible run contexts. | Phase 6 owns canonical decision-time context; later run-specific variants remain downstream or unresolved. |
| `MC-005` `PolicyUpdateTrace` lifecycle | Update-enabled results can contaminate frozen A9 evidence. | Ordinary Phase 6 A9 is frozen supervised; update-enabled branches are downstream and require trace. |
| `MC-007` dashboard metric boundary | Dashboard-derived values may be mistaken for evidence. | Treat dashboard outputs as derived/read-only; do not use as source features. |
| `MC-008` metric dictionary schema/path | Metrics without definitions cannot support thesis-ready claims. | Require `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or diagnostic-only status. |
| `MC-009` repository paths/storage homes | Exact locations may be unresolved. | Use manifest mapping; do not invent official paths. |
| `MC-011`/`MC-012` Layer 10/Layer 0 evidence boundaries | Cards/claims can overstate evidence. | Preserve source-vs-derived and claim-safety boundaries. |

#### 2.4 Continuity decision

The Phase 6 playbook section can be appended because accepted Phase 0–5 playbook content is present. Actual execution of Phase 6 is **conditional** on the existence and validation of the upstream records named above. If actual records are absent, invalid, unmatched, or leakage-tainted, affected Phase 6 outputs must be blocked, excluded, or marked diagnostic-only rather than treated as claim-ready. [PRIOR: Phase 5 handoff] [EXEC: Phase 6 entry gates]

### 3. Architecture-grounded phase objective and active layers/modules

#### 3.1 Objective

Phase 6 operationalizes the Layer 6 policy plane by creating leakage-safe readiness contexts, learned evidence-quality estimates, and frozen supervised policy actions from validated upstream evidence. The phase tests whether learned reliability scoring and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ improve proxy readiness trade-offs over raw decoder, calibration, threshold, uncertainty/selective-prediction, ordinary aggregation/ensemble, IHARQ-lite, and RegimeRisk-aware contexts under matched comparison. [ARCH: Layer 6 problem solved] [EVAL: A6/A9 design]

#### 3.2 Active layer participation

| Layer | Role in Phase 6 | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, negative results, and forbidden claim wording. | Does not produce empirical evidence or policy scores. |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Supplies immutable public-data, split, window/trial, preprocessing, label-map, and artifact lineage. | Public EEG labels remain task labels, not readiness labels. |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Supplies predictions, model IDs, baseline metrics, subject profiles, failure cases, and ordinary control lineage. | No decoder retraining or hidden model selection in Phase 6. |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Supplies calibration, uncertainty, threshold, selective-prediction, leakage warnings, and matched operating points. | No test-threshold retuning or calibration repair in Phase 6. |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Supplies IHARQ-lite decisions, traces, reason codes, action tokens, fallback/unsafe/uncertain status, and A5 comparator records. | Layer 6 must not overwrite or rename Layer 4 source tokens. |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Supplies optional RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss context and A7 comparison context. | Regime/trust remains proxy temporal trust, not clinical fatigue or patient state. |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Primary producer of readiness contexts, learned evidence-quality outputs, supervised policy actions, A6/A9 evaluations, and handoff artifacts. | Ordinary Phase 6 is offline/frozen supervised; update-enabled adaptation belongs to later simulation-authorized phases. |
| Layers 7–9 | Downstream consumers of Phase 6 records in simulation, stress, and embodiment-proxy contexts. | Not required for core Phase 6; their records must not be assumed present or used for stronger claims. |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Reads Phase 6 source bundles for dashboard/card/export/reproducibility. | Does not create hidden primary evidence, pseudo-labels, policies, or repairs. |

#### 3.3 Primary and supporting modules

| Module/submodule | Role | Output or check |
|---|---|---|
| Module F — Adaptive Policy Engine | Primary Layer 6 policy-learning family; Phase 6 uses its evidence-quality and supervised-policy stages only. | Phase 6 policy/evidence-quality source records. |
| P0 / 6.0 IHARQ-lite reference policy | Reference/comparator stage inherited from Phase 4/Layer 4 records; not a new Phase 6 IHARQ-lite producer. | Preserved A5 baseline/action-token context and source `IHARQDecisionRecord` lineage. |
| P1 / 6.1 Evidence-quality estimator | Learns reliability/failure-probability estimates from legal features and proxy targets. | Learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, reliability-vs-coverage, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics. |
| P2 / 6.2 Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Learns multi-action readiness decisions from split-safe pseudo-labels, action-space, legality-mask, and cost model. | `PolicyActionRecord`, action distributions, matched-cost/coverage reports. |
| Context construction | Assembles decision-time-observable policy context from Layers 1–5 records. | `ReadinessContextRecord`, observable-field-set ID, feature-provenance bundle. |
| Target-construction / pseudo-label governance | Creates training/evaluation targets and pseudo-labels, with target/evaluation partitioning and leakage guards. | Target-construction card/source bundle, pseudo-label files, target-construction ID/version. |
| Action-space and legality-mask governance | Preserves Layer 4 tokens and validates legal policy actions. | Action-space version, action alias map, legality-mask ID. |
| Cost-model governance | Defines declared computational costs and sensitivity variants. | Cost-model config and cost-model card/source bundle. |
| Layer 6 evaluation exporter | Produces evaluation records, matched reports, negative notes, and diagnostic flags. | Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, A6/A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Handoff manifest builder | Packages source IDs, configs, hashes, validation statuses, open issues, and claim tags. | Phase 6 handoff manifest / `ReproducibilityManifest` input. |

#### 3.4 Feedforward and loopback constraints

Phase 6 receives feedforward records from Layers 1–5 and feeds `ReadinessContextRecord`, learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, and evaluation artifacts to Layers 7–10 and Phase 15. Any diagnostic warning from Layer 6 back to earlier layers, such as high-confidence failure clusters or calibration drift warnings, must be a visible diagnostic warning or versioned correction request; it must not retune upstream models, thresholds, calibrators, or IHARQ rules silently. [ARCH: Layer 6 consumers/connections] [FRAME: non-destructive record discipline]

| Input | Status | Purpose | Missing/invalid behavior |

| Target-construction config/card/source bundle | Required | Documents proxy targets, allowed labels/future information, leakage guard, split use, target route, limitation tags. | A6/A9 learned claims diagnostic-only. |
| Pseudo-label files/version | Required for supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Provides training targets and per-action cost vectors. | A9 blocked or diagnostic-only. |
| Observable-field-set / feature-set manifest | Required | Declares decision-time-legal fields and excluded target/evaluation fields. | Block if feature legality cannot be audited. |
| Metric dictionary references | Required for metric-based claims | Provides metric definitions, denominator, direction, aggregation, and claim eligibility. | Metrics diagnostic-only. |
| Phase 6 run/config/seed/schema manifest | Required | Reproducibility, lineage, and export readiness. | Handoff incomplete. |

#### 4.3 Forbidden inputs as ordinary decision-time features

The following may be used only in target construction or evaluation partitions where explicitly allowed and split-safe, never as ordinary policy features at decision time: `true_label`, decoder correctness, held-out labels, future-window evidence not causally available, future reward, oracle action, oracle cost, future stress outcome, future embodiment outcome, dashboard-generated metrics/cards/warnings, and any manually repaired or post-hoc-retuned upstream value. [ARCH: Layer 6 target construction] [EVAL: A9 forbidden designs]

### 4A. Entry conditions

Phase 6 execution may begin only when these entry conditions are met or explicitly downgraded:

| Entry condition | Required evidence | If not satisfied |
|---|---|---|
| Accepted Phase 0–5 playbook content present | Cumulative Phase 0–5 playbook exists and is immutable. | Stop or generate only a non-cumulative diagnostic draft; here, condition is satisfied. |
| Upstream records exist and are readable | Phase 1–5 handoff manifests and record IDs/hashes/statuses. | Block affected rows; emit diagnostic flags or BPCR if upstream defect is grounded. |
| Split and leakage status known | `SplitRecord`, split manifest, `SplitIntegrityReport`, `LeakageWarningRecord`. | Block claim-ready target/policy training and evaluation. |
| Layer 4 IHARQ baseline valid | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, canonical tokens, A5 matched report. | A6/A9 vs A5 claim blocked. |
| Optional RegimeRisk context validated before use | `RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, stop-loss warnings, temporal cutoff status. | Regime-aware context rows diagnostic-only or omitted with limitation. |
| Action-space/cost/legality/target governance available | Versioned action-space, alias map, legality mask, cost config, target-construction card/source bundle. | A9 blocked or diagnostic-only. |
| Metric dictionary references available | `MetricDictionaryEntry` IDs for reported metric families. | Metric rows diagnostic-only. |
