### 8. Validation gates and exit criteria

#### 8.1 Phase-entry gates

- **Gate 6.1 — Prior handoff availability:** Phase 0–5 handoff manifests or accepted playbook sections must be available, with source IDs and validation statuses for consumed records. [PRIOR: Phase 0–5 handoffs]
- **Gate 6.2 — Upstream immutability:** Phase 6 must operate on immutable upstream records; any correction uses overlays, exclusion, rerun/versioning, or BPCR. [FRAME: immutable discipline]
- **Gate 6.3 — Split/leakage eligibility:** split roles, leakage warnings, and target/evaluation partitions must be known before any learned estimator or supervised policy training. [EVAL: A6/A9 leakage rules]

#### 8.2 Internal validation gates

| Gate | Validation requirement | Pass | Diagnostic-only | Blocked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gate 6.4 — Context schema and feature legality | `ReadinessContextRecord` schema, source IDs, observable-field-set ID, and forbidden-field exclusion validate. | Context can support A6/A9. | Noncritical optional feature missing but disclosed. | Forbidden target/future/dashboard field present. |
| Gate 6.5 — Evidence-quality target legality | Target-construction card exists and decoder-correctness/high-confidence wrong targets are partition-safe. | A6 training/evaluation allowed. | Target ambiguity or missing optional target narrows claim. | Target leakage or missing required target lineage. |
| Gate 6.6 — Learned quality variant distinction | Learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` has producer/phase/variant/source/target/schema fields. | A6 quality comparisons allowed. | Ambiguous rule/learned variants diagnostic-only. | Variant ambiguity affects all A6 evidence. |
| Gate 6.7 — Action-space and alias validation | Action-space version, alias map, Layer 4 source-token preservation, and policy-only tokens validate. | A9 action export allowed. | Alias-affected rows diagnostic-only. | Invalid/unknown action tokens emitted as valid. |
| Gate 6.8 — Legality-mask validation | Unsafe/stop-loss/fallback/request-budget/no-future-window constraints apply before optimization and evaluation. | Policy rows allowed. | Missing legality explanation narrows claim. | Illegal actions counted as valid. |
| Gate 6.9 — Cost and pseudo-label validation | Cost config, pseudo-label version, per-action cost vectors, split safety, and target-construction lineage validate. | A9 supervised training allowed. | Cost-sensitivity missing narrows superiority claims. | Leaky/unversioned pseudo-labels or test-tuned costs. |
| Gate 6.10 — Frozen held-out evaluation | Policy selected on validation only and evaluated frozen on held-out rows. | A9 claim-ready if other gates pass. | Training curves shown diagnostic only. | Updates or test selection mixed with held-out evaluation. |
| Gate 6.11 — Matched-comparison eligibility | A6/A9 comparisons include required row/config/model/split/action/cost/metric keys. | Comparative claim allowed. | Partial match visible as diagnostic-only. | Unmatched row used for superiority claim. |
| Gate 6.12 — Metric dictionary coverage | Each metric has `MetricDictionaryEntry` or explicit diagnostic-only status. | Metric supports claim. | Metric shown with warning only. | Metric claim made without definition. |
| Gate 6.13 — Negative-result visibility | Baseline sufficiency, estimator weakness, policy collapse, instability, or null results produce `NegativeResultNote`. | Results can be interpreted. | Limited negative note narrows claim. | Negative result hidden or omitted. |
| Gate 6.14 — Layer 10 source-bundle readiness | Dashboard/card/export source bundles include source IDs, hashes, diagnostics, limitations, metrics, and matched reports. | Layer 10 can read/render later. | Missing optional display source flagged. | Source lineage missing for key outputs. |
| Gate 6.15 — Layer 0 claim-safety readiness | Required limitation labels attached; forbidden claim wording blocked. | Claim-ready under bounded language. | Diagnostic-only or narrowed claim. | Clinical/deployment/real-control overclaim persists. |

#### 8.3 Exit conditions

Phase 6 exits as **pass** for claim-eligible Phase 6 evidence only if required inputs are valid, `ReadinessContextRecord` and learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`/`PolicyActionRecord` outputs validate, A6/A9 matched comparisons are complete for the claimed comparisons, metric dictionary references exist, negative results are visible, Layer 10 source bundles are handoff-ready, and Layer 0 limitations are attached.

Phase 6 exits as **diagnostic-only** when outputs are usable for debugging, dashboard warnings, or future repair but fail matched keys, metric dictionary, target-construction, feature-legality, variant-distinction, cost-sensitivity, or baseline-comparator requirements.

Phase 6 is **blocked** for affected records when leakage, forbidden decision-time fields, test-set tuning, illegal valid actions, missing required pseudo-labels/cost configs, missing required context records, or clinical/deployment overclaims cannot be corrected by local diagnostic flags.

#### 9.2 Required comparison preservation

| Comparison | Required matching | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A6 vs A2 | Same rows/splits/model/calibration lineage, threshold registry, matched coverage/cost or operating point, metric dictionary. | Missing threshold registry, test-tuned threshold, unmatched coverage/cost. |
| A6 vs A3 | Same rows/splits/model/calibration/uncertainty/selective lineage, risk/coverage rows. | Different row populations or missing selective/uncertainty lineage. |
| A6 vs A4 | Same window/session/model family universe and ordinary control config. | Different window history or no delay/evidence-cost accounting. |
| A6 vs A5 | Same source `IHARQDecisionRecord`, action token, reason code, trace ID, prediction/calibration rows. | Missing trace, action-token rewrite, quality-feature circularity. |
| A6 learned vs rule-derived evidence-quality variants | Producer layer/phase, variant, target-construction ID, source IDs. | Learned/rule variant ambiguity. |
| A9 vs A0/A1 | Same data rows, model, split, seed/config, calibration status where applicable. | Different row population or missing model/calibration lineage. |
| A9 vs A2/A3 | Same threshold/uncertainty/selective operating point and matched coverage/cost. | Test-tuned threshold or unmatched coverage/cost. |
| A9 vs A4 | Same row/window population, aggregation/ensemble config, model family, split, seed/config. | Ordinary control evaluated on different windows without diagnostic flag. |
| A9 vs A5 | Same `IHARQDecisionRecord`, source token, reason code, cost/action-space mapping. | Missing source action token or alias mapping. |
| A9 vs A6 | Same evidence-quality variant, target-construction ID, producer module, split, feature legality. | Untagged evidence-quality variant or target leakage. |
| A9 with vs without A7 context | Same rows/policy protocol except legal RegimeRisk/trust fields. | Future regime fields, invalid temporal cutoff, or clinical overclaim. |
| A9 vs A8 | Future-only at Phase 6 exit: compare only after Phase 7 `DeferralRecord` exists, using same deferral target/fallback/cost/action-space/coverage. | Phase 7 rows missing in Phase 6; preserve keys and mark comparison `prepared_later`, not claimed. |
| Context/action/cost ablations | Same rows/splits/policy family except declared feature/action/cost difference. | Hidden feature/action/cost changes or unmatched rows. |

#### 9.3 Missing-key handling

If a required key is absent, the affected row/comparison/metric must be marked `diagnostic_only`, listed in the matched report, surfaced to Layer 10 warnings, and prevented from supporting Phase 15 thesis-confirmatory claims. When the missing key reveals an upstream source defect that cannot be handled locally, actual execution must emit a BPCR. [FRAME: BPCR] [EVAL: missing key handling]

### 10. Ablation and evaluation obligations

#### 10.1 Directly produced or enabled by Phase 6

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 6 obligation |
|---|---|---|
| A6 | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Directly produce learned evidence-quality outputs, target-construction lineage, reliability-vs-coverage and high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, A6 matched comparisons, metric-linked evaluation records, negative-result notes, and diagnostic flags. |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Directly produce split-safe readiness contexts, pseudo-label/cost/action-space/legality artifacts, frozen supervised policy artifact/metadata, `PolicyActionRecord`, A9 matched comparisons, context/action/cost ablations, metric-linked evaluation records, negative-result notes, and diagnostic flags. |

#### 10.2 Consumed or preserved comparators

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 6 treatment |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder baseline | Required raw/accept-all comparator where prediction records exist; preserved from Phase 2/evaluation lineage. |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder baseline | Calibration context/comparator where available; not sufficient alone to claim evidence quality. |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Required simple threshold comparator for A6/A9; threshold registry and matched operating point required. |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Required uncertainty/selective comparator where records exist; risk/coverage and matched rows required. |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Required where ordinary controls exist, to prevent crediting aggregation/smoothing as learned policy value. |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite | Primary rule-based IHARQ comparator and source action-token context. |
| A7 | IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Optional/conditional RegimeRisk context and comparison where Phase 5 records are valid; Phase 6 does not produce A7. |
| A8 | Learning-to-defer | Prepared for Phase 7 comparison; not produced in Phase 6. |

#### 10.3 Downstream ablations prepared but not completed

Phase 6 prepares but does not complete A8 learning-to-defer, A10 contextual bandit, A11 RL policy, A12 stress tests, and A13 MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demonstration. No A14 is introduced. [EVAL: A0–A13 ladder]

#### 10.4 Metric families to prepare for Layer 10

| Metric family | Phase 6 use | Claim condition |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence-quality ranking/calibration | A6 reliability/failure score quality. | Requires metric dictionary and score-calibration evidence if calibrated probability is claimed. |
| Reliability-vs-coverage / risk-coverage | A6 and A9 accepted-decision quality under thresholds/policies. | Requires matched rows and denominator definitions. |
| High-confidence-wrong detection | A6 failure-risk visibility. | Diagnostic-only if target/audit missing or weak. |
| Wrong-accept / unsafe-accept | A9 proxy risk reduction. | Not real patient safety; requires legal evaluation labels and matched coverage/cost. |
| Coverage / accepted-decision | A9 useful-decision preservation. | Must be reported with burden/cost, not alone. |
| Request/wait/fallback/no-action/unsafe burden | Detects over-conservatism or policy collapse. | Required for adaptive-policy claims. |
| Declared proxy utility / cost | A9 cost-sensitive comparison. | Requires cost config and sensitivity; computational utility only. |
| Action distribution and legality | Validates action-space use, action-class imbalance, and legality-mask compliance. | Illegal action count and action collapse must be surfaced. |
| Action-probability calibration where probabilistic policies are used | Checks whether reported action probabilities are meaningful policy uncertainty rather than decorative scores. | Required only for probabilistic policies; otherwise mark `not_applicable`; missing probability calibration downgrades probability-specific claims. |
| Context ablation | Tests value of calibration/IHARQ/evidence-quality/RegimeRisk/history context. | Same rows/splits; hidden feature changes diagnostic-only. |
| Cost sensitivity | Tests robustness to cost weights. | Superiority claims narrowed if wins only under arbitrary cost. |
| Matched deltas | A6/A9 superiority or baseline sufficiency. | Requires `MatchedComparisonReport` and metric dictionary. |
| Generalization/stability | Subject/session/dataset/seed stability. | Final statistics deferred; missing stability narrows claim. |

#### 10.5 Negative-result interpretation

A6/A9 may legitimately show that a simpler threshold, uncertainty/selective predictor, ordinary ensemble, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality threshold, RegimeRisk context, or future deferral baseline is sufficient. Such outcomes must be recorded with `NegativeResultNote` and used to narrow claims rather than hidden. [EVAL: negative-result discipline]

### 11. Dashboard, card, reproducibility, and export obligations

#### 11.1 Layer 10 dashboard visibility

Phase 6 must hand Layer 10 source material for:

- evidence-quality score distributions, reliability-vs-coverage views, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, learned vs rule-derived quality variant status, and feature/context ablations;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ action distributions, legality-mask violations, cost/coverage/wrong-accept trade-offs, request/wait/fallback/no-action/unsafe burden, cost sensitivity, and matched-comparison summaries;
- diagnostic-only counts by source reason: missing keys, target leakage, feature illegality, metric dictionary gap, variant ambiguity, action alias issue, cost/pseudo-label gap, missing comparator, negative-result status, forbidden claim wording;
- limitation tags and source-record lineage filters by dataset, subject/session, split, model, calibration, threshold, IHARQ action, evidence-quality variant, RegimeRisk/trust context, policy family, cost config, seed, and ablation ID.

#### 11.2 Card-source bundles

Phase 6 prepares source bundles for Layer 10 cards, but rendered cards are Layer 10-derived artifacts:

| Source bundle | Must include | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence-quality card source bundle | Estimator family, feature groups, target construction, split/seed/config, learned/rule variant, metric dictionary IDs, reliability-vs-coverage, high-confidence-wrong findings, matched reports, negative notes, diagnostics, limitations. | Supports A6 display only; not primary evidence. |
| Controller-card source bundle | Policy ID/family, input records, action space, legality rules, target/pseudo-label route, cost model, training/validation/test protocol, baselines, matched metrics, action distributions, failure cases, negative notes, limitations, lineage, claim tags. | Supports A9 display only; not a policy-repair/model-selection interface. |

#### 11.3 Reproducibility and export readiness

Required reproducibility fields include source record IDs, output record IDs, target-construction ID/version, pseudo-label version, action-space version, alias-map ID, legality-mask ID, cost-config ID, policy ID/family, metric dictionary IDs, matched-comparison IDs, run ID, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, validation statuses, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result note IDs, limitation tags, and open issue IDs. Exact repository paths and commands remain deferred unless already manifest-mapped. [REG: ReproducibilityManifest]

#### 11.4 Layer 10 prohibited actions

Layer 10 must not retrain the estimator/policy, retune thresholds or cost weights, create pseudo-labels, repair leakage, rewrite source records, hide negative results, or convert dashboard warnings/cards into empirical evidence. [ARCH: Layer 10 boundary]

### 12. Claim-safety and limitation boundaries

#### 12.1 Allowed claim level after Phase 6

If all relevant gates pass, Phase 6 may support bounded claims such as:

- a split-safe learned evidence-quality estimator improved proxy evidence-reliability ranking or reliability-vs-coverage under the declared public-EEG protocol;
- learned evidence-quality scoring detected some high-confidence wrong cases that simpler confidence/uncertainty/IHARQ-lite baselines missed, if matched evidence supports it;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ improved declared proxy readiness-policy trade-offs over specified matched baselines in held-out frozen evaluation;
- a simpler baseline was sufficient, limiting the need for learned evidence-quality or supervised adaptive policy in the tested condition;
- Phase 6 produced a frozen supervised policy/evidence-quality context for later simulated closed-loop, stress, bandit/RL, embodiment-proxy, dashboard, and thesis-integration phases.

#### 12.2 Required limitation labels

Applicable outputs must carry labels from:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based
computational_policy_only
evaluation_only
frozen_supervised_policy
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
diagnostic_only where applicable
simulation_only where downstream simulation records are used
stress_conditioned where downstream stress records are used
embodiment_proxy_only where downstream embodiment records are used
```

#### 12.3 Forbidden overclaims

Phase 6 must not claim or imply:

- validated clinical readiness decisions;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real BCI-FES deployment readiness;
- real-time online adaptive safety;
- real rehabilitation efficacy or therapeutic benefit;
- real muscle stimulation control or real assistive-control safety;
- clinical fatigue, drift, neurological decline, or physiological diagnosis;
- human expert readiness labels unless separately supplied and validated, which the provided source set does not establish;
- contextual-bandit, RL, stress, or embodiment success without later phase records;
- dashboard/card outputs as primary empirical evidence.

#### 12.4 Evidence required before stronger claims

Any stronger claim requires later validated simulation/stress/embodiment records, Phase 14 dashboard/export closure, Phase 15 final claim-evidence integration, final metric dictionary/run-matrix decisions, and explicit Layer 0 review. Phase 6 alone cannot authorize those stronger claims. [EXEC: Phase 14/15 handoff] [EVAL: A10–A13 boundaries]

### 13. Failure, missingness, diagnostic-only handling, and BPCR behavior

#### 13.1 Failure modes and required response

| Failure mode | Required response | Claim effect |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream record missing, invalid, or unjoinable | Block affected row or mark diagnostic-only; emit BPCR only if accepted upstream artifact requires repair. | No claim-ready A6/A9 use for affected rows. |
| Split leakage or target leakage | Block affected learned estimator/policy evidence. | A6/A9 thesis-facing claim invalid. |
| Forbidden decision-time feature in `ReadinessContextRecord` | Remove in versioned rerun if local; otherwise diagnostic/block and log. | Affected context/policy rows non-claim-ready. |
| Learned/rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants not distinguishable | Mark A6/A9 quality-variant comparisons diagnostic-only. | No learned-quality improvement claim. |
| Target-construction card/source bundle missing | Mark learned A6/A9 target-dependent claims diagnostic-only. | No thesis-ready learned target claim. |
| Pseudo-label files missing, unversioned, or leaky | Block A9. | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ claim unavailable. |
| Action-space or legality mask missing | Block `PolicyActionRecord` claim-ready export. | No policy-action claim. |
| Illegal actions emitted as valid | Invalidate affected policy rows; produce diagnostic flag/negative note. | A9 blocked or narrowed. |
| Source IHARQ action token not preserved | Diagnostic-only for affected comparisons; repair requires alias-map validation or BPCR if upstream. | A5/A9 linkage blocked. |
| Cost model unversioned or sensitivity absent | Downgrade cost-superiority claims. | A9 may remain descriptive only. |
| Policy selected/tuned on test labels | Block A9 claim-ready evidence. | Held-out policy claim invalid. |
| Frozen evaluation mixed with update-enabled traces or missing required no-mutation proof | Split into diagnostic/update branch; require `PolicyUpdateTrace` for actual updates and disabled-update/no-mutation audit status when update hooks exist but frozen evaluation is claimed. | A9 frozen claim blocked or diagnostic-only if separation cannot be proven. |
| Baseline comparator missing without disclosure | Produce limitation/diagnostic flag. | Superiority language narrowed. |
| Metric dictionary missing | Mark affected metrics diagnostic-only. | No metric-bearing claim. |
| Negative result hidden | Emit `NegativeResultNote`; Layer 0 warning. | Claim-safety failure until visible. |
| Dashboard/card treated as primary evidence | Layer 0 blocks claim and Layer 10 warning required. | Derived-output overclaim blocked. |
| Forbidden clinical/deployment/real-control wording | Layer 0 blocks or rewrites claim boundary. | Claim cannot proceed. |

#### 13.2 Diagnostic-only downgrade rules

Affected records, rows, metrics, comparisons, or claims must be marked diagnostic-only when any minimum gate fails but the artifact remains useful for debugging, dashboards, or future repair. Diagnostic-only artifacts must remain visible to Layer 10 and Layer 0; they must not be omitted from export packages in a way that hides failure. [FRAME: diagnostic-only discipline]

#### 13.3 Back-Propagation Correction Request handling

No BPCR is emitted by this generated playbook section. Actual Phase 6 execution must emit a BPCR instead of editing previous phases when a real grounded upstream defect is found, such as a missing required upstream canonical record, schema failure, matched-key mismatch, leakage risk, invalid status, unsupported claim, or stale artifact that cannot be handled locally.

Template to use during execution:

```yaml
back_propagation_request:
  request_id: "BPCR-P6-<short-id>"
  discovered_in_phase: "P6"
  affected_prior_phase: "P<0-5>"
  affected_artifact_or_record: "<canonical name or GAP>"
  affected_source_record_ids: []
  issue_type: "naming_mismatch | missing_record | schema_failure | lineage_gap | matched_key_mismatch | leakage_risk | invalid_status | unsupported_claim | stale_artifact | other"
  severity: "blocking | claim_limiting | diagnostic_only_risk | non_blocking | optional_stretch"
  source_conflict: []
  downstream_risk: []
  required_action: "revalidate | regenerate | exclude | add_overlay | update_registry_decision_needed | user_confirmation_needed | other"
  whether_current_phase_can_continue: "yes | no | diagnostic_only | partial | requires_confirmation"
  diagnostic_only_effect: "none | current_phase_only | downstream_phases | affected_ablation_only | requires_confirmation"
  claim_safety_effect: []
  layer10_visibility_required: true
  layer0_review_required: true
  notes: ""
```

#### 13.4 Current BPCR status

`none_emitted_by_generated_playbook_section`. This is not a guarantee that execution will find no upstream defects; it means that, during playbook generation, no grounded contradiction requiring accepted Phase 0–5 mutation was identified. [FRAME: BPCR audit]

### 14. Repository, storage, and reproducibility expectations

#### 14.1 Conceptual storage groups

The source documents allow conceptual storage/manifests but leave exact implementation paths/commands partly deferred. Phase 6 should maintain manifest-mapped storage groups for:

- readiness context records;
- learned evidence-quality records;
- policy records;
- target-construction and pseudo-label artifacts;
- action-space, alias-map, legality-mask, and cost-model configs;
- policy artifacts and metadata;
- evaluation outcomes and matched comparison reports;
- negative-result notes and diagnostic-only flags;
- card source bundles;
- handoff/reproducibility manifests and export inputs.

#### 14.2 Path-status rule

Do not invent final repository paths, commands, tests, class names, or CLI names. Where the registry or execution plan names conceptual locations or manifest families, use manifest mapping and mark exact paths as `implementation_detail_deferred` if they are not canonical. [FRAME: implementation-domain boundary]

#### 14.3 Reproducibility invariants

Every Phase 6 claim-bearing artifact must be reproducible from saved inputs, configs, seeds, hashes, schema versions, metric dictionary entries, matched comparison keys, and validation statuses. Reruns that change feature sets, target construction, pseudo-labels, costs, action spaces, policies, or upstream records must create versioned outputs rather than overwriting validated records. [REG: ReproducibilityManifest] [FRAME: versioned record discipline]

### 15. Phase handoff package

#### 15.1 Handoff to Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer

Phase 7 receives:

- validated `ReadinessContextRecord` rows;
- learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants where valid;
- `PolicyActionRecord` outputs from supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- action-space version, alias map, legality-mask ID, and cost config;
- pseudo-label/target-construction limitations and diagnostic flags;
- A9 policy outputs and matched reports so Phase 7 can compare learning-to-defer against supervised Adaptive-IHARQ without reinterpreting Phase 6 evidence;
- claim tags and warnings preventing pseudo-labels from being treated as real readiness labels. [EXEC: Phase 6 to Phase 7 handoff]

#### 15.2 Handoff to Phase 8 and later simulation/policy phases

Phase 8 and Phases 10–11 receive frozen policy outputs and policy-context lineage only as simulation-compatible inputs. Update-enabled contextual-bandit/RL claims require later `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, and `PolicyUpdateTrace` records; Phase 6 does not complete those claims. [REG: PolicyUpdateTrace] [EXEC: Phase 8–11 downstream handoff]

#### 15.3 Handoff to Phase 9 StressForge-Lite and Phases 12–13 embodiment demos

Stress and embodiment phases receive Phase 6 readiness/action context and limitation tags. They must not treat Phase 6 outputs as stress robustness, embodiment success, real motor control, or real assistive-control safety evidence without their own later records and claim boundaries. [EVAL: A12/A13 boundaries]

#### 15.4 Handoff to Phase 14 and Phase 15

Phase 14 receives dashboard-readable Phase 6 source records, validation reports, evaluation artifacts, card source bundles, matched reports, metrics, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, limitation tags, and handoff manifest. Phase 15 receives those same lineage artifacts for final claim-evidence integration, but may not upgrade Phase 6 beyond public-EEG/proxy/frozen-supervised computational policy boundaries. [ARCH: Layer 10] [EXEC: Phase 14/15 handoff]

#### 15.5 Handoff integrity status

Handoff integrity at playbook-generation time is `conditional_pass_pending_actual_execution_records`. The section is complete for planning, but actual phase execution must validate and materialize records before downstream phases treat outputs as claim-ready.

### 16. Open issues and requires-confirmation items

| Open issue | Status category | Phase 6 impact | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact pseudo-label file names/paths | implementation-detail deferred | A9 reproducibility weakened if unmapped. | Use manifest mapping; do not invent final paths. |
| Target-construction card/source bundle canonical name/path | non-blocking but claim-limiting | A6/A9 target provenance may be ambiguous. | Keep as required source bundle; mark exact name/path requires confirmation. |
| Feature-table/feature-provenance bundle canonical name/path | implementation-detail deferred | Feature legality audit may be hard to locate. | Manifest-map feature sets and observable-field IDs. |
| `EvidenceQualityRecord` learned/rule-derived variant distinction | diagnostic-only risk | A6/A9 quality comparisons can collapse producer branches. | Require producer layer/phase, derivation type, target-construction ID/version, source IDs. |
| `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/Layer 7 boundary | downstream claim-limiting | Later simulation may create run-specific compatible contexts. | Preserve Layer 6 canonical context; mark Layer 7 variants downstream/unresolved. |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` lifecycle | downstream contamination risk | Update-enabled content can contaminate frozen A9. | Ordinary Phase 6 remains frozen; later update branches require trace. |
| Disabled-update/no-mutation audit schema/path | diagnostic-only risk | Frozen supervised evaluation can be contaminated if update hooks exist but disabled status is not auditable. | Require disabled-update/no-mutation audit status where applicable; manifest-map exact schema/path until implementation detail is finalized. |
| Action-token aliases and source `uncertain` state | diagnostic-only risk | Invalid action distributions and A5/A9 comparison corruption. | Validate alias map and preserve `source_iharq_action`. |
| Deferral target/reason vocabularies | optional/stretch clarification | Phase 7/A8 comparison depends on deferral definitions. | Defer output to Phase 7; prepare only context/cost lineage. |
| Cost-model card/source-bundle schema/path | non-blocking but claim-limiting | Cost superiority cannot be audited if missing. | Require versioned cost config and sensitivity references. |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema/path | diagnostic-only risk | Metric claims cannot be thesis-ready without definitions. | Require metric IDs or diagnostic-only status. |
| Final statistical tests, run counts, seed counts | evaluation-protocol-v1 deferred | v0.1 cannot lock final inference. | Defer to later official evaluation protocol. |
| Dashboard routes and final figure/table numbering | final-integration deferred | Does not block source bundles but affects final presentation. | Defer to Phase 14/15. |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` vs `ClaimEvidenceManifest` | source ambiguity carried forward | Final claim linkage may fragment. | Preserve naming ambiguity until registry/final integration resolves it. |
| Real expert readiness labels | source not found / claim-limiting | Cannot claim human readiness labels. | Use pseudo-label limitation unless real labels are later documented. |
| Exact repository paths/commands/classes/tests | implementation-detail deferred | Build book needed for execution details. | Do not invent; defer to Implementation Build Book. |

### 17. Definition of done

#### 17.1 Playbook-section definition of done

This generated Phase 6 playbook section is complete when:

- official phase identity and title are preserved;
- source extraction digest is included;
- active layers/modules, scope/non-scope, input contract, procedure, output contract, lifecycle, validation gates, matched keys, A6/A9 obligations, Layer 10 handoff, Layer 0 claim boundaries, failure modes, BPCR handling, and downstream handoff are specified;
- previous Phase 0–5 sections are not modified;
- open issues are visible;
- machine-readable handoff block is complete;
- domain non-interference and final self-audit sections are included.

#### 17.2 Actual Phase 6 execution definition of done

Actual Phase 6 execution is done only when:

1. all required Phase 1–5 inputs validate or affected rows are explicitly blocked/diagnostic-only;
2. split, leakage, source-ID, config-hash, seed, and schema-version lineage is complete;
3. `ReadinessContextRecord` rows exist for eligible rows and exclude forbidden decision-time features;
4. target-construction card/source bundle and pseudo-label/cost artifacts are versioned and leakage-audited;
5. learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` outputs exist with producer/variant/source/target lineage;
6. A6 reliability-vs-coverage, high-confidence-wrong, calibration/ranking, matched comparison, negative-result, diagnostic-only, and metric dictionary obligations are satisfied or downgraded;
7. action-space, alias-map, legality-mask, and cost-model configs validate;
8. supervised Adaptive-IHARQ is trained/selected using train/validation only and evaluated frozen on held-out rows;
9. disabled-update/no-mutation audit status is recorded where update hooks exist or frozen-policy contamination must be ruled out;
10. `PolicyActionRecord` outputs validate and preserve `source_iharq_action` where applicable;
11. A9 action distribution, matched cost/coverage, context/action/cost ablation, negative-result, diagnostic-only, and metric dictionary obligations are satisfied or downgraded;
12. all required baselines are present or missing comparators are explicitly disclosed with limitation/downgrade;
13. every metric has `MetricDictionaryEntry` lineage or is diagnostic-only;
14. Layer 10 source bundles and reproducibility/export inputs are complete;
15. Layer 0 claim-safety labels and forbidden-claim checks are complete;
16. Phase 6 handoff manifest is complete and usable by Phases 7–15 without hidden reinterpretation.

### 0A. Source Extraction Digest

**Architecture facts used:**

- Phase 7 executes the Layer 6 learning-to-defer branch: Layer 6 is the Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer, and submodule 6.3 learns when to route away from direct prediction toward fallback, safer model, request route, no-action/safe-hold, or simulated supervisor proxy. [ARCH: Layer 6 / 6.3 Learning-to-defer]
- `DeferralRecord` is the canonical record family for defer decisions, deferral targets, deferral reasons, fallback availability, direct-versus-defer expected cost, matched coverage group, and simulation-only flags where a supervisor proxy or embodiment route is used. [ARCH: DeferralRecord] [REG: DeferralRecord]
- Phase 7 must preserve Layer 4 stored IHARQ tokens when consuming `IHARQDecisionRecord`; policy-only actions such as `defer` and `no_action` require explicit action-space and alias-map governance rather than replacing upstream tokens. [ARCH: Layer 6 policy action space]
- Layer 6 may use public-EEG proxy readiness-policy evidence, but it may not convert public task labels, decoder correctness, oracle labels, simulated supervisor routes, or future outcomes into clinical readiness labels. [ARCH: Layer 0 claim safety]
- Layer 10 may read, validate, warn, visualize, export, and package Phase 7 records, but it must not train, retune, repair leakage, mutate source records, or turn rendered cards into primary evidence. [ARCH: Layer 10 dashboard/export boundary]
- Capability-tier relevance is C2-primary because learning-to-defer is part of the adaptive policy layer; C0 and C1 are upstream evidence dependencies, while C3/C4 are downstream simulation, stress, embodiment, dashboard, and final-integration contexts only. [ARCH: C0–C4 Stretch C tiers]

**Registry facts used:**

- `ReadinessContextRecord` is a Phase 6 / Layer 6 decision-time context record consumed by Phase 7; it carries source lineage, decision-time cutoff, observable-field set, action-space version, split identity, and upstream prediction/calibration/uncertainty/IHARQ/RegimeRisk/evidence-quality references. [REG: ReadinessContextRecord]
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` can be rule-derived from Layer 4 or learned from Phase 6 / Layer 6; Phase 7 must preserve producer variant, source IDs, target-construction lineage, and validation status when using it as a feature or comparator. [REG: EvidenceQualityRecord]
- `PolicyActionRecord` logs policy identity/family, selected action, action-space version, legality mask, expected cost/reward where applicable, source context, action origin, and claim boundary. Phase 7 may emit deferral-aware rows only where source-supported and legality-mapped. [REG: PolicyActionRecord]
- `DeferralRecord` is produced by Phase 7 / Layer 6 learning-to-defer and consumed by Phase 8, optional downstream policy/stress/embodiment contexts, Layer 10, and final thesis integration. [REG: DeferralRecord]
- `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, `CardRecord`, and `ReproducibilityManifest` provide evaluation, dashboard, audit, and claim-safety governance. [REG: evaluation/dashboard/reproducibility artifacts]
- Exact final controlled vocabularies for `deferral_target` and `deferral_reason`, exact metric dictionary path/schema, and some repository storage homes remain unresolved or require confirmation; Phase 7 must manifest-map or diagnostic-only affected outputs instead of inventing canonical values. [REG: unresolved vocabulary/path/metric issues]

**Execution-plan facts used:**

- Official phase identity is `Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer`; it follows Phase 6 and precedes Phase 8. [EXEC: Phase 7 identity and official order]

### 1. Phase identifier, official phase title, purpose, and thesis role

#### 1.1 Identifier and official title

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 7` |
| Official phase title | `Learning-to-defer` |
| Official predecessor | `Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ` |
| Official successor | `Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness` |
| Primary architecture layer | Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer |
| Primary submodule | 6.3 Learning-to-defer |
| Primary ablation/evaluation linkage | A8 — learning-to-defer / deferral comparison |
| Primary canonical record produced | `DeferralRecord` |

#### 1.2 Purpose

Phase 7 is the routing and fallback baseline gate. Its purpose is to determine whether uncertain, unstable, unsupported, expensive, high-risk, or low-quality decision points should be routed away from direct prediction toward a declared fallback, safer model, request-more-evidence route, wait/no-action/safe-hold route, or explicitly labeled supervisor-proxy route. [ARCH: Layer 6 / 6.3 Learning-to-defer] [EXEC: Phase 7 purpose] [EVAL: A8 scientific question]

#### 1.3 Thesis role

Phase 7 prevents the thesis from treating abstention, rejection, or thresholding as the only response to uncertainty. It produces explicit deferral/routing evidence and asks whether a simpler learning-to-defer baseline is sufficient compared with supervised Adaptive-IHARQ or other adaptive-readiness policies. A baseline-equivalent or simpler-sufficient result remains thesis-relevant and must be reported rather than hidden. [EVAL: A8 baseline sufficiency] [EVAL: negative-result discipline]

#### 1.4 In-scope work

- Declare deferral semantics and keep them distinct from rejection, `uncertain`, wait, request evidence, fallback, no-action, safe-hold, and unsafe outcomes. [EXEC: Phase 7 core tasks]
- Validate Phase 6 context/action/cost/legality inputs without mutating them. [PRIOR: Phase 6 handoff]
- Define deferral targets, route availability, fallback-source assumptions, proxy/oracle/simulation status, cost components, and legality relations. [EXEC: Phase 7 input/output contract]
- Train, select, or instantiate learning-to-defer baselines under split-safe and leakage-safe procedures. [EVAL: A8 split/leakage requirements]
- Emit `DeferralRecord` rows and conditional deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows where supported. [REG: DeferralRecord] [REG: PolicyActionRecord]
- Evaluate A8 under matched cost, matched coverage, request budget, fallback burden, deferral burden, and baseline-sufficiency discipline. [EVAL: A8 matched comparison]
- Prepare Layer 10 source bundles and Layer 0 claim-safety inputs. [ARCH: Layer 10] [ARCH: Layer 0]

#### 1.5 Explicit non-scope

- Phase 7 does not redesign the architecture, redefine A8, rename `DeferralRecord`, or create new canonical records. [FRAME: domain non-interference]
- Phase 7 does not overwrite `ReadinessContextRecord`, `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord`, or `TrustStateRecord`. [FRAME: immutability discipline] [REG: producer-consumer contracts]
- Phase 7 does not produce Phase 8 simulation records: `TransitionRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, or `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`. [EXEC: Phase 7 non-output boundary]
- Phase 7 does not produce stress records, embodiment records, dashboard-rendered evidence, final thesis claims, or deployed/human-in-the-loop clinical evidence. [ARCH: Layer 0] [ARCH: Layer 10]
- Phase 7 does not claim that simulated supervisor proxies are real expert labels unless an actual documented expert source exists. [EVAL: A8 proxy/oracle boundary]

### 8. Artifact immutability and versioning rules

| Artifact/record family | Source records | Phase 7 output/handling | Lineage fields required | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DeferralRecord` | `ReadinessContextRecord`, `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord` where used, fallback definitions, cost config. | New derived/versioned Phase 7 record; never overwrites upstream policy/context/evidence records. | source record IDs, phase ID, ablation ID A8, schema version, run ID, config hash, seed, split ID/role, policy/router ID, action-space version, cost config ID, validation status, claim tags. | Claim-ready only if all gates pass; otherwise diagnostic-only/proxy-only. |
| Deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` | Phase 6 context/action records and Phase 7 router outputs. | Conditional new rows or versioned derivative; upstream Phase 6 rows are not edited. | source context ID, source IHARQ action where applicable, policy ID, action-space version, legality mask, config hash, frozen/update status, validation status. | Claim-ready only with legal action mapping and matched evaluation. |
| `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` / `MatchedComparisonReport` | Phase 7 output records plus A0–A7/A9 comparator records. | New evaluation artifacts with explicit matched keys and exclusions. | matched comparison key, metric dictionary ID, comparator IDs, diagnostic flag IDs, negative-result IDs, source IDs. | Diagnostic-only if unmatched or missing metric dictionary. |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Evaluation outputs and validation reports. | New notes where required; never hidden. | affected phase, affected ablation, source IDs, reason, claim effect. | Required for scientific integrity; can narrow claims. |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Validation failures, leakage checks, missing metrics/keys, proxy misuse. | New validation overlay; does not mutate source records. | affected records, trigger, severity, claim effect, dashboard warning. | Blocks or downgrades affected claims. |
| Deferral target/fallback definitions | Phase 6 cost/action-space context and Phase 7 declared targets. | Versioned config/source-bundle artifact; exact canonical name/path requires confirmation. | config hash, target vocabulary version, reason vocabulary version, fallback source IDs, cost config IDs, proxy/oracle tags. | Required for thesis-ready A8. |
| Layer 10 card/source bundle | Source records and evaluation artifacts. | Source bundle prepared in Phase 7; rendered card deferred to Phase 14. | source record IDs, metric IDs, report IDs, flags, limitations, export manifest references. | Dashboard-ready, not primary evidence. |

Immutability rule: validated upstream records remain read-only. If an upstream record is invalid, stale, missing, or incompatible, Phase 7 must exclude affected rows, mark them diagnostic-only, create versioned derived outputs, or create a BPCR. It must not repair upstream records silently. [FRAME: artifact immutability]

### 9. Validation gates and exit criteria

#### 9.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream input gate | Phase 1–6 source records exist, validate, and join on matched keys. | Block affected rows or mark diagnostic-only. |
| Deferral target gate | Each deferral route has declared target, source type, availability rule, proxy/oracle/simulation status, and legality relation. | `DeferralRecord` blocked for targetless rows; rejection-only results are not A8. |
| Fallback-source gate | Fallback or safer-model source is versioned, split-safe, and not hidden oracle unless tagged analysis-only. | Fallback claims diagnostic-only. |
| Action-space/alias gate | `defer` and `no_action` are policy-only; Layer 4 source tokens are preserved; aliases are mapped. | Invalid action rows diagnostic-only or blocked. |
| Cost-model gate | Direct/defer/fallback/request/wait/no-action costs are versioned and sensitivity/limitation status is reported. | Matched-cost claims blocked if missing. |
| Leakage gate | No true label, decoder correctness, future window, future reward/outcome, or oracle cost is visible as ordinary policy input. | Leakage blocks thesis-ready A8. |
| Split gate | Training/validation/test, subject/session, calibration, target construction, and held-out evaluation boundaries are preserved. | Leakage or unmatched splits make results diagnostic-only. |
| Frozen-evaluation gate | Final A8 comparison uses frozen router/policy outputs on held-out data. | Mixed training/evaluation curves blocked. |
| Baseline sufficiency gate | Required baselines are present or missingness is disclosed. | Claims narrowed if baselines are missing. |
| Matched-comparison gate | Cost, coverage, request budget, fallback burden, and matched lineage are preserved. | Unmatched comparisons diagnostic-only. |
| Metric dictionary gate | Deferral metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references. | Missing metrics diagnostic-only. |
| Negative-result gate | Over-deferral, no benefit, worse cost, baseline-equivalence, unrealistic fallback, and instability are visible. | Hidden negative results block claim use. |
| Layer 10 source-bundle gate | Dashboard/card/export inputs have source IDs, metric IDs, flags, and lineage. | Dashboard readiness blocked. |
| Layer 0 claim-safety gate | Claim tags, proxy/simulation/oracle status, diagnostic flags, and forbidden-claim scan are complete. | Phase 15 claim use blocked. |

#### 9.2 Exit criteria

Phase 7 exits as playbook-complete when this section is appended and audited. Actual Phase 7 exits as execution-complete only when:

- all required upstream Phase 1–6 inputs either validate or are explicitly excluded/downgraded;
- deferral targets, fallback-source definitions, cost configs, action-space/legality masks, and target-construction lineage are versioned;
- `DeferralRecord` outputs exist for eligible rows and validate against registry-required content;
- conditional deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows validate if emitted;
- A8 matched-cost/matched-coverage/burden/baseline-sufficiency reports are generated with metric dictionary references;
- negative results and diagnostic-only flags are exported and visible;
- Layer 10 source bundles and Layer 0 claim-safety inputs are complete;
- Phase 8 receives a clean deferral-policy/action/context handoff without simulation records being pre-created in Phase 7. [EXEC: Phase 7 definition of done]

### 10. Ablation and evaluation obligations

#### 10.1 Directly produced or enabled by Phase 7

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 7 relationship | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A8 | Learning-to-defer / deferral comparison | Directly produced/enabled through `DeferralRecord`, deferral targets, fallback-source logs, matched-cost/matched-coverage comparisons, deferral burden metrics, negative notes, and diagnostic flags. | Claim-ready only if all Phase 7 gates pass; otherwise diagnostic-only/proxy-only. |

#### 10.2 Consumed or preserved comparators

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 7 use |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder baseline | Direct/accept-all comparator and baseline for cost of no deferral. |
| A1 | Calibrated decoder baseline | Calibrated confidence/reliability context and comparator where valid. |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Required simple rejection/threshold comparator under matched operating points. |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Required uncertainty/selective comparator; rejection must not be renamed as deferral without a declared target/cost route. |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Ordinary-control comparator and possible fallback source where valid and declared. |
| A5 | IHARQ-lite | Required interpretable evidence-verification comparator and source of reason codes/fallback/request/unsafe behavior. |
| A6 | IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Feature source and comparator where learned quality records validate; Phase 7 does not produce A6. |
| A7 | IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Conditional temporal-trust context/comparator where Phase 5 records validate; not clinical state evidence. |
| A9 | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Direct Phase 6 comparator for baseline-sufficiency: Phase 7 tests whether simpler deferral explains or matches A9. |

#### 10.3 Downstream ablations prepared but not completed

| Ablation ID | Official identity | Phase 7 role |
|---|---|---|
| A10 | Contextual bandit | Prepares fixed deferral-route/action context for later simulation-bounded immediate-reward adaptation; no update traces or bandit claims. |
| A11 | RL policy | Prepares non-RL deferral baseline and route context; no RL reward/transition/rollout claim. |
| A12 | Stress tests | Prepares clean deferral baseline that can later be stress-conditioned; no stress records. |
| A13 | MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demonstration | Prepares fallback/no-action/hold-compatible deferral route lineage for optional embodiment proxy; no embodiment records or real-control claim. |

#### 10.4 Local A8 sub-ablation policy

Local A8 sub-ablations may be used only as descriptive child variants of `A8`. They are grounded in the v0.1 evaluation protocol, but they remain candidate/local labels until a later final run matrix confirms exact naming, inclusion, seeds, and statistics. They must not become new global ablation IDs and must not introduce `A14`. [EVAL: A8 local sub-ablation policy] [FRAME: single official ablation ladder]

| Local label | Parent global ID | Variant tested | Required Phase 7 handling | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A8.1` | A8 | Confidence-only deferral router | Use calibrated probability/confidence context with declared fallback/cost configuration and matched A2 operating-point lineage. | `inferred_candidate`; requires final run-matrix confirmation. |
| `A8.2` | A8 | Uncertainty-aware deferral router | Add entropy, margin, disagreement, and/or selective-prediction fields only where decision-time legal. | `inferred_candidate`; diagnostic-only if A3 lineage or split legality is missing. |
| `A8.3` | A8 | IHARQ-reason-code deferral router | Add `IHARQDecisionRecord` / `IHARQTraceRecord` action/reason/request/fallback/unsafe context while preserving Layer 4 source tokens. | `inferred_candidate`; alias-map gaps downgrade affected rows. |
| `A8.4` | A8 | Evidence-quality-aware deferral router | Add rule-derived or learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants with producer/phase/variant tags. | `inferred_candidate`; diagnostic-only if A6-compatible lineage fails. |
| `A8.5` | A8 | Regime-aware deferral router | Add causal `RegimeStateRecord` and conditional `TrustStateRecord` fields where Phase 5 validation passes. | Optional; no clinical fatigue/state claim. |
| `A8.6` | A8 | Fallback-source sensitivity | Vary declared fallback source or safer-model route while preserving matched split/cost/source keys. | `inferred_candidate`; fallback assumptions must be disclosed. |
| `A8.7` | A8 | Cost-weight sensitivity | Vary declared cost weights without selecting final weights on held-out outcomes. | Required for cost-superiority claims; otherwise claim-limiting. |
| `A8.8` | A8 | Deferral-target ablation | Separate request-evidence, wait, no-action/safe-hold, fallback, safer-model, and supervisor-proxy routes. | `inferred_candidate`; final target enum unresolved. |

#### 10.5 Metric families to prepare for Layer 10

Phase 7 must prepare metric source data for the A8 learning-to-defer comparison, but it must not finalize table numbering, figure numbering, exact statistical tests, or final run-matrix decisions. Every reported metric must reference a `MetricDictionaryEntry`; otherwise the affected metric row remains diagnostic-only. [EVAL: A8 metric governance] [FRAME: v0.1/final-protocol boundary]

| Metric family | Phase 7 source records / artifacts | Required interpretation | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deferral quality and burden | `DeferralRecord`, deferral target manifest/local vocabulary, reason vocabulary, legality/action-space records | Deferral rate, non-deferral/direct rate, target distribution, reason distribution, over-deferral, no-action/safe-hold, request/wait burden; lower burden is not automatically better unless wrong-accept, coverage, and cost are matched. | Missing target/reason vocabulary, missing denominator, or hidden over-deferral. |
| Fallback/request burden | `DeferralRecord`, fallback-source log/table, cost configuration, IHARQ fallback/request evidence where used | Report fallback rate, fallback-source usage, request-more-evidence burden, fallback-unavailable cases, and missed fallback cases under declared proxy/fallback assumptions. | Missing fallback source, unlicensed/undocumented real-expert fallback, or proxy route not labeled. |
| Coverage and retained performance | `PredictionRecord`, calibration/selective-prediction records, `DeferralRecord`, evaluation labels used only offline | Interpret accepted-trial accuracy, retained error, direct accepted count, and deferred count jointly with cost and wrong-accept. | Unmatched coverage, evaluation labels exposed as decision-time features, or missing matched group. |
| Wrong-accept and high-risk accept | Prediction/calibration/IHARQ/RegimeRisk records, `DeferralRecord`, offline labels | Measure wrong-accept, high-confidence wrong accepted, high-risk accepted error, and accepted error under deferral; never label these as real patient-safety rates. | Missing labels for evaluation, source leakage, or clinical/safety wording. |
| Direct-versus-defer cost | Cost configuration, direct-versus-defer expected-cost table, `DeferralRecord`, matched reports | Report expected direct cost, expected defer cost, realized proxy cost where available, matched-cost delta, and cost-weight sensitivity under declared cost weights. | Unversioned or outcome-selected cost weights; cost model not declared. |
| Matched-coverage / matched-cost delta | `MatchedComparisonReport`, source records, metric references | Compare A8 with A0–A7 and A9 using delta wrong-accept at matched coverage, delta coverage at matched cost, and fallback burden at matched cost. | Required baseline missing, unmatched comparator, or post-hoc operating-point selection. |
| Action distribution and policy stability | `PolicyActionRecord` where emitted, `DeferralRecord`, policy artifact hash, run/seed/config IDs | Report action distribution, action entropy, seed stability, subject/session stability, and collapse-to-defer/collapse-to-direct indicators as reproducibility diagnostics. | Missing seed/config hash, hidden collapsed policy, or unstable policy not flagged. |
| Temporal/regime-aware deferral | `RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, `DeferralRecord` | Optional A7/A8 interaction only: deferral by regime band, stop-loss compliance, and risk-conditioned deferral rate. | Regime/trust records invalid, causal cutoff missing, or clinical fatigue/state claim implied. |
| Dashboard/reproducibility completeness | Layer 10 source bundles, manifests, matched reports, diagnostic flags | Completeness supports auditability and export readiness; it is not empirical superiority evidence. | Missing source IDs, metric dictionary entries, or manifest lineage. |
| Claim-evidence completeness | Layer 0 claim tags, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, claim-evidence/linkage artifacts where defined | Supports final claim review by preserving limitation tags, negative notes, and diagnostic flags. | Missing Layer 0 tags or hidden negative/baseline-equivalent result. |

These metric families refine, rather than replace, the shorter operational list required for dashboard visibility: deferral route distribution, direct-versus-defer cost, matched coverage/cost, fallback/request/wait/no-action burden, unsafe/wrong-accept behavior, retained accepted-case performance, reliability/cost curves, over-deferral diagnostics, stability/sensitivity, RegimeRisk-aware comparisons where valid, and baseline-sufficiency deltas. [EVAL: A8 metric families] [ARCH: Layer 10 read/export role]

#### 10.6 Negative-result interpretation

If learning-to-defer fails, over-defers, is unstable, depends on unrealistic fallback, or does not improve over simpler thresholds/selective prediction/IHARQ-lite/supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, the result must be preserved as a `NegativeResultNote`. If learning-to-defer matches A9 under matched conditions, the thesis claim should be narrowed toward baseline sufficiency rather than upgraded to complex-policy superiority. [EVAL: negative-result discipline] [EVAL: A8 baseline sufficiency]

This subsection makes the framework-required repository/storage expectations explicit without inventing implementation paths, class names, CLI commands, or test-suite names. Where the registry provides only conceptual or unresolved storage homes, Phase 7 must use manifest mapping and keep the item open rather than treating it as a finalized repository contract. [FRAME: repository/storage expectations] [REG: repository/path gaps]

| Local deferral target / reason vocabulary | Store or manifest-map the local controlled vocabulary used for `deferral_target` and `deferral_reason`; include confirmation status and version/hash. | Required because final enum remains unresolved; diagnostic-only if not manifest-mapped. |
| Fallback-source log/table | Store or manifest-map fallback availability, fallback source ID, fallback prediction/source where applicable, fallback cost config ID, proxy/supervisor limitation tag, and split/decision-time legality. | Exact canonical artifact status requires confirmation; no real expert fallback may be implied. |
| Cost configuration and direct-versus-defer table | Preserve cost-model version, cost weights, direct/defer cost fields, selection split, and sensitivity rows where cost-sensitive claims are made. | Outcome-selected or unversioned cost weights downgrade affected comparisons. |
| Policy/action-space artifacts | Preserve action-space version, legality-mask ID, action alias map, deferral policy ID where applicable, and frozen/update-disabled status. | Update-enabled traces remain later-phase/simulation-authorized unless explicitly recorded. |
| Matched-comparison reports | Preserve matched group IDs, comparator IDs, metric dictionary IDs, coverage/cost operating points, and diagnostic-only status. | Missing matched keys makes A8 report diagnostic-only. |
| Layer 10 source bundle | Prepare dashboard-readable source bundles for deferral burden curves, direct-versus-defer cost table, comparator matrix, controller/deferral card, negative-result page, and export manifest. | Dashboard renders later; Phase 7 produces source bundles only. |
| Reproducibility manifest | Include source document/checksum lineage, run/config/seed/hash metadata, schema versions, validation overlays, open issues, and Layer 0/Layer 10 tags. | Required for Phase 14 export and Phase 15 claim-evidence integration. |

Phase 7 must not silently create new repository locations for unresolved artifacts. If an implementation needs a concrete file path that is not canonical, it must be recorded as an implementation-detail deferred item or future build-book decision, not as a Phase Execution Playbook canonical path. [FRAME: domain non-interference] [REG: unresolved storage homes]

### 13. Layer 0 claim-safety handoff

#### 13.1 Allowed claim level after Phase 7

If all gates pass, Phase 7 may support bounded claims such as:

- under declared public-data, split, cost, fallback, and proxy assumptions, learning-to-defer was evaluated as a computational routing baseline;
- deferral/routing behavior was compared against thresholds, selective prediction, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality-aware variants, RegimeRisk-aware context where valid, and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ under matched cost/coverage where possible;
- deferral improved, matched, or failed relative to comparators under explicitly stated limitations.

#### 13.2 Required limitation labels

- public-data-only / proxy-readiness evidence;
- computational deferral/routing baseline;
- simulated supervisor proxy where used;
- oracle-for-analysis-only where used;
- no real expert fallback unless documented;
- no clinical readiness labels;
- no deployed BCI/FES safety validation;
- no real muscle stimulation or assistive-control validation;
- no medical-device, rehabilitation, or patient-safety claim;
- cost-model-dependent result;
- fallback-source-dependent result;
- matched-comparison-dependent result;
- diagnostic-only where gates fail.

#### 13.3 Forbidden overclaims

Phase 7 must not claim:

- clinical triage, real expert handoff, or validated human-in-the-loop safety;
- real patient-safe BCI control, rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation readiness, or medical-device validation;
- that deferral targets are real available supervisors when they are proxies/oracles/simulations;
- that public EEG task labels are readiness labels;
- that cost models are clinically validated utility functions;
- superiority over A0–A7/A9 if matched keys, costs, coverage, fallback burden, or baselines are missing;
- deployment-readiness or online safety from offline Phase 7 evidence;
- Phase 8 closed-loop, Phase 9 stress, Phase 10 bandit, Phase 11 RL, or Phase 12/13 embodiment conclusions.

#### 13.4 Evidence required before stronger claims

Stronger claims require later validated Phase 8 simulation records, Phase 9 stress records where stress is claimed, Phase 10/11 update traces and held-out frozen evaluations for adaptive learning claims, Phase 12/13 embodiment records for optional embodiment-proxy claims, Phase 14 dashboard/export closure, Phase 15 final claim-evidence integration, and Layer 0 approval. [EXEC: downstream phase order]

### 14. Failure modes and diagnostic-only downgrade rules

| Failure / missingness condition | Consequence | Required record/tag |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `ReadinessContextRecord` | Block affected rows. | validation failure. |
| Missing fallback-source definition | `DeferralRecord` blocked or diagnostic-only. | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Deferral target absent or targetless rejection only | Not valid A8 deferral evidence. | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Real expert implied without documented source | Claim blocked. | forbidden-claim flag / limitation tag. |
| Oracle label used as decision-time feature | Leakage; block thesis-ready use. | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`; Layer 0 warning. |
| Future windows/outcomes visible before decision | Leakage; block affected comparison. | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Unversioned cost model | Matched-cost claims blocked. | diagnostic note. |
| No cost sensitivity or limitation disclosure | Claim weakened. | limitation tag. |
| Missing action-space or legality mask | Deferral action invalid. | diagnostic-only/block. |
| `uncertain`, rejection, or threshold non-selection treated as `defer` without target/cost/alias map | Invalid action mapping. | diagnostic-only/block. |
| Over-deferral hides low coverage | Negative result; claim narrowed. | `NegativeResultNote`. |
| Required baselines missing | Claim narrowed or diagnostic-only. | baseline-sufficiency note. |
| Metric dictionary entries missing | Affected metrics diagnostic-only. | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Matched comparison keys missing | Comparison diagnostic-only. | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Mixed Phase 7 frozen results with later update-enabled simulation | Block adaptive-policy claim. | Layer 0 warning. |
| Dashboard outputs used as primary evidence | Invalid. | Layer 10/Layer 0 warning. |
| Clinical/deployment/safety claim attempted | Forbidden. | invalid-claim flag / limitation tag. |

Diagnostic-only trigger vocabulary for Phase 7:

```text
leakage_detected
fallback_source_missing
fallback_source_oracle_only_without_label
unmatched_cost_or_coverage
metric_dictionary_missing
required_baseline_missing
split_boundary_invalid
action_alias_unresolved
deferral_target_vocabulary_missing
cost_model_unversioned
negative_result_hidden
proxy_limitation_missing
dashboard_generated_output_used_as_source
```

### 15. Back-Propagation Correction Request handling

#### 15.1 BPCR rule

If actual Phase 7 execution discovers that an accepted prior phase record is incomplete, inconsistent, stale, invalid, or insufficient for Phase 7, the prior phase text and validated artifacts must not be edited silently. The current Phase 7 execution must either exclude affected rows, mark them diagnostic-only, create a versioned derived overlay, or create a formal Back-Propagation Correction Request. [FRAME: BPCR handling]

#### 15.2 BPCR template

```yaml
back_propagation_request:
  request_id: "BPCR-Phase7-<sequence>"
  discovered_in_phase: "Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer"
  affected_prior_phase: "Phase <N> — <official title>"
  affected_artifact_or_record: "<official record/artifact name>"
  issue_type: "naming_mismatch | missing_record | schema_failure | lineage_gap | matched_key_mismatch | leakage_risk | invalid_status | unsupported_claim | stale_artifact | other"
  severity: "blocking | high | medium | low"
  source_conflict: "<source anchors or not_applicable>"
  downstream_risk: "<risk to Phase 7 and later phases>"
  required_action: "<repair, exclusion, revalidation, versioned overlay, or confirmation>"
  whether_current_phase_can_continue: "yes | yes_with_diagnostic_only_limits | no"
  diagnostic_only_effect: "<affected rows/artifacts/claims>"
  claim_safety_effect: "<Layer 0 consequence>"
```

#### 15.3 Current BPCR status

No formal BPCR is required at playbook-generation time because no actual upstream execution artifact has been validated as defective in this chat. The execution-plan wording ambiguity about Phase 7 versus Phase 8 simulation keys is carried as an open issue and resolved procedurally by following the more specific architecture and phase-specific contracts: Phase 7 produces deferral evidence; Phase 8 produces simulation records. [ARCH: Layer 6/7 boundary] [EXEC: Phase 7 non-output boundary] [EXEC: Phase 8 ownership]

### 17. Handoff to the next phase and later phases

#### 17.1 Handoff to Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness

Phase 8 receives:

- validated `DeferralRecord` IDs and source record IDs;
- conditional deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows;
- `ReadinessContextRecord` IDs used by deferral decisions;
- deferral policy/router ID where applicable;
- action-space version and legality-mask ID;
- deferral target and fallback-source definitions;
- cost config and fallback burden fields;
- matched comparison keys and diagnostic flags;
- proxy/oracle/simulation limitation tags;
- source IDs, split IDs, run IDs, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, and validation status.

Phase 8 must create any `TransitionRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, and `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` itself under its own simulation contract. Phase 7 does not pre-create them. [EXEC: Phase 8 handoff]

#### 17.2 Handoff to Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite

Phase 9 may consume clean Phase 7 deferral-policy/route lineage for clean-versus-stress comparisons after stress profiles and schedules are declared. Phase 7 does not produce stress records. [EXEC: Phase 9 boundary]

#### 17.3 Handoff to Phases 10–11 — Contextual bandit and reinforcement-learning policy

Phases 10–11 may use Phase 7 as a fixed deferral baseline or route/action context. Any update-enabled evidence, reward/transition training, or policy mutation belongs to later phases and must be separated from Phase 7 frozen evaluation through `PolicyUpdateTrace` or disabled-update audit handling where applicable. [REG: PolicyUpdateTrace]

#### 17.4 Handoff to Phases 12–13 — Embodiment demo/replay contexts

Phases 12–13 may consume Phase 7 fallback/no-action/safe-hold/unsafe-compatible route lineage only after intervening simulation/stress phases validate compatibility. Phase 7 does not support real muscle stimulation, real assistive control, rehabilitation, or clinical embodiment evidence. [ARCH: Layer 9 boundary] [ARCH: Layer 0]

#### 17.5 Handoff to Phase 14 and Phase 15

Phase 14 receives dashboard-readable source records, matched reports, metric references, negative notes, diagnostic flags, card source bundles, lineage, reproducibility metadata, and warning inputs. Phase 15 receives bounded claim-evidence pointers, limitation tags, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, matched-comparison status, and open issues. [ARCH: Layer 10] [EXEC: Phase 15 integration]

### 17A. Phase definition of done

Phase 7 is done only when the produced learning-to-defer evidence is traceable, matchable, claim-bounded, and handoff-ready. This definition of done is procedural; it does not assert that the actual experiment has already passed. [FRAME: definition of done] [EXEC: Phase 7 definition of done]

| Completion criterion | Required Phase 7 evidence | Status if unmet |
|---|---|---|
| Required inputs validated | Validated `ReadinessContextRecord`, relevant upstream prediction/calibration/uncertainty/IHARQ/RegimeRisk/evidence-quality records, action-space version, legality-mask ID, cost configuration, fallback definitions, split IDs, and claim tags. | Block affected rows or mark A8 diagnostic-only. |
| `DeferralRecord` produced and validated | Every deferral row has source IDs, decision-time context, deferral target, reason, fallback/cost lineage, matched group, proxy/simulation flag where applicable, and validation status. | A8 evidence incomplete or blocked. |
| Deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows handled | Emitted only where source-supported and legality-mapped; upstream IHARQ tokens preserved through source fields rather than overwritten. | Affected policy rows diagnostic-only; alias gaps visible. |
| Matched-comparison package complete | `MatchedComparisonReport` includes A0–A7/A9 comparators where available, matched cost/coverage keys, required baselines, metric dictionary references, and missingness status. | Superiority/sufficiency claims blocked or diagnostic-only. |
| Metric governance complete | Metric families have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or explicit diagnostic-only labels; denominators and cost weights are not hidden. | Layer 10 and Phase 15 claim use blocked for affected metrics. |
| Negative-result visibility complete | Over-deferral, baseline-equivalent, unstable, high-cost, fallback-missing, null/worse, or missing-baseline outcomes create `NegativeResultNote` / `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` as applicable. | Claim-safety failure; Layer 10 warning required. |
| Layer 10 handoff complete | Source bundles, lineages, validation overlays, card inputs, burden/cost curve source data, matched reports, export metadata, and warnings are prepared without dashboard mutation. | Phase 14 dashboard/export incomplete. |
| Layer 0 handoff complete | Allowed claim level, forbidden claims, limitation labels, diagnostic-only triggers, proxy/simulation/public-data boundaries, and required stronger-evidence conditions are attached. | Thesis-facing claims blocked. |
| Open issues and BPCR status visible | Requires-confirmation items, unresolved registry gaps, inherited ambiguities, and BPCR status are listed in the section and YAML handoff. | Handoff integrity incomplete. |
| Downstream handoff coherent | Phase 8 receives only deferral/action/context/cost/fallback lineage, not pre-created simulation records; later phases receive only bounded downstream context. | Downstream phase must block or downgrade affected inputs. |

Minimum viable Phase 7 consists of validated `DeferralRecord` rows, declared target/reason/fallback/cost lineage, a frozen held-out A8 comparison against the required available baselines, visible negative-result/diagnostic flags, Layer 10 source-bundle readiness, and Layer 0 claim tags. Strong/thesis-ready Phase 7 additionally requires fully matched A0–A7/A9 comparators where available, complete metric dictionary linkage, stable sensitivity/seed reporting, and no unresolved claim-blocking gaps. [EVAL: A8 baseline sufficiency] [ARCH: Layer 0/Layer 10]

### 0A. Source Extraction Digest

**Architecture facts used:**

- Phase 8 is the official implementation phase for `Simulated closed-loop readiness` and is owned architecturally by Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment. It follows Phase 7 and precedes StressForge, contextual bandit, RL, embodiment, dashboard, and final integration phases. [ARCH: Layer 7 / simulated closed-loop readiness] [EXEC: Phase 8 identity]
- Layer 7 runs repeated readiness sessions with state, actions, delayed consequences, reward, declared stress/regime variables, safety events, and policy logs. Its outputs make policy behavior measurable as sequential simulated consequences instead of only static per-window decisions. [ARCH: Layer 7 responsibility]
- Phase 8 must consume but not mutate Layer 1–6 and Phase 7 records. It may replay upstream baseline, calibration, uncertainty, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, Adaptive-IHARQ, and learning-to-defer outputs under declared simulator assumptions. [ARCH: feed-forward contracts] [EXEC: Phase 8 input contract]
- The Layer 7 module inventory includes core replay modules (`EnvironmentConfig Registry`, `SessionBuilder`, `ReplayCursor`, `StateAssembler`, `PolicyAdapter`, `ActionValidator`, `ActionApplier`, `EvidenceRequestManager`, `RewardEngine`, `TransitionLogger`, `PolicyComparisonHarness`, `EnvironmentValidator`), supporting diagnostic/export helpers (`RewardSensitivityRunner`, `SanityCheckRunner`, `EpisodeSummaryBuilder`, `PolicyRolloutExporter`, `SafetyEventExtractor`, `CardGenerator` where source-bundle/card generation is active), and conditional/stretch modules (`PolicyUpdateHook`, `RegimeCoupler`, `StressCoupler`, `EmbodimentGateway`). Conditional modules must not precede clean deterministic replay, transition logging, and frozen-policy validation. [ARCH: Layer 7 module table / implementation roadmap] [REG: Layer 7 module inventory]
- Frozen-policy replay is the default. Update-enabled hooks are disabled or explicitly traced and must not contaminate held-out frozen evaluation. [ARCH: update/frozen separation] [EXEC: Phase 8 frozen/update status]
- Layer 10 may read, validate, warn, visualize, export, and package Phase 8 records, but it must not recompute hidden transition/reward logic, retune policies, mutate records, filter failures, or convert dashboard views into primary evidence. [ARCH: Layer 10 dashboard/export boundary]
- Layer 0 must keep Phase 8 claims simulation-only and must block claims of clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real deployment readiness, or real assistive-control safety. [ARCH: Layer 0 claim-safety ledger]
- Capability-tier relevance is C3-primary because Phase 8 directly strengthens the simulated closed-loop environment; C0–C2 are replayed upstream evidence tiers, and C4 is only prepared through downstream transition/action/safety lineage. [ARCH: C0–C4 Stretch C tiers] [EXEC: Phase 8 capability tiers]
