Phase 8 answers the question: under a declared simulated environment, what downstream consequences appear when upstream readiness policies repeatedly accept, wait, request evidence, combine evidence, fall back, defer, take no action, or block unsafe actions? [EXEC: Phase 8 purpose]

It is the first phase allowed to create Layer 7 transition, reward, session, rollout, episode, and environment-diagnostic records. It must preserve the Phase 7 boundary: Phase 7 owns deferral evidence; Phase 8 owns simulated consequences of using that evidence. [PRIOR: Phase 7 handoff] [EXEC: Phase 8 ownership]

### 1A. Capability-tier and thesis-validity relevance

| Capability tier | Phase 8 relationship | Claim-maturity effect |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Raw decoder, calibrated decoder, threshold, selective, and ordinary-control baselines may be replayed where upstream records exist. | Phase 8 does not redefine C0; it can show simulated consequences of C0-style decisions. |
| C1 | IHARQ-lite and RegimeRisk evidence may be replayed through declared environment/reward rules. | Phase 8 can strengthen interpretation of evidence verification and temporal trust under simulation-only sequential consequences. |
| C2 | Adaptive-IHARQ and learning-to-defer policies may be replayed where Phase 6/7 records exist. | Phase 8 tests whether learned/proxy readiness policies produce useful simulated consequences beyond static metrics. |
| C3 | Phase 8 directly contributes to C3 simulation-environment maturity. | A stable Layer 7 simulator with validated transition/reward/session records, matched comparisons, and frozen/update separation can justify a C3 stopping point. |
| C4 | Embodiment is prepared only through transition/action/safety lineage. | Phase 12/13, not Phase 8, determine C4 embodiment-demo maturity. |

If Phase 8 fails while Phase 6/7 remain valid, the thesis may still stop at C2 with explicit limitation that sequential consequence simulation is incomplete. If Phase 8 succeeds but Phase 10/11/12 are not executed, the thesis may claim simulation-environment readiness, not online adaptation or embodiment success. [EXEC: Phase 8 capability-tier governance]

### 2. Upstream inheritance and continuity check

#### 2.1 Accepted prior-phase content

The accepted Phase 0–7 playbook is immutable upstream material. Phase 8 consumes prior outputs only through read-only source records, versioned configuration references, validation overlays, diagnostic flags, and handoff manifests. No prior phase section is rewritten or corrected here. [FRAME: cumulative behavior] [PRIOR: Phase 0–7 accepted playbook]

#### 2.2 Required inherited foundation

| Upstream phase | Required / conditional Phase 8 inputs | Continuity rule |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 | Schemas, validators, run IDs, seed/config-hash conventions, manifest conventions, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, dashboard/export placeholders, policy-update/no-mutation fixtures. | Missing schemas/validators/config-hash/metric placeholders block or downgrade Phase 8. |
| Phase 1 | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `ArtifactFlagRecord` where available, split manifest, source hashes, temporal/session ordering. | Clean source records are immutable; Phase 8 derives replay sessions without modifying them. |
| Phase 2 | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, baseline predictions, fallback model evidence where used, model IDs, score schemas. | Predictions must join to Phase 1 lineage; no hidden model alias changes. |
| Phase 3 | `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, matched operating points, leakage/eligibility status. | Thresholds and calibration must not be retuned from simulation outcomes. |
| Phase 4 | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, `UnsafeEventRecord`, rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord` where used, action/reason-code taxonomy. | Preserve source IHARQ tokens and reason-code lineage; map non-executable tokens through declared simulator logic only. |
| Phase 5 | `RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, regime timelines, trust scores where applicable, stop-loss warnings. | Use only temporally causal regime/trust fields declared simulation-visible. |
| Phase 6 | `ReadinessContextRecord`, learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, policy IDs, action-space version, legality-mask ID, cost/reward configs, target-construction status, A6/A9 flags. | No labels, future rewards, future windows, future embodiment outcomes, oracle costs, or dashboard metrics in policy-visible state. |
| Phase 7 | `DeferralRecord`, fallback-source logs, deferral target definitions, deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows where emitted, cost/fallback tables, A8 diagnostic flags. | Distinguish deferral from rejection, wait, request-evidence, fallback, no-action, unsafe, and Layer 4 `uncertain` through explicit mapping. |

#### 2.3 Phase 7 handoff consumption

Phase 7 prepared deferral-route and fallback-source evidence without producing Phase 8 records. Phase 8 consumes that package and creates simulation-derived records only after validating action-space version, legality-mask ID, deferral target, fallback availability, cost configuration, matched group, and diagnostic flags. [PRIOR: Phase 7 handoff] [EXEC: Phase 8 continuity]

#### 2.4 Cross-phase continuity issues preserved

| Issue | Affected records | Required Phase 8 handling | Diagnostic-only effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layer 6/7 context boundary | `ReadinessContextRecord`, run-specific state views | Preserve Layer 6 ownership; create only derived/run-specific simulation-visible state linked to source context IDs. | Any row requiring unrecorded reinterpretation is diagnostic-only. |
| Action alias governance | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, `DeferralRecord`, action-space/legality map | Store adapter mapping, action-space version, legality-mask ID, and validation status. | Unresolved or invalid alias maps make affected transitions diagnostic-only. |
| Unsafe versus safety-event boundary | `UnsafeEventRecord`, `SafetyEventRecord` | Preserve evidence-side unsafe outputs separately from simulation-side safety events. | If mapping/storage alias is unresolved, safety summaries are diagnostic-only with warning. |
| Frozen/update separation | `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit, transition update fields | Default to frozen replay; require no-mutation audit; trace any mutation. | Untraced mutation blocks frozen and update-enabled claims. |
| Matched-key and metric dictionary continuity | `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, rollout/session summaries | Preserve matched source/session/reward/config/seed/metric IDs. | Unmatched or undefined metrics remain visible but diagnostic-only. |

### 3. Architecture-grounded phase objective

Phase 8 operational objective is to build a validated, replayable, simulation-only closed-loop readiness environment from saved upstream records. It must: [DERIVED from ARCH/REG/EXEC/EVAL/PRIOR]

1. declare environment, action, reward, cost, session, episode, replay, and update/frozen configurations;
2. build closed-loop sessions from immutable source windows and validated upstream policy/action/deferral records;
3. assemble policy-visible state without future/oracle/dashboard-generated leakage;
4. normalize upstream actions into a declared simulator vocabulary without overwriting source action tokens;
5. validate action legality, budgets, fallback availability, request/wait limits, unsafe/no-action behavior, and simulator constraints;
6. apply declared consequence and reward/cost rules to produce transition and reward records;
7. aggregate transitions into rollout, session, and episode summaries;
8. run environment diagnostics, no-mutation checks, reward consistency checks, and matched comparison checks;
9. preserve negative results, baseline sufficiency, warnings, and diagnostic-only flags;
10. prepare Layer 10 dashboard/export/reproducibility inputs and Layer 0 simulation-only claim-safety handoff.

The objective is not to prove that any policy is clinically safe or deployable. It is to make the simulated consequences of readiness decisions auditable, reproducible, and bounded by explicit assumptions. [ARCH: Layer 0] [EXEC: Phase 8 purpose]

### 3A. Active layers and modules

Phase 8 has one primary execution layer and mandatory governance/handoff layers. The module split below is source-grounded and procedural; it does not create new canonical module names or implementation paths. [ARCH: Layer 7 submodule architecture] [REG: Layer 7 module inventory]

| Layer/module family | Phase 8 role | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Primary execution layer for sessions, replay, state/action/transition/reward logic, rollout comparison, diagnostics, and simulation-only evidence. | Produce only Layer 7 simulation-derived records; never mutate upstream Layer 1–6 or Phase 7 source records. |
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Mandatory claim-boundary gate. | Preserve `simulation_only`, `proxy_readiness`, `evaluation_only`, `diagnostic_only`, non-clinical, non-deployment, non-real-stimulation, and non-real-patient-safety limitations. |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Mandatory read-only consumer/export layer. | Read, warn, visualize, card, and export Phase 8 records without retuning policies, recomputing hidden rewards, filtering failures, or becoming primary evidence. |
| Consumed upstream layers: Layers 1–6 plus accepted Phase 7 | Immutable source lineage for public data, predictions, calibration/uncertainty, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, Adaptive-IHARQ, and deferral/fallback evidence. | Consume by ID, validation status, split role, matched key, diagnostic flag, and claim tag; produce only derived/versioned Phase 8 records. |
| Conditional downstream context: Layer 8 and Layer 9 | Stress and embodiment context only where valid records already exist or later phases consume Phase 8 outputs. | Do not create StressForge or embodiment source evidence in Phase 8. |

| Module | Module class for Phase 8 | Source-grounded function | Phase 8 boundary rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| EnvironmentConfig Registry | Core | Stores environment, reward, episode, action, evidence, stress, embodiment, and policy-comparison settings. | Config changes create new run/config hashes; missing config blocks reproducibility. |
| SessionBuilder | Core | Builds replay sessions from `WindowRecord`, split manifest, metadata, and policy/stress config. | Fails on identifier, split, or session inconsistency. |
| ReplayCursor | Core | Advances through chronological, randomized, stress, or request-driven replay under seed/replay mode. | Must not expose future labels or future windows to policy-visible state. |
| StateAssembler | Core | Assembles simulation-visible context from upstream records and declared observable history. | `ReadinessContextRecord` canonical ownership remains Layer 6; Phase 8 state views are derived/run-specific unless registry confirms otherwise. |
| PolicyAdapter | Core | Normalizes upstream policy/baseline outputs into the Layer 7 action vocabulary. | Cannot overwrite source IHARQ tokens, `PolicyActionRecord`, or `DeferralRecord`. |
| ActionValidator | Core | Checks action legality, budgets, fallback availability, deferral target validity, uncertain-token mapping, stress, and embodiment mode. | Invalid actions must be blocked/mapped/logged, not silently repaired. |
| ActionApplier | Core | Applies validated action and determines declared simulation consequence using scoring-only hidden labels only where allowed. | Hidden labels remain evaluation-only and never policy-visible. |
| EvidenceRequestManager | Core | Handles wait, request-evidence, combine-evidence, request counts, delay, max-request termination, and evidence history. | No unbounded request loop; history changes must be transition-logged. |
| RewardEngine | Core | Computes reward/cost decomposition and reward components. | Reward arbitrariness and sensitivity must be surfaced; rewards update policies only through trace-governed hooks. |
| TransitionLogger | Core | Writes transitions, reward traces, safety events, and diagnostics. | Every step must have one complete transition record or a diagnostic-only failure record. |
| PolicyComparisonHarness | Core | Runs matched policies over identical sessions, seeds, budgets, reward configs, and conditional stress/embodiment contexts. | Unmatched comparisons become diagnostic-only. |
| EnvironmentValidator | Core | Runs invariants, leakage checks, reward consistency checks, no-mutation checks, and sanity experiments. | Failed invariants block thesis-level Phase 8 claims. |
| RewardSensitivityRunner | Supporting | Tests sensitivity of reward/cost interpretation where reward design can alter rankings. | Required for strong Phase 8 when reward rankings are thesis-facing; otherwise mark reward-sensitive outputs. |
| SanityCheckRunner | Supporting | Executes sanity checks for leakage, deterministic replay, invalid actions, reward totals, and impossible transitions. | Failure produces `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` and diagnostic-only overlays. |
| EpisodeSummaryBuilder | Supporting | Builds session/episode aggregate summaries from transition and reward records. | Must link to metric dictionary entries and matched-comparison keys. |
| PolicyRolloutExporter | Supporting | Exports policy rollout source data for evaluation and Layer 10. | Exported views remain derived/read-only and source-linked. |
| SafetyEventExtractor | Supporting | Extracts safety-event summaries where unsafe/blocked/fallback/no-action/safe-hold events are materialized. | Safety summaries require canonical `SafetyEventRecord` or manifest-mapped alias records. |
| CardGenerator | Supporting / Layer 10-adjacent | Converts saved summaries into environment, rollout, safety, reward, and reproducibility cards where this source-supported route is used. | No hidden evidence computation; card outputs are Layer 10/dashboard inputs or derivatives, not primary Phase 8 evidence. |
| PolicyUpdateHook | Conditional / stretch | Provides update feedback for later bandit/RL training/adaptation. | Disabled in frozen evaluation; mutation requires `PolicyUpdateTrace` and separation from held-out frozen curves. |
| RegimeCoupler | Conditional / full-C support | Consumes or forwards `RegimeStateRecord` under declared Layer 5 rules. | Must not duplicate or silently override Layer 5 temporal-trust semantics; loopbacks must be logged. |
| StressCoupler | Conditional / downstream stress support | Applies Layer 8 stress profiles/schedules when stress context is active. | Phase 9 owns stress artifacts; unmatched stress schedules invalidate comparisons. |
| EmbodimentGateway | Conditional / downstream embodiment support | Sends readiness-gated commands to Layer 9 adapter paths and receives saved proxy outcomes. | Phase 12/13 own embodiment evidence; Phase 8 only preserves transition/action/safety lineage. |

Implementation order must prioritize clean deterministic replay and frozen-policy transition logging before update hooks, stress coupling, regime coupling, embodiment gatewaying, or card generation. This is a procedural ordering rule, not a repository/class/CLI specification. [ARCH: Layer 7 implementation roadmap] [FRAME: future Implementation Build Book boundary]

### 4. Input contract

#### 4.1 Required input records and artifacts

| Input family | Required fields / lineage | Validation before use | Diagnostic-only if invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clean source lineage | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id` where available, `window_id`, `split_id`, `split_role`, `preprocessing_id`, `label_map_id`, source hashes, schema/config/run/seed IDs. | Phase 1 schema, split, ordering, source hash, and immutability validation. | Yes. |
| Decoder/model evidence | `prediction_id`, `model_id`, model registry link, score schema, class order, split role, source window IDs. | Phase 2 prediction/model/baseline validation. | Yes. |
| Calibration/uncertainty/selective evidence | `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, uncertainty fields, selective-prediction status, matched operating point. | Phase 3 split/leakage/threshold validation. | Yes. |
| IHARQ evidence | `iharq_decision_id`, source IHARQ action token, reason code, trace ID, fallback/unsafe/request/combine references where present. | Phase 4 token/reason/trace validation. | Yes. |
| RegimeRisk evidence | `regime_state_id`, `TrustStateRecord` link where applicable, stop-loss status, temporal cutoff status. | Phase 5 temporal-causality and cutoff validation. | Yes. |
| Readiness policy context | `readiness_context_id`, observable field set, decision-time cutoff, action-space version, policy-visible fields. | Phase 6 leakage and decision-time visibility validation. | Yes. |
| Policy actions | `policy_action_id`, `policy_id`, action origin, policy family, legality mask, frozen/update mode. | Phase 6 action-space and legality validation. | Yes. |
| Deferral records | `deferral_record_id`, deferral target, reason, fallback source, cost config, matched group. | Phase 7 target/fallback/cost validation. | Yes. |
| Environment config | Environment version, replay mode, state schema, transition rules, done rules, episode definition, simulation-only claim tags. | Phase 0/8 config and schema validation. | Blocking if absent. |
| Reward/cost config | Reward config ID, cost config ID, reward-term version, component definitions, sensitivity status. | Hash validation and reward component-sum validation. | Yes. |
| Delay/request settings | Delay costs, max request count, evidence-request behavior, wait behavior, post-limit fallback/no-action rule. | Config and legality validation. | Yes. |
| Fallback and safety definitions | Fallback availability, fallback source, unsafe-event trigger, safety-event severity vocabulary, response taken. | Alias/path/event-schema validation. | Yes. |
| Held-out simulated sessions | Session split, replay session list, policy-comparison config, held-out/frozen status. | Split and no-tuning validation. | Blocks thesis-ready evaluation if absent. |
| Optional stress inputs | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, clean/stressed pairing ID, stress seed. | Only if stress is active or pre-existing. | Stress claims not ready otherwise. |
| Optional embodiment inputs | `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, command mapping, safety gate, `embodiment_run_id`. | Only for downstream/conditional linkage; not core Phase 8. | Embodiment claims not ready otherwise. |
| Optional update hook config | Update mode, update step, policy update trace ID, disabled-update audit status. | Must be disabled or traced; frozen no-mutation check required. | Untraced mutation blocks claims. |

#### 4A. Entry conditions

Phase 8 may begin only when all of the following conditions are true or explicitly marked as diagnostic limitations:

1. Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundations are available for Layer 7 records, or Phase 8 is explicitly diagnostic-only. [EXEC: Phase 0 inheritance]
2. Phase 1 clean source records, split identities, and replay ordering are immutable and source-hashed. [EXEC: Phase 8 upstream dependency]
3. At least one replayable baseline or upstream readiness policy family has complete source lineage. [EXEC: Phase 8 minimum viable exit]
4. Environment, reward, action, legality, session, episode, replay, and frozen/update configs are versioned and hashable. [REG: Layer 7 config/versioning]
5. Policy-visible state construction excludes labels, future rewards, future windows, future embodiment outcomes, oracle costs, and dashboard-generated metrics. [ARCH: leakage control] [EXEC: forbidden input uses]
6. Phase 7 deferral inputs, if used, have target/fallback/cost/matched-group lineage and diagnostic flags. [PRIOR: Phase 7 handoff]
7. Metric dictionary references exist for all thesis-facing metrics, or affected metrics are pre-labeled diagnostic-only. [REG: MetricDictionaryEntry]
8. Layer 0 limitation tags and Layer 10 source-vs-derived handoff conventions are available. [ARCH: Layer 0 / Layer 10]

#### 4B. Forbidden input uses

Phase 8 must not use true labels, decoder correctness, future reward, future transition/window features, future embodiment outcome, oracle costs, dashboard-generated metrics, post-hoc failure annotations, or final evaluation outcomes as ordinary decision-time state or policy-visible context. These fields may be used only in hidden scoring, validation, or evaluation-only compartments and must be tagged accordingly. [EXEC: Phase 8 forbidden input uses] [ARCH: Layer 6/7 leakage controls]

### 5. Execution procedure

The following procedure is [DERIVED] from the architecture, registry, execution plan, evaluation protocol, and accepted Phase 7 handoff. It is procedural playbook guidance, not a replacement for future Detailed Design / Nuts-and-Bolts or Implementation Build Book specifications.

#### Step 1 — Lock Phase 8 identity, authority, and non-scope

Confirm that the active section is `Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness`; record source-document versions/checksums; import the accepted Phase 0–7 handoff as immutable prior material; and record non-scope boundaries for stress, contextual bandit, RL, embodiment, dashboard rendering, final thesis claims, and clinical/deployment claims. [FRAME: cumulative behavior] [EXEC: Phase 8 identity]

#### Step 2 — Validate Phase 0 inheritance

Check schemas, validators, config families, run IDs, seed rules, config-hash rules, manifest conventions, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, dashboard/export placeholders, and update/no-mutation fixtures for all Phase 8 record families. Missing schema/config/run/hash/seed/validator foundations block thesis-ready Phase 8 and may allow diagnostic-only exploratory records. [EXEC: Phase 0 inheritance]

#### Step 3 — Build the immutable upstream input inventory

Create an inventory of consumed Phase 1–7 records and artifacts, including clean source lineage, prediction/model evidence, calibration/uncertainty/selective/threshold outputs, IHARQ evidence, RegimeRisk/trust context, readiness policy context/actions, and deferral/fallback outputs. The inventory must include source IDs, split roles, validation status, diagnostic flags, matched keys, and claim tags. [EXEC: Phase 8 upstream dependency]

#### Step 4 — Declare environment, reward, action, replay, and session configuration

Version and hash the environment config, reward/cost config, action-space map, legality mask, delay/request/fallback/no-action/unsafe rules, session/episode definitions, replay mode, held-out session plan, policy comparison config, and frozen/update mode. Do not proceed to thesis-ready transition generation without these hashes. [ARCH: EnvironmentConfig Registry] [REG: config/versioning discipline]

#### Step 5 — Construct closed-loop sessions from immutable source windows

Use SessionBuilder and ReplayCursor behavior to convert eligible source windows into `ClosedLoopSessionRecord` and replay order/session manifests. Preserve dataset, subject, session, trial/window, split, preprocessing, label-map, run, seed, and config lineage. Do not alter the clean source records or split assignments. [ARCH: SessionBuilder / ReplayCursor] [REG: ClosedLoopSessionRecord]

#### Step 6 — Assemble simulation-visible state with leakage controls

Use StateAssembler behavior to create simulation-visible state from `ReadinessContextRecord` and allowed prior context. Exclude hidden labels, future reward, future windows, future embodiment outcome, oracle costs, dashboard-generated metrics, and post-hoc failure annotations from policy-visible fields. Any evaluation-only target fields must remain compartmentalized. [ARCH: StateAssembler] [EXEC: forbidden input uses]

#### Step 7 — Normalize policy and baseline actions without mutating source tokens

Use PolicyAdapter behavior to map upstream raw decoder replay, threshold/selective replay, IHARQ tokens, RegimeRisk-aware policies, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ actions, and learning-to-defer routes into the declared Layer 7 action vocabulary. Preserve `source_iharq_action`, `policy_action_id`, `deferral_record_id`, action origin, action-space version, legality-mask ID, and adapter mapping. Do not rewrite upstream records. [ARCH: PolicyAdapter] [REG: action alias governance]

#### Step 8 — Validate action legality, budgets, fallback availability, and unsafe/no-action rules

Use ActionValidator behavior to check action-space version, legality mask, budget state, fallback availability, request count, wait/delay limits, deferral target validity, no-action/safe-hold rules, unsafe blocking, and simulator constraints. Invalid actions must be blocked, mapped to a declared diagnostic route, or marked diagnostic-only with `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` and `SafetyEventRecord` linkage where materialized. [ARCH: ActionValidator] [REG: EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord / SafetyEventRecord]

#### Step 9 — Apply declared consequences and evidence-request behavior

Use ActionApplier and EvidenceRequestManager behavior to apply validated actions to the declared simulation consequence logic. Handle wait, request_evidence, combine_evidence, fallback, deferral, no-action, unsafe-block, delay cost, evidence budget, max-request termination, and post-limit fallback/no-action behavior exactly as configured. True labels may be used only for scoring/evaluation where permitted, not policy-visible state. [ARCH: ActionApplier / EvidenceRequestManager]

#### Step 10 — Compute reward/cost traces and preserve reward-design dependence

Use RewardEngine behavior to compute `RewardTraceRecord` entries from transition context, reward config, cost config, reward-term version, and component definitions. Validate that components sum to reported totals; record reward-design dependence, sensitivity status, and diagnostic flags when reward rankings are unstable or unversioned. [ARCH: RewardEngine] [REG: RewardTraceRecord] [EVAL: reward/cost metric discipline]

#### Step 11 — Emit transition, reward, safety, and diagnostic records

Use TransitionLogger behavior to emit `TransitionRecord` rows with source state, validated action, optional source IHARQ action, mapped simulator command where applicable, next-state pointer, reward link, done flag, safety-event link where materialized, stress/embodiment fields only where valid, update-trace link where applicable, schema version, run/config/seed IDs, source IDs, validation status, and claim tags. Emit `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` for invalid, incomplete, anomalous, unmatched, or diagnostic-only outcomes. [REG: TransitionRecord / EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord]

#### Step 12 — Aggregate rollouts, sessions, and episodes

Use PolicyComparisonHarness and evaluation-export behavior to create `PolicyRolloutRecord` and `EpisodeSummaryRecord` entries with policy identity, policy family, frozen/update mode, action sequence pointers, transition pointers, reward-trace pointers, evidence-request/delay/fallback/deferral/no-action/unsafe summaries, matched-comparison keys, metric dictionary IDs, diagnostic flags, and claim boundaries. [REG: PolicyRolloutRecord / EpisodeSummaryRecord]

#### Step 13 — Run frozen-policy no-mutation and update-trace checks

Verify that held-out frozen replay contains no policy parameter mutation. If update hooks are configured but disabled, write disabled-update audit status. If mutation occurs or `policy_update_trace_id` is present, require valid `PolicyUpdateTrace` linkage and separate update-enabled/adaptation curves from held-out frozen evaluation. Untraced mutation makes affected evidence diagnostic-only or blocked. [ARCH: update/frozen separation] [REG: PolicyUpdateTrace]

#### Step 14 — Build matched comparisons and baseline-sufficiency outputs

Create Phase 8 `MatchedComparisonReport` entries for selected policy families under matched source lineage, replay sessions, reward/cost configs, action legality constraints, seeds, frozen/update modes, metric dictionary entries, warnings, and claim tags. Preserve available comparisons among A0–A9 contexts and record missing baselines as baseline-sufficiency limitations or `NegativeResultNote` entries. [EXEC: Phase 8 matched comparison] [EVAL: baseline sufficiency]

#### Step 15 — Produce evaluation records, negative-result notes, and diagnostic-only overlays

Create Phase 8 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, metric references, baseline-sufficiency table, reward/cost curve source data, action-distribution trajectory source data, safety-event summary where materialized, environment diagnostic report, `NegativeResultNote`, and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` outputs. Negative or null results must remain visible and must not be overwritten by later phases. [REG: evaluation artifacts] [EVAL: negative-result discipline]

#### Step 16 — Prepare Layer 10 dashboard/reproducibility/export source bundles

Prepare dashboard-readable record inventory, warning inputs, closed-loop environment card source bundle, policy rollout card source bundle, figure/table manifest input, and `ReproducibilityManifest` input. Explicitly separate source records from later Layer 10 generated views/cards/exports. [ARCH: Layer 10] [EXEC: Phase 8 Layer 10 obligations]

#### Step 17 — Prepare Layer 0 claim-safety handoff

Attach required limitation tags, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result pointers, reward-design dependence, simulation-only warnings, forbidden-claim checks, and capability-tier status. Block any wording that implies clinical validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real deployment readiness, or real assistive-control safety. [ARCH: Layer 0] [EXEC: Phase 8 claim boundaries]

#### Step 18 — Assemble downstream handoff package

Create the Phase 8 handoff manifest for Phase 9–15 with validated record paths or manifest-mapped equivalents, source lineage, policy families, environment/reward/action/session config hashes, held-out session definitions, frozen/update status, transition/reward/session/rollout paths, safety-event paths where materialized, diagnostic and negative-result paths, metric dictionary references, matched-comparison reports, Layer 10 source-bundle references, and Layer 0 claim tags. [EXEC: downstream handoff]

### 6. Output contract

#### 6.1 Produced records and artifacts

| Output | Output class | Source records | Claim status if valid | Diagnostic-only condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TransitionRecord` | Canonical simulation-derived record | Phase 1–7 source records, policy/action/context/deferral records, environment/reward configs. | Simulation-only transition evidence. | Missing source/action/reward/next-state lineage, invalid action, impossible transition, or missing claim tags. |
| `RewardTraceRecord` | Canonical reward/cost metric record | `TransitionRecord`, reward/cost configs, policy/action/session IDs. | Simulation-only reward/cost evidence. | Component mismatch, unversioned reward, missing transition link, hidden reward tuning. |
| `ClosedLoopSessionRecord` | Canonical session metadata record | Source windows/splits, environment/session configs, policy IDs, seeds. | Replay/session reproducibility evidence. | Missing split/seed/config/session definition or source immutability failure. |
| `PolicyRolloutRecord` | Canonical rollout/evaluation artifact | `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, policy/action records. | Simulation-only rollout evidence. | Missing transitions, reward traces, action sequence, matched key, or frozen/update status. |
| `EpisodeSummaryRecord` | Canonical aggregate metric summary | Rollout/session/reward/safety records and metric dictionary references. | Thesis-facing summary only if matched and metric-defined. | Missing metric dictionary, unmatched comparison, hidden warnings, missing diagnostic flag. |
| `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` | Validation report / warning log record | All Phase 8 configs and outputs. | Diagnostic/validation evidence. | Always visible; failed gates downgrade affected outputs. |
| `SafetyEventRecord` | Canonical warning/failure log where materialized | Action validation, transition events, unsafe/fallback/no-action/safety triggers. | Simulation-only safety-event warning evidence. | Claimed safety events not logged or only unmapped CSV/log aliases. |
| Optional `PolicyUpdateTrace` | Conditional update trace/audit artifact | Update-enabled runs or transitions with mutation. | Only update-enabled diagnostic/support evidence for later phases. | Missing where mutation occurs; mixed with frozen evaluation. |
| Disabled-update audit entry | Conditional audit artifact | Configured update hooks with frozen evaluation. | No-mutation support. | Missing when update hooks exist. |
| Phase 8 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Evaluation artifact | Simulation records, matched reports, metric definitions. | Bounded simulation outcome evidence. | Missing validation, matched keys, metrics, or claim tags. |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | Evaluation artifact | Matched rollouts/sessions/rewards/policy families. | Thesis-facing comparison if matched. | Unmatched sessions, configs, seeds, frozen/update modes, or metric definitions. |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Metric governance artifact | Metric definitions and produced outputs. | Metric interpretation support. | Missing or unresolved metric definitions. |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Evaluation/claim-safety artifact | Evaluation outcomes and diagnostics. | Required evidence of honest negative/null/failure outcomes. | Missing when negative or baseline-sufficiency findings occur. |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Validation/claim-safety overlay | Affected records and gates. | Blocks claim use while preserving artifact. | Required when any diagnostic-only trigger occurs. |
| Card source bundles | Layer 10 source input | Phase 8 records, warnings, metrics, configs, matched reports. | Dashboard/export input only. | Source-vs-derived boundary broken. |
| Figure/table manifest input | Export lineage artifact | Records/configs/metrics/source tables. | Phase 14/15 export support. | Missing checksums/source pointers. |
| `ReproducibilityManifest` input | Reproducibility artifact | All run/config/seed/source/validator metadata. | Audit/replay support. | Missing run/config/seed/source lineage. |

#### 6.2 Output exclusions

Phase 8 must not produce the following as official Phase 8 outputs:

- `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifest, or stress robustness evidence, unless they already exist as external/conditional inputs; Phase 9 owns these. [EXEC: Phase 9 handoff]
- Contextual-bandit update evidence or A10 final results; Phase 10 owns these. [EXEC: Phase 10 handoff]
- Reinforcement-learning policy evidence or A11 final results; Phase 11 owns these. [EXEC: Phase 11 handoff]
- `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, `Layer9RewardTrace`, embodiment demo manifest, or embodiment success evidence; Phase 12/13 own these. [EXEC: Phase 12/13 handoff]
- Rendered final dashboard pages, final thesis figures/tables, or final paper claims; Phase 14/15 own these. [FRAME: domain non-interference]

### 7. Artifact lifecycle matrix

| Artifact / record | Producer in Phase 8 | Mutability after validation | Versioning / lineage requirement | Layer 10 status | Layer 0 status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upstream Phase 1–7 source records | Prior phases | Immutable read-only | Referenced by source IDs and validation status. | Dashboard-readable only where source-supported. | Claim limitations inherited. |
| Environment/reward/action/session configs | Phase 8 / Layer 7 configuration process | Versioned, not overwritten | Config hash, schema version, producer, claim tags. | Export/reproducibility input. | Reward-design and simulation-only limitation required. |
| `ClosedLoopSessionRecord` | SessionBuilder | Immutable after validation; new version for config changes | Source windows, split/session IDs, seed, replay mode, environment/reward/action/evidence hashes. | Session timeline source. | Simulation-only session evidence. |
| `TransitionRecord` | TransitionLogger | Immutable after validation; new run/version for repairs | State/action/next-state/reward/source IDs, config hash, validation status, claim tags. | Transition trajectory source. | Simulation-only; diagnostic if invalid. |
| `RewardTraceRecord` | RewardEngine | Immutable per reward config; new version for reward changes | Reward config/cost config/reward-term version, component sums, source transition IDs. | Reward/cost curve source. | Reward-design dependent; diagnostic if component failure. |
| `PolicyRolloutRecord` | PolicyComparisonHarness | Immutable per run/config; new version for rerun | Policy family, frozen/update mode, action sequence, transition/reward links, matched key. | Policy rollout card source. | Bounded simulation evidence only. |
| `EpisodeSummaryRecord` | Evaluation reporter / PolicyComparisonHarness | Immutable per metric dictionary/config | Metric dictionary ID, matched key, diagnostic flag, reward/cost/safety summary. | Table/card source. | Claim-ready only if matched and metric-defined. |
| `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` | EnvironmentValidator | Append-only validation overlay | Failed invariants, invalid actions, leakage checks, update/no-mutation status. | Warning panel source. | Claim downgrade/control evidence. |
| `SafetyEventRecord` | ActionValidator/ActionApplier/TransitionLogger/EnvironmentValidator where materialized | Append-only or versioned by safety config | Event ID, source policy/action/transition IDs, severity, response, simulation step. | Safety-event panel source. | Simulation-only safety warning, not real patient safety. |
| Optional `PolicyUpdateTrace` | Conditional update hook | Append-only trace; separated from frozen evaluation | Update ID, policy/source/action/reward/session links, update mode. | Update trace card source only. | Blocks claims if missing where mutation occurs. |
| Evaluation reports and notes | Phase 8 evaluation exporter | Immutable once exported; corrections become new reports or overlays | Source records, matched keys, metrics, diagnostics, limitation tags. | Dashboard metric/export input. | Claim-evidence input only if valid. |
| Card/figure/reproducibility source bundles | Phase 8 source-bundle assembly | Versioned by source manifest | Paths/checksums/source IDs/config IDs/metric IDs/warnings. | Layer 10 may render derived outputs later. | Claim warnings must propagate. |

### 7A. Artifact immutability and versioning rules

- Validated upstream records remain immutable. Phase 8 must not silently overwrite or repair `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `PredictionRecord`, `CalibrationRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord`, `ReadinessContextRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, or `DeferralRecord`. [FRAME: immutable discipline] [REG: producer-consumer contracts]
- Phase 8 outputs are simulation-derived and run-scoped. Any correction to environment, reward, action, session, replay, legality, or update/frozen configuration creates a new run/config version rather than mutating prior records. [REG: versioning]
- Derived outputs must include source records, config hashes, seed, schema version, validation status, claim tags, and diagnostic-only status where applicable. [REG: lineage envelope]
- Dashboard cards, figures, tables, and exports are derived Layer 10 products unless explicitly source-bundled; they must link back to Phase 8 source records and must not become primary evidence. [ARCH: Layer 10]
- Claim-ready status requires complete lineage, matched comparison keys, metric dictionary references, no hidden leakage, no untraced mutation, no unresolved claim-blocking aliases, and Layer 0 limitation tags. Otherwise the output is diagnostic-only or stretch-only. [EXEC: Phase 8 gates]

### 8. Validation gates and exit conditions

#### 8.1 Validation gates

| Gate | Pass condition | Failure effect |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream completeness gate | Required Phase 1–7 source records exist or missing families are explicitly excluded with baseline-sufficiency notes. | Affected policy family unavailable or diagnostic-only. |
| Clean-source immutability gate | Phase 8 creates derived records without overwriting clean source records. | Blocks thesis-ready Phase 8. |
| Schema and lineage gate | All Phase 8 records validate required fields, IDs, source links, run/config/seed/schema fields, and claim tags. | Invalid records retained only as diagnostics. |
| Split and decision-time visibility gate | No hidden labels, future reward, future windows, future embodiment outcomes, oracle costs, or dashboard metrics in policy-visible state. | Blocks policy/simulation claims. |
| Environment config gate | State/action/reward/episode/done/replay/update/frozen definitions are declared and hashed. | Blocks Phase 8 evidence. |
| Action legality gate | Actions validate against action-space version, legality mask, budgets, fallback availability, and simulator constraints. | Invalid transitions diagnostic-only. |
| Reward consistency gate | Reward terms sum correctly and link to reward config/cost config/reward-term version. | Reward comparisons diagnostic-only. |
| Transition completeness gate | Every step has state hash, validated action, next-state pointer, reward trace link, source IDs, and validation status. | Transition/rollout not thesis-ready. |
| Session and episode gate | Sessions/episodes have definitions, split/held-out status, policy IDs, environment config, seed, and replay mode. | Session/episode summaries not thesis-ready. |
| Safety-event gate | `SafetyEventRecord` exists whenever safety events are materialized or claimed. | Safety-event summaries diagnostic-only. |
| Frozen-policy no-mutation gate | Held-out frozen replay has no policy parameter mutation. | Blocks frozen-policy claims. |
| Policy-update trace gate | Any mutation or `policy_update_trace_id` has valid `PolicyUpdateTrace`; disabled hooks have disabled-update audit status. | Blocks update-enabled and/or frozen-policy claims if violated. |
| Held-out evaluation gate | Simulator parameters and policies are not tuned on final evaluation outcomes. | Blocks thesis-ready evaluation. |
| Matched-comparison gate | Policy families are compared under matched sessions, reward/cost config, seeds, baseline set, and compatible lineage. | Unmatched reports diagnostic-only. |
| Metric dictionary gate | All reported metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references. | Metric/report diagnostic-only. |
| Negative-result gate | Failures, baseline sufficiency, reward sensitivity, invalid simulator assumptions, and missing evidence are recorded. | Blocks honest thesis integration if missing. |
| Dashboard boundary gate | Layer 10 inputs are source records or explicit warning inputs; derived views/cards/exports are not primary evidence. | Blocks Phase 14 thesis-ready export. |
| Layer 0 claim-safety gate | Simulation-only and forbidden-claim tags are present. | Blocks claim use. |

#### 8.2 Exit criteria

Phase 8 exits successfully when the simulator can replay selected simpler and upstream readiness policy families before any learned online policy is claimed. Required exit evidence includes:

- `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, and `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` for each selected policy family;
- `SafetyEventRecord` wherever safety events are materialized or claimed;
- stable/versioned state/action/reward/done/episode definitions;
- declared held-out simulated sessions;
- frozen-policy no-mutation evidence;
- disabled-update audit or valid `PolicyUpdateTrace` where update hooks exist;
- matched-comparison reports and metric dictionary references for thesis-facing summaries;
- negative-result notes, baseline-sufficiency notes, limitation tags, and diagnostic-only flags where applicable;
- Layer 10 source-bundle and reproducibility/export manifest inputs;
- Layer 0 simulation-only claim-safety handoff. [EXEC: Phase 8 exit condition]

#### 8.3 Minimum viable Phase 8

A minimum viable Phase 8 may exclude stress and embodiment branches. It must include deterministic or seed-logged replay, stable environment and reward configs, at least one simpler baseline policy family, at least one upstream readiness policy family where available, complete transition/reward/session/rollout records, environment diagnostics, no-mutation evidence, matched comparison keys, metric dictionary references, and simulation-only claim tags. [EXEC: Phase 8 minimum viable exit]

#### 8.4 Strong / thesis-ready Phase 8

A strong Phase 8 additionally includes multiple policy families across A0–A9 contexts, reward sensitivity analysis, action-distribution trajectories, safety-event summaries where materialized, deferral/fallback/request/delay burden analysis, subject/session generalization summaries, multiple seeds where stochastic, baseline-sufficiency discussion, complete Layer 10 card/export source bundles, and complete Layer 0 claim-evidence linkage. [EXEC: Phase 8 strong exit]

#### 8.5 Layer 7 readiness checkpoints as non-canonical internal validation markers

The architecture describes Layer 7 readiness levels as implementation-readiness markers. They are not official phase IDs, not global ablation IDs, and not canonical artifacts. Phase 8 may use them only as internal validation checkpoints. [ARCH: Layer 7 readiness levels] [REG: local labels non-authoritative]

| Internal readiness checkpoint | Phase 8 interpretation | Claim effect |
|---|---|---|
| L7-RL2 | State/action/transition/reward schemas exist. | Enables schema-level preparation only; no consequence claim. |
| L7-RL3 | Clean replay works. | Minimum replay demonstration; still not thesis-level policy-comparison evidence. |
| L7-RL4 | Evidence dynamics work. | Supports request/wait/combine/fallback/delay behavior inspection if diagnostics pass. |
| L7-RL5 | RegimeRisk state is included where declared. | Enables regime-aware simulation summaries only when Layer 5 lineage is valid. |
| L7-RL6 | Matched policy comparison works. | Minimum checkpoint for major Phase 8 simulation-comparison claims. |
| L7-RL8 | Bandit/RL can train or evaluate inside the environment with update traces and frozen evaluation separated. | Required before Phase 10/11 adaptive-policy claims can be considered; Phase 8 itself still only prepares A10/A11. |
| L7-RL9 | Layer 9 adapter can receive readiness-gated commands. | Required before embodiment-linked claims; Phase 12/13 own embodiment evidence. |
| L7-RL10 | Metrics, ablations, cards, limitations, and reproducibility package are complete. | Supports Phase 14/15 export readiness when all source records and claim tags validate. |

Phase 8 must not use readiness checkpoints to hide failed validation gates. A run below L7-RL6 can still be useful diagnostically, but it cannot support thesis-ready matched simulation-comparison claims. [ARCH: Layer 7 claim maturity]

### 9. Matched-comparison key preservation

#### 9.1 Required matched-comparison key fields

Phase 8 comparisons must preserve fields sufficient to ensure competing policies are replayed under the same evidence and environment conditions:

```text
matched_comparison_key
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id where available
window_id or episode source window range
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
policy_id
policy_family
action_space_version
legality_mask_id
reward_config_id
cost_config_id
environment_config_id
episode_definition_id
replay_mode
run_id
config_hash
seed
phase_id
ablation_id where applicable
regime_state_id where applicable
deferral_record_id where applicable
stress_profile_id where applicable
stress_schedule_id where applicable
embodiment_run_id where applicable
frozen_or_update_mode
policy_update_trace_id where applicable
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
```

[EXEC: Phase 8 matched key] [EVAL: matched-comparison discipline]

#### 9.2 Matched comparison rules

| Rule | Requirement | Diagnostic-only condition |
|---|---|---|
| Same clean source lineage | Compared policies share the same source dataset/window/session/split lineage. | Missing or mismatched source IDs. |
| Same replay session | Compared rollouts use the same episode/session definition. | Different episode boundaries without matched mapping. |
| Same reward/cost definition | Reward config is identical for direct policy ranking, or comparison is labeled reward-sensitivity analysis. | Unversioned or changed reward config. |
| Same action legality constraints | Policies use compatible action-space and legality-mask versions. | Missing legality-mask ID or incompatible action spaces. |
| Same frozen/update mode | Frozen policies compare only with frozen policies; update-enabled curves are separate. | Mixed frozen and update-enabled curves. |
| Same stress/embodiment condition where claimed | Stress or embodiment-linked comparisons require matched stress/embodiment IDs. | Missing paired condition or hidden stress/embodiment branch. |
| Same metric dictionary | Reported metrics use shared metric definitions. | Missing metric dictionary ID. |
| Same warning/claim status | Diagnostic-only and limitation tags remain visible. | Warnings hidden or overwritten. |

#### 9.3 Baseline family matching

Phase 8 must preserve matched comparisons among available policy families, including:

- accept-all / raw decoder replay;
- confidence-threshold replay;
- selective-prediction replay;
- longer-window / voting / ordinary ensemble controls where upstream records exist;
- IHARQ-lite replay;
- IHARQ plus evidence-quality estimator replay;
- RegimeRisk-aware replay where valid regime records exist;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ replay;
- learning-to-defer replay;
- later contextual-bandit/RL-compatible environment baselines without claiming Phase 10/11 results.

If a baseline is unavailable, Phase 8 must write a baseline-sufficiency note, negative-result note, or diagnostic-only limitation rather than hiding the missing comparison. [EVAL: baseline sufficiency]

### 10. Ablation and evaluation obligations

#### 10.1 A0–A13 evaluation-use linkage

A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata only. They do not own Phase 8 artifacts. Phase 8 creates Layer 7 simulation records that may be used by evaluation contexts.

| Evaluation context | Phase 8 relationship | Artifact linkage / handling |
|---|---|---|
| A0 — raw decoder baseline | May be replayed as accept-all/direct baseline where Phase 2 predictions exist. | `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, matched report. |
| A1 — calibrated decoder baseline | May be replayed as calibrated confidence policy where Phase 3 records exist. | Same Phase 8 records plus calibration lineage. |
| A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | May be replayed as registered-threshold/confidence-threshold baseline. | Same Phase 8 records plus threshold registry lineage. |
| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | May be replayed if uncertainty/selective-prediction outputs exist. | Same Phase 8 records plus uncertainty/selective operating-point lineage. |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | May be replayed as ordinary evidence-aggregation controls. | Same Phase 8 records plus longer-window/ensemble/voting lineage. |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Replayed from Phase 4 decisions. | Same Phase 8 records plus IHARQ decision/trace lineage. |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Replayed where Phase 6 learned evidence-quality outputs exist. | Same Phase 8 records plus evidence-quality lineage; Phase 8 does not own A6. |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Replayed where Phase 5 regime/trust context exists. | Same Phase 8 records plus regime/trust lineage. |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Replayed from Phase 7 deferral records. | Same Phase 8 records plus deferral/fallback lineage; Phase 8 does not own A8. |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Replayed where Phase 6 supervised policy actions exist. | Same Phase 8 records plus policy/action lineage; Phase 8 does not own A9. |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Prepared, not produced, as a Phase 8 policy result. | Stable transition/reward/session definitions, held-out session plan, no-mutation/trace audit. |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Prepared, not produced, as a Phase 8 policy result. | Stable delayed-consequence environment, reward/done logic, update/frozen separation. |
| A12 — stress tests | Prepared through stable simulator handoff only. | Stress profiles and stress-conditioned comparisons are Phase 9-owned. |
| A13 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demonstration | Prepared through transition/action/safety lineage only. | Embodiment demo evidence is Phase 12/13-owned. |

#### 10.2 Evaluation artifacts and metrics prepared

Phase 8 directly produces or links:

- Phase 8 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` for selected policy-family replay outcomes;
- Phase 8 `MatchedComparisonReport` for simulation-policy comparisons;
- `MetricDictionaryEntry` references for reward/cost, delay, evidence-request burden, fallback burden, deferral burden, no-action burden, unsafe/safety-event summaries, rollout/session completeness, action distributions, regret/reward where used, and diagnostic counts;
- reward/cost curve source data;
- action-distribution trajectory source data;
- safety-event summaries where materialized;
- environment diagnostic reports;
- baseline-sufficiency tables;
- `NegativeResultNote` and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` outputs;
- card source bundles and reproducibility/export manifest inputs. [EXEC: Phase 8 explicit evaluation artifacts]

#### 10.3 Evaluation interpretation rule

Phase 8 may show that a policy behaves better, worse, or similarly under a declared simulation environment. It may not generalize that behavior to real deployment, real patient safety, real muscle stimulation, or real rehabilitation. If simpler baselines match stronger policies under matched simulation, that is a valid negative or baseline-sufficiency result and must be preserved. [EVAL: negative-result discipline] [ARCH: Layer 0]

### 12. Claim-safety and limitation boundaries

#### 12.1 Allowed claim classes after Phase 8

Phase 8 may support bounded claims about:

- simulation-only closed-loop readiness replay;
- sequential consequence analysis under declared environment assumptions;
- reward/cost visibility for readiness actions;
- delay, request-count, fallback, deferral, no-action, and unsafe-event burden under simulation;
- comparison of policy families under matched simulated sessions;
- frozen-policy replay and no-mutation evidence;
- readiness of the simulator as a prerequisite for later contextual bandit/RL experiments;
- reproducibility of simulated transition/reward/session records;
- dashboard/readiness traceability for closed-loop simulation evidence. [EXEC: allowed claims]

#### 12.2 Forbidden claim classes after Phase 8

Phase 8 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real human supervisor fallback unless an explicit licensed/approved source exists, which is not assumed here;
- contextual bandit or RL policy superiority before Phase 10/11 evidence exists;
- stress robustness before Phase 9 evidence exists;
- MyoSuite/OpenSim embodiment success before Phase 12/13 evidence exists. [ARCH: Layer 0 forbidden claims]

#### 12.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 8 records, summaries, cards, exports, and claim-evidence entries must include relevant tags:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol where inherited
proxy_readiness
simulation_only
evaluation_only
computational_policy_only
reward_design_dependent
pseudo_label_based where inherited from upstream target construction
fallback_proxy_limited where applicable
oracle_for_analysis_only where applicable
diagnostic_only where applicable
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
stress_conditioned only where valid Phase 9 stress records exist
embodiment_proxy_only only where valid Phase 12/13 embodiment linkage exists
```

[EXEC: Phase 8 required limitation tags]

#### 12.4 Stronger-claim requirements

Any stronger claim than simulation-only sequential consequence analysis requires later validated evidence from the appropriate official phase: Phase 9 for stress robustness, Phase 10 for contextual-bandit evidence, Phase 11 for RL policy evidence, Phase 12/13 for embodiment demonstrations, Phase 14 for dashboard/export derivations, and Phase 15 for final thesis integration. Clinical, medical-device, real-patient, real-actuation, real-deployment, and real-assistive-control safety claims remain forbidden by the provided architecture. [ARCH: Layer 0]

### 13. Failure, missingness, and diagnostic-only handling

#### 13.1 Failure modes

| Failure mode | Phase 8 consequence | Required record / flag |
|---|---|---|
| Missing upstream source records | Affected session/policy cannot be replayed thesis-ready. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`. |
| Split mismatch or leakage | Policy/simulation comparison invalid. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, Layer 0 claim block. |
| Hidden future/oracle fields in state | Policy evidence invalid. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, diagnostic-only. |
| Invalid action token or alias | Transition invalid or mapped only with explicit diagnostic mapping. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`; possibly `SafetyEventRecord` if blocked. |
| Missing legality mask | Policy action cannot be validated. | Diagnostic-only or blocked. |
| Impossible transition | Transition and rollout invalid. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`. |
| Missing reward trace | Reward/rollout comparison invalid. | Diagnostic-only. |
| Reward component sum failure | Reward metrics invalid. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, `NegativeResultNote` if material. |
| Unversioned reward config | Reward comparison invalid. | Diagnostic-only. |
| Missing session/episode definition | Session summary invalid. | Diagnostic-only. |
| Missing held-out simulated sessions | Frozen-policy evaluation not thesis-ready. | Diagnostic-only. |
| Safety event claimed but not logged | Safety-event summary invalid. | Diagnostic-only and Layer 0 warning. |
| Policy mutation during frozen replay | Frozen evaluation invalid. | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, `PolicyUpdateTrace` check, diagnostic-only. |
| Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` where mutation occurs | Update-enabled claim blocked. | Diagnostic-only. |
| Mixed update-enabled and frozen curves | Policy comparison invalid. | Diagnostic-only and dashboard warning. |
| Unmatched sessions/configs/seeds | Comparative claim invalid. | `MatchedComparisonReport` marked diagnostic-only. |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Metric cannot support thesis-ready claim. | Diagnostic-only. |
| Dashboard recomputation or hidden filter | Export invalid. | Layer 10 warning and blocked export. |
| Clinical/deployment wording attempted | Claim invalid. | Layer 0 invalid-claim flag / diagnostic-only. |

#### 13.2 Missingness categories

Missing records are not repaired silently. Phase 8 must classify missingness as:

- blocking missingness: prevents valid simulation record creation;
- policy-family missingness: removes a policy family from comparison with a baseline-sufficiency note;
- metric missingness: makes a metric diagnostic-only;
- dashboard/export missingness: blocks thesis-ready card/export but preserves source records;
- downstream optional missingness: marks stress, embodiment, bandit, or RL branches as not yet supported. [EXEC: Phase 8 missingness handling]

#### 13.3 Diagnostic-only preservation

Diagnostic-only records remain saved and visible. They may support debugging, threats-to-validity analysis, future repair, and negative-result discussion, but not confirmatory thesis claims. Layer 10 must not hide diagnostic-only outputs, and Layer 0 must ensure diagnostic-only labels survive into final claim-evidence artifacts. [EVAL: diagnostic-only downgrade discipline]

### 14. Repository, storage, and reproducibility expectations

Phase 8 storage must follow Phase 0 repository and manifest conventions and the registry. Exact local paths, class names, commands, and tests remain deferred to the future Implementation Build Book unless already canonical. [FRAME: implementation boundary]

Required storage principles:

- all records are run-scoped and schema-versioned;
- every output has `run_id`, `config_hash`, `seed`, and source-record lineage;
- environment/reward/action/session/policy comparison configs are versioned;
- record paths are registered in the artifact manifest;
- safety-event CSV/log aliases map to canonical `SafetyEventRecord` where used;
- diagnostic-only and negative-result files are stored, not discarded;
- dashboard/card/export source bundles are separated from Layer 10 generated outputs;
- optional policy-update traces are separated from frozen replay outputs;
- update-enabled training/adaptation outputs are separated from held-out frozen evaluation outputs. [EXEC: Phase 8 storage principles]

| Storage family | Contents | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 8 / Layer 7 configs | Environment configs, reward configs, cost configs, action-space maps, legality masks, session/episode definitions, replay configs, policy comparison configs, frozen/update configs. | Manifest-mapped; exact paths deferred where unresolved. |
| Phase 8 records | `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, `SafetyEventRecord` where materialized. | Required for Phase 8 exit. |
| Policy-update governance | Disabled-update audit entries and optional `PolicyUpdateTrace` files where declared. | Conditional but claim-blocking if update hooks exist. |
| Evaluation artifacts | Phase 8 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry` links, baseline-sufficiency table, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags. | Required for thesis-facing interpretation. |
| Dashboard/card source bundles | Closed-loop environment card source bundle, policy rollout card source bundle, trajectory/reward/action source data. | Layer 10 input only. |
| Manifests | Phase 8 handoff manifest, artifact manifest entries, reproducibility manifest inputs, figure/table manifest inputs. | Required for downstream handoff. |
| Validation logs | Schema, lineage, action legality, reward, no-mutation, trace completeness, matched-comparison validation. | Required for auditability. |

Phase 10 must produce contextual-bandit-specific update/action/reward evidence and separate training/adaptation from held-out frozen evaluation. [EXEC: Phase 8 to Phase 10]

#### 15A.3 Handoff to Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy

Phase 8 hands Phase 11 stable delayed-consequence transitions, episode/done definitions, reward decomposition and sensitivity status, policy rollout and episode summaries for baseline policies, update/frozen separation rules, trace-governance requirements, invalid-action handling, and safety-event handling. Phase 11 must not claim RL evidence unless Phase 8 environment records validate and Phase 11 maintains update trace completeness and held-out evaluation separation. [EXEC: Phase 8 to Phase 11]

#### 15A.4 Handoff to Phase 12/13, Phase 14, and Phase 15

Phase 8 hands Phase 12/13 transition/action/reward/safety lineage and optional embodiment placeholders without claiming embodiment execution. It hands Phase 14 dashboard-readable records, warnings, metrics, matched reports, card source bundles, and export/reproducibility manifest inputs. It hands Phase 15 simulation-only evidence summaries, diagnostic-only and negative-result notes, baseline-sufficiency results, claim-evidence pointers, and limitations. [EXEC: Phase 8 downstream handoff]

| Exact repository homes for records/cards/logs | `deferred_to_build_book` / `requires_registry_confirmation` | Use conceptual storage families and artifact manifests; do not invent final paths. |
| Final statistical run matrix, tests, figure/table numbering | `deferred_to_final_experiment_protocol` / `deferred_to_paper_evidence_map` | Keep Phase 8 outputs metric-ready and lineage-ready; do not define final thesis placement. |
| Internal transition/reward/action algorithms | `deferred_to_nuts_and_bolts` | Declare procedural obligations only; do not canonize algorithm internals. |
| Stress and embodiment fields in transition/session records | `downstream_preparation_only` | Leave null/not applicable unless valid Phase 9/12/13 records exist; no early stress/embodiment claims. |

### 16A. Back-Propagation Correction Request handling

No new Back-Propagation Correction Request is required for Phase 8 generation. The accepted Phase 0–7 content provides the needed handoff boundaries, and unresolved issues can be handled forward through diagnostic-only rules, manifest mapping, versioned overlays, or requires-confirmation items.

If actual Phase 8 execution reveals a grounded upstream defect, the following template must be used rather than editing accepted prior phases:

```yaml
back_propagation_request:
  request_id: BPCR-P8-<sequence>
  discovered_in_phase: Phase 8
  affected_prior_phase: <Phase 0-7 identifier>
  affected_artifact_or_record: <canonical record/artifact/interface name>
  issue_type: <schema_gap|lineage_gap|alias_conflict|metric_gap|claim_safety_gap|handoff_inconsistency|other>
  severity: <blocking|major|minor>
  source_conflict: <compact source anchors>
  downstream_risk: <risk to Phase 8-15 evidence>
  required_action: <non-destructive repair, versioned overlay, diagnostic-only use, or registry/execution confirmation>
  whether_current_phase_can_continue: <yes|yes_diagnostic_only|no>
  diagnostic_only_effect: <affected rows/metrics/claims>
  claim_safety_effect: <Layer 0 impact>
```

Current Phase 8 BPCR status: `none_opened`. [FRAME: BPCR template] [PRIOR: no grounded mutation requirement]

### 17. Definition of done

#### 17.1 Required completion criteria

Phase 8 playbook section is complete when it defines:

- official Phase 8 identity and non-scope;
- source extraction digest with architecture, registry, execution-plan, evaluation-protocol, and previous-phase anchors;
- active layers and modules;
- entry conditions and input contract;
- operational execution procedure;
- output contract and artifact lifecycle/versioning rules;
- validation gates and exit criteria;
- matched-comparison preservation requirements;
- A0–A13 evaluation obligations;
- Layer 10 dashboard/reproducibility/export handoff;
- Layer 0 claim-safety handoff;
- failure, missingness, diagnostic-only rules, and negative-result handling;
- BPCR handling;
- downstream handoff package;
- machine-readable handoff block;
- source-grounding ledger, domain non-interference notes, and final self-audit. [FRAME: required structure]

#### 17.2 Actual phase execution definition of done

Actual Phase 8 execution is done only when:

1. Phase 0 foundations validate all Phase 8 schemas/configs/validators/manifests or diagnostic-only status is explicit;
2. selected Phase 1–7 inputs validate and are immutable;
3. environment/reward/action/session/replay/frozen-update configs are versioned and hashed;
4. `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, and `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` exist for selected policy families;
5. `SafetyEventRecord` exists wherever safety events are materialized or claimed;
6. frozen no-mutation checks pass, and update hooks are disabled or traced;
7. held-out simulated sessions are declared;
8. matched comparison reports and metric dictionary references exist for thesis-facing summaries;
9. negative results and diagnostic-only flags are saved and visible;
10. Layer 10 source bundles and Layer 0 claim tags are complete;
11. downstream handoff to Phase 9–15 is discoverable through manifests. [EXEC: Phase 8 definition of done]

### 1A. Phase purpose and thesis role

Phase 9 turns validated clean upstream evidence into declared, reproducible stress-test evidence. Its thesis role is to show how the already-built BenchGuard/IHARQ stack behaves when exposed to predeclared synthetic perturbations such as delay, dropout, noisy intent, weakness proxy, drift, fatigue-like degradation, and curated combined stress. [ARCH: Layer 8 purpose] [EVAL: A12 scientific question]

Phase 9 is not a proof of real clinical robustness. It supports stress-conditioned, simulation/proxy-bounded evidence only. Any robustness, safety, fatigue, electrode, device, rehabilitation, or deployment wording must remain inside Layer 0 claim boundaries. [ARCH: Layer 8 claim boundary] [EVAL: A12 limitations]

The phase also creates the downstream stress-conditioned substrate for later phases. Phase 10 and later policy/adaptation phases may consume stress-conditioned records only if Phase 9 gates pass and the required stress lineage/matched keys are preserved. [EXEC: Phase 9 handoff] [EVAL: A12 relationship to downstream phases]

---

### 1B. Capability-tier relevance

| Capability tier | Phase 9 relevance | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|
| C0 / public-data baseline tier | Stress can be applied only to records that preserve public-data provenance, split roles, preprocessing lineage, and clean-source IDs. | Public-data/proxy-only stress behavior; no subject-general clinical robustness claim. |
| C1 / calibrated decoder and threshold tier | Stress-conditioned changes in calibrated/thresholded outputs may be compared if calibration and threshold registry IDs are preserved. | Controlled degradation/sensitivity only; no claim that calibration handles real-world physiological change. |
| C2 / IHARQ and evidence-quality tier | IHARQ, evidence-quality, RegimeRisk, and deferral behavior can be stress-conditioned where upstream records exist. | Diagnostic or bounded evidence only unless complete clean/stressed lineage and metric dictionaries exist. |
| C3 / simulated closed-loop tier | Layer 7 session/rollout/transition/reward records can be replayed or viewed under stress if Phase 8 records are validated. | Simulated consequence behavior only; no real actuation or device-safety claim. |
| C4 / stretch embodiment or policy-adaptation tier | Stress artifacts may feed later contextual bandit/RL/embodiment demonstration phases if those phases are enabled. | Stretch/proxy demonstration only unless later evidence gates explicitly allow stronger wording. |

[DERIVED from ARCH: Layer 8 scope; EXEC: Phase 9 placement; EVAL: A12 relation to A0–A13; PRIOR: Phase 8 handoff.] This tier mapping is procedural and does not create a new canonical capability taxonomy.

### 3. Architecture-grounded phase objective

The operational objective of Phase 9 is to instantiate Layer 8 StressForge-Lite by:

- declaring stress profiles and schedules before stress-conditioned evaluation;
- applying seed-controlled, bounded perturbations through source-supported injection adapters;
- preserving immutable clean source records and generating derived stressed pointers/views;
- collecting stress-conditioned metrics and matched clean/stressed comparison reports;
- writing validation reports, StressCards, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and Layer 10 export metadata;
- handing Phase 10 a validated stress-conditioned evidence package when gates pass.

| Schedule engine | Produce reproducible `StressScheduleRecord` entries with seeds, schedule hashes, and clean-run pairing. |
| Injection adapter | Apply declared stress to supported target record families while preserving original clean records. |
| Consistency guard | Verify supported target families, valid intensities, immutable clean records, no split/label mutation, and no leakage. |
| Run orchestrator | Execute or coordinate stress-conditioned runs/views and maintain stress-run manifests. |
| Metric collector | Produce stress-conditioned metric outputs with metric dictionary linkage. |
| `StressProfileRecord` writer | Materialize profile records with required registry fields. |
| Layer 8 evaluation-outcome writer | Emit stress-specific `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` entries and diagnostic status. |
| Stress-card generation | Produce StressCards/source bundles for dashboard/reporting, with limitations and negative results. |
| Dashboard exporters | Hand off dashboard-readable views without becoming primary evidence. |
| Failure-taxonomy writer | Record stress failure envelopes, unsupported targets, instability, null/worse results, and missingness. |
| Config hashing and matched-seed manifest generation | Preserve reproducibility, clean/stressed matching, and stress-run auditability. |
| Stress-run validation reports | Validate profile, schedule, injection, matching, metrics, and claim-safety status. |

### 4. Entry conditions

Actual Phase 9 execution may begin only when the following entry conditions are satisfied or explicitly downgraded:

| Entry condition | Required status | Failure effect |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 8 handoff package available | Required | Missing Phase 8 clean simulation lineage blocks claim-ready A12 and triggers diagnostic-only stress exploration. |
| Clean upstream records immutable and addressable | Required | Any overwrite or untraceable mutation invalidates clean/stressed comparison. |
| Matched clean-run references available | Required for A12 | Missing clean-run pairing downgrades stress results to diagnostic-only. |
| Upstream diagnostic flags and negative notes carried forward | Required | Hidden negative/missing upstream status blocks claim-ready evidence. |
| Supported stress family/intensity/target vocabulary selected | Required | Unsupported vocabulary/target triggers diagnostic-only or open issue. |
| Predeclared stress profile and schedule plan exists | Required before stress execution | Post-hoc stress tuning or schedule selection blocks claim-ready A12. |
| Metric dictionary scope prepared | Required before report generation | Missing metric definitions make metrics non-claim-ready. |
| Layer 0 limitation tags prepared | Required | Missing claim boundaries block dashboard/export and thesis-facing use. |
| Layer 10 export/readiness expectations prepared | Required | Missing dashboard/reproducibility/export handoff blocks phase completion. |

[EXEC: Phase 9 gates] [REG: Layer 8 records] [EVAL: A12 diagnostic-only triggers]

### 4B. Allowed Phase 9 execution modes and mode-specific boundaries

Every Phase 9 run must declare one of the source-supported execution modes below before stress artifacts are generated. This is a procedural execution-mode declaration, not an implementation command or simulator redesign. [ARCH: Layer 8 execution modes] [FRAME: domain non-interference]

| Execution mode | Source-supported meaning | Required additional inputs | Outputs that become required in this mode | Claim-safety boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Record-only mode | Produce stress profiles, schedules, stressed views/pointers, manifests, validation reports, and stress-readiness artifacts without executing a full closed-loop simulation. | Validated source/evidence records from upstream phases, stress registry/profile/schedule inputs, seeds, config hashes, clean-source IDs, matched-key plan. | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stressed pointer/view or manifest-mapped equivalent, stress-run manifest, stress validity report, metric plan, diagnostic flags where applicable. | Supports only stress-preparation, source-lineage, and diagnostic stress-readiness statements; no simulated consequence or policy-survival claim unless corresponding evaluation records exist. |
| Layer 7 simulation mode | Inject declared stress into repeated readiness sessions and evaluate stress-conditioned simulated transitions, rewards, actions, fallback/deferral behavior, and safety-event summaries where materialized. | Valid Phase 8 `TransitionRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, environment/reward/action/session hashes, clean-run pairing. | Layer 8 stress `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, stress-conditioned metrics, matched clean/stressed comparison, negative-result notes, stress failure taxonomy, Layer 10 stress source bundle. | Simulation-only and stress-conditioned; cannot be described as real-time deployment, real patient safety, or clinical assistive-control evidence. |
| Layer 9 embodiment-proxy mode | Inject embodiment-side delay/weakness or related declared stress into simulated action consequences while keeping EEG/evidence stress separate from musculoskeletal-response proxy stress. | Valid Layer 9 records only when later Phase 12/13 artifacts exist or are explicitly produced downstream: `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, demo manifest, command-mapping IDs, safety-event/log linkage where materialized. | A12.5 bridge lineage, stress-to-embodiment matched links, embodiment-proxy stress metrics, StressCard warnings, downstream handoff to Phase 12/13 if active. | Embodiment-proxy/stretch-only; no real physiology, real weakness, rehabilitation efficacy, stimulation-control, or device-safety claim. |

If a run mixes modes, each mode segment must preserve its own source IDs, mode label, profile/schedule IDs, clean/stressed pair, metric dictionary entries, diagnostic status, and Layer 0 limitation tags. Mixed-mode evidence cannot be aggregated into a stronger claim unless a later official protocol defines the aggregation and all component gates pass.
