## 1. R35 purpose and execution continuity

The governing order remains Architecture -> Canonical Registry -> Execution and Evidence Plan -> Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol -> Phase Execution Playbook -> accepted Method Selection -> Nuts-and-Bolts -> Implementation Build Book -> execution evidence. Detailed design may reveal representational or feasibility evidence, but it cannot silently override a superior authority. Conversely, once an authority successor is accepted, every dependent detailed-design reference, configuration, artifact, interface, test, manifest and consumer handoff must explicitly rebind or be invalidated.

R35 preserves R34 and exact Phase 5 ordering. It adds the complete operational mechanism needed to keep upstream authorities and Layer 5 R8 synchronized after any accepted correction.

## 2. Ten-stage bidirectional synchronization procedure

| Order | Action | Required record/evidence | Stop rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Detect and classify divergence | issue/evidence record with exact document/version and affected proposition | stop affected branch on critical causal/identity/ownership conflict |
| 2 | Freeze current compatibility set | predecessor hashes, manifests, run/config IDs and consumer list | no mutation of released members |
| 3 | Build impact graph | records/interfaces/steps/gates/ablations/modules/consumers and earliest root | no broad invalidation without dependency evidence |
| 4 | Route to authority owner | bidirectional synchronization packet | Layer 5 cannot self-approve superior-authority change |
| 5 | Decide accept/reject/defer | owner disposition and rationale | deferred/rejected branch remains blocked/downgraded/inapplicable/diagnostic |
| 6 | Create immutable successor | new document/profile/protocol/build version and predecessor pointer | no in-place rewrite |
| 7 | Migrate/rebind references | version/supersession ledger and compatibility manifest | historical anchors preserved; forward set unambiguous |
| 8 | Invalidate and regenerate | topological rebuild log and explicit absence/failure rows | no descendant reuse across changed root |
| 9 | Validate consumers and promotion | schema/interface/chronology/consumer acceptance checks | no promotion on failed required facet |
| 10 | Close or retain open facets | validation report, residual owner-gated ledger and manifest | no atomic green light across unrelated maturity facets |

## 3. Exact Phase 5 binding

The R34 step and gate tables remain controlling. R35 additionally requires each step to record its input authority versions, product dispositions, owner, gate contribution, consumer, invalidation root and regeneration status. Step 15 cannot close a compatibility set while required predecessors, schemas, Protocol slots, Build adapters, consumer acknowledgements or empirical evidence are absent.

## 4. Promotion and release hygiene

Release validation is read-only by default and writes dynamic results outside the manifest-covered package. Only final intended deliverables are released; LaTeX auxiliary files are not package members. Promotion requires exact manifest/hash verification, ZIP integrity, consumer-compatible interfaces and explicit maturity qualification.

## 5. Re-entry and rollback

A bidirectional synchronization packet contains at minimum: packet ID and version; initiating document/version; affected proposition or decision IDs; exact evidence and source hashes; direction (`authority_to_realization` or `realization_to_authority`); impacted record/artifact/interface/step/gate/ablation/module/consumer sets; earliest invalidation root; compatibility and migration effects; owner and decision state; required regeneration order; closure tests; predecessor/successor pointers; and residual owner-gated matters. A packet cannot mark a facet complete unless the responsible owner and required evidence exist.

The reverse-impact matrix in the package is normative for this compatibility set. Re-entry begins at the earliest changed dependency, not automatically at Step 1 and not merely at the observed failure surface.

## 6. R35 completion statement

`PROCEDURE, STOP, ROLLBACK, RE-ENTRY, REBINDING AND PROMOTION CONTRACT CLOSED; EXECUTION EVIDENCE PENDING`.

The assertion identifiers and normalized values above are normative for this compatibility set. Historical wording remains provenance; current interpretation must not contradict these values.

## R36 operational change-packet state machine

| Order | State | Entry | Required action | Exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | DRAFT | finding or accepted authority change identified | identify proposition and evidence | packet complete enough for submission |
| 2 | SUBMITTED | packet has required fields | route to authorized owner | owner acknowledges receipt |
| 3 | OWNER_REVIEW | owner accepts review duty | assess authority, evidence, compatibility, impact | ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or HELD |
| 4A | ACCEPTED | owner approves proposition change/clarification | issue immutable successor and migration/invalidation decision | SUCCESSOR_ISSUED |
| 4B | REJECTED | owner rejects change | preserve authority; block/downgrade/diagnostic affected branch | CLOSED with rejection rationale |
| 4C | HELD | evidence or authority incomplete | preserve current authority and explicit pending state | OWNER_REVIEW when evidence arrives |
| 5 | SUCCESSOR_ISSUED | accepted successor exists | bind compatibility set and predecessor/successor links | INVALIDATION_APPLIED |
| 6 | INVALIDATION_APPLIED | earliest root identified | mark affected descendants stale/blocked/superseded | REGENERATION_REQUIRED or VERIFIED if no descendants |
| 7 | REGENERATION_REQUIRED | dependent artifacts require rebuild | regenerate in topological order without overwriting history | VERIFIED |
| 8 | VERIFIED | closure tests pass | record consumer acknowledgments and residual gates | CLOSED |
| 9 | CLOSED | decision, successor/invalidation, tests, and residual facets recorded | retain immutable packet and lineage | new packet only if new evidence appears |

## Stop, rollback, regeneration, and closure procedure

1. Stop the affected branch at the narrowest valid boundary; do not mutate accepted predecessors.
2. Create and submit the packet to the authorized domain owner.
3. Until acceptance, preserve the current authority and mark the affected branch blocked, downgraded, inapplicable, or diagnostic-only.
4. On acceptance, issue an immutable authority successor and a new compatibility set.
5. Apply transitive invalidation from the earliest root and regenerate dependents in topological order.
6. Re-run schema/profile, identity, causality, interface, step/gate, evaluation, package, and consumer tests.
7. Close only after successor binding, regenerated evidence, consumer acknowledgment, and residual owner-gated facets are recorded.

Repository promotion remains fail-closed: a failed candidate stays visible as a run-specific unpromoted artifact; it is never silently repaired in canonical storage.

## Acceptance, compatibility and rollback

The owner must accept, reject or revise each clause individually or as an explicitly enumerated package. Partial acceptance activates only the named clauses. Every acceptance record must identify the effective version, scope, compatibility set, migration, rollback, dependent Layer 10 sections and consumer acknowledgments. Rejection leaves the controlling predecessor in force and the affected Layer 10 product blocked or downgraded.
